var pack = manifest.GetSingleSettingsPack(); var warning = pack.GetSingleWarning(manifest.Id); var panel = manifest.GetRequiredPanel(); services.AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition<FoundationTagsSettings, SettingsPackContext>( new SettingsPackRegistration<FoundationTagsSettings, SettingsPackContext> { SettingsSection = settingsSection, PackKey = pack.Key, PackTitle = pack.Title, RibbonPanel = panel, ApplyBehavior = SettingsPackApplyBehavior.NextToolRun, ContextFactory = (sp, input) => new SettingsPackContext( sp.GetRequiredService<ISettingsWarningService>(), input.RequireWarningId(), input.HostContext, sp.GetRequiredService<IErrorNotifier>(), sp.GetRequiredService<ILogger<SettingsPackContext>>()), ViewFactory = context => new FoundationTagsSettingsPackView { DataContext = context }, Warning = new SettingsPackWarningRegistration<SettingsPackContext> { Id = warning.Id, Title = warning.Title, Message = warning.Message, ToolInternalNamesToDisable = warning.DisableTools, FlagGetter = context => context.HasWarning, FlagSetter = (context, active) => { context.HasWarning = active; if (active) context.AutoUpdateEnabled = false; } } }); } Every mandatory registration value and delegate is a C# required member. The pack definition captures the typed section, so its load and staged-write operations cannot silently choose different names. Warning id/title/message and flag delegates are likewise required whenever a warning is configured. AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition also performs runtime non-empty/null validation at the DI boundary; compile-time requiredness does not replace that admission check. Source: src/DBTools.Core/Settings/Composition/SettingsPackServiceCollectionExtensions.cs Tool-Owned Contexts at Runtime Every production settings pack registers a tool-owned context type. Joist Girder Weight constructs JoistGirderWeightSettingsPackContext in its module's ContextFactory; Elevation Tags builds ElevationTagsSettingsPackContext through ElevationTagsSettingsPackContextFactory. When a settings context needs Revit host state, Core passes SettingsPackHostContext to ISettingsPackDefinition.CreateRuntime(...); packs without host needs receive SettingsPackHostContext.Empty. The host value can be created only through Empty or FromApplication(...), and contexts extract a typed host through TryGetApplication<TApplication>(). The definition immediately binds the resulting typed context, view factory, typed persistence section, and warning operations into one ISettingsPackRuntime; callers never pass an erased context back to a definition or warning. Elevation Tags reads the host only to populate preview type snapshots and still uses an empty list when no active document exists. Foundation Tags reads the same value for prerequisite actions and reports the action-unavailable status when no active Revit document exists. Contexts that carry the standard auto-update toggle derive from the Core production base SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<TOptions> (see Production Base below). The Core AutoUpdateViewModel<TSettings> under Settings/DesignTime is an internal design-time sample for the settings window designer composition, not production infrastructure. Settings Pack Context The context is the ViewModel for your settings UI. It must implement ISettingsPackContext<T>. Required Interface Methods public interface ISettingsPackContext<TOptions> : ISettingsPackContext { void Load(TOptions options); // Load settings into bindable properties TOptions BuildOptionsSnapshot(); // Create settings object from current state } public interface ISettingsPackContext { Task<SettingsValidationResult> ValidateAsync(CancellationToken ct = default); } Optional Context Interfaces Interface Purpose ISettingsStateContext Fire StateChanged event when properties change IPendingChangesContext Track HasPendingChanges for save button state IOwnerAwareContext Receive parent window for file dialogs ISettingsPackSaveState<TOptions> Establish the persisted baseline with MarkSaved(committedOptions) without overwriting newer edits ISettingsWarningContext Trigger warning evaluation via WarningId ISettingsPackSaveValidation Block settings save when ValidateAsync returns invalid Use ISettingsPackSaveValidation for settings where invalid values should never be persisted (for example, invalid regex patterns that would be ignored at runtime). After the file commit, the runtime passes each pack its exact committed options snapshot. The context updates its baseline before post-commit warning validation or ribbon application. Those later failures must not make persisted values appear unsaved. Edits made while the commit was pending remain dirty against the committed snapshot. If applying committed flags or warning state fails, the workflow reports the committed operation and phase while keeping the persisted values as the saved state; the settings window remains open. Production Base: SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext Auto-update settings pack contexts derive from the Core production base, which owns the shared mechanics: header text (Title, Description, ToggleToolTip), the AutoUpdateEnabled/HasWarning toggle state with ToggleEnabled, ClearWarningCommand, WarningId (validate-aware), BlockSaveOnInvalid (always true), pending-change tracking against a saved baseline (HasPendingChanges), StateChanged notification, and the validation envelope. public abstract partial class SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<TOptions> : ObservableObject, ISettingsPackContext<TOptions>, ISettingsStateContext, IPendingChangesContext, ISettingsWarningContext, ISettingsPackSaveState<TOptions>, ISettingsPackSaveValidation where TOptions : class, IAutoUpdateSettings, new() { protected SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext(string warningId, string title, string description, string toggleToolTip); // Derived contexts own everything shaped by their settings type: protected abstract void LoadCore(TOptions options); // bindable state + SetBaseline(...) protected abstract void CollectValidationErrors(List<string> errors); protected abstract bool SettingsEqual(TOptions left, TOptions right); public abstract TOptions BuildOptionsSnapshot(); } Load applies the auto-update toggle, clears the warning flag, delegates to LoadCore, and raises the final state change. MarkSaved resets the baseline from the current snapshot only after a successful settings commit. ValidateAsync collects errors from CollectValidationErrors and converts them into a SettingsValidationResult. Current consumers: ElevationTagsSettingsPackContext and JoistGirderWeightSettingsPackContext. FoundationTagsSettingsPackContext intentionally implements the context interfaces directly — it owns prerequisite runtime state, warning-fix provider behavior, and shared-parameter refresh/install/repair actions that do not fit the base's shape. Regex Pattern Lists Settings packs that expose editable regex rows use the Core shell RegexPatternListContext. It owns the bindable RegexPatternEntry collection, add/remove commands, maximum-row guard, default seeding when a loaded list is empty, blank-value omission from snapshots, and StateChanged notifications. Tool contexts keep their own binding-facing property names so XAML remains tool-specific while the repeated list mechanics stay in Core. Current consumers are ElevationTagsPatternContext and the Foundation Tags settings-pack pattern partial. Foundation Tags still owns prerequisite runtime state, warning-fix behavior, and shared-parameter refresh/install/repair actions; only the regex-list mechanics moved to the shared context. Custom Context Example For tools requiring additional UI beyond the toggle, create a custom context: public sealed partial class FoundationTagsSettingsPackContext : ObservableObject, ISettingsPackContext<FoundationTagsSettings>, ISettingsStateContext, IPendingChangesContext { private const int MaxPatterns = 3; private FoundationTagsSettings _baseline = new(); private readonly RegexPatternListContext _tagFamilyPatterns = new(MaxPatterns, FoundationTagsSettings.DefaultTagFamilyPatterns[0]); [ObservableProperty] [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(ToggleEnabled))] private bool _autoUpdateEnabled = true; [ObservableProperty] [NotifyPropertyChangedFor(nameof(ToggleEnabled))] private bool _hasWarning; public FoundationTagsSettingsPackContext() { _tagFamilyPatterns.StateChanged += OnTagFamilyPatternsStateChanged; RequiredParametersStatusMessage = "Click Refresh to check required shared parameters for the active Revit document."; } public ObservableCollection<RegexPatternEntry> TagFamilyPatterns => _tagFamilyPatterns.Patterns; public IRelayCommand AddTagPatternCommand => _tagFamilyPatterns.AddPatternCommand; public IRelayCommand<RegexPatternEntry?> RemoveTagPatternCommand => _tagFamilyPatterns.RemovePatternCommand; public void Load(FoundationTagsSettings options) { AutoUpdateEnabled = options.AutoUpdateEnabled; _tagFamilyPatterns.Load(options.TagFamilyPatterns); // ... load other collections _baseline = CloneOptions(options); NotifyStateChanged(); } public FoundationTagsSettings BuildOptionsSnapshot() { return new FoundationTagsSettings { AutoUpdateEnabled = AutoUpdateEnabled, TagFamilyPatterns = _tagFamilyPatterns.BuildSnapshot(), // ... etc }; } public Task<SettingsValidationResult> ValidateAsync(CancellationToken ct = default) { var errors = new List<string>(); ValidatePatternGroup(errors, TagFamilyPatterns, "tag family"); // ... validate other groups return errors.Count == 0 ? Task.FromResult(SettingsValidationResult.Success) : Task.FromResult(SettingsValidationResult.FromErrors(errors.ToArray())); } [RelayCommand] private void ClearWarning() { HasWarning = false; RefreshRequiredParameters(); NotifyStateChanged(); } } Custom context constructors should stay passive. Foundation Tags initializes bindable collections and the status prompt in its constructor; active Revit prerequisite reads happen only through explicit Refresh/Clear Warning/Install-Repair actions. Accessing Settings at Runtime In Commands (One-time Read) Inject the typed section with ISettingsProvider for a snapshot of current settings: public sealed class MyWorkflow { private readonly ISettingsProvider _settings; private readonly SettingsSection<MyToolSettings> _section; public MyWorkflow( ISettingsProvider settings, SettingsSection<MyToolSettings> section) => (_settings, _section) = (settings, section); public void Execute() { var settings = _settings.Get(_section); if (!settings.SomeFeatureEnabled) { return; } // Use settings.SomeValue, settings.SomeList, etc. } } In Services (Current Read) Inject ISettingsProvider for a current settings snapshot: public class MyService { private readonly ISettingsProvider _settings; private readonly SettingsSection<MyToolSettings> _section; public MyService( ISettingsProvider settings, SettingsSection<MyToolSettings> section) { _settings = settings; _section = section; } public void DoWork() { var current = _settings.Get(_section); if (current.AutoUpdateEnabled && !current.HasWarning) { // Perform auto-update logic } } } In ViewActivatedTask (Auto-update Pattern) The ViewActivatedTask<T> abstracts settings access for view-activated tools: public sealed class AutoUpdateTask : ViewActivatedTask<FoundationTagsSettings> { public AutoUpdateTask( ISettingsProvider settingsProvider, SettingsSection<FoundationTagsSettings> settingsSection, ISettingsWarningService warnings, IErrorNotifier notifier, ILogger<AutoUpdateTask> logger, string[] warningIds) : base( settingsProvider, settingsSection, warnings, notifier, logger, "structural.foundation_tags.updater", "Combined Foundation Tags", warningIds) { } protected override void ExecuteTask(Document document, View view) { // Called only when AutoUpdateEnabled && !HasWarning } } Persisting Settings Automatic Save (Settings Window) When the user clicks Save in the Settings window, SettingsWindowViewModel delegates persistence to SettingsPersistenceWorkflow under Settings/Persistence: var flags = BuildFlagsSnapshot(); await _persistence.SaveAndValidateAsync(flags, _packs.Rows); Note: The PublishPackChanged / PackChanged / SettingsPackChangedEventArgs event surface was deleted during the Core Full-Tree Cleanup. Consumers read current values through ISettingsProvider when they need them. The settings window groups visible packs into SettingsPanelBlock instances under Settings/ViewModels. SettingsPackCollection carries the explicit SettingsPackHostContext from the window factory and asks each definition for one runtime. SettingsPackViewModel owns that runtime: lazy view creation, pending-change and reset-target projection, owner-window propagation, state-change subscription, bound warning projection/application, and runtime disposal. The window view model builds rows and panel groups, but it cannot separately pair definitions, contexts, or warning delegates. Manual Save (Programmatic) Save settings directly using ISettingsProvider: var section = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<SettingsSection<MyToolSettings>>(); var settingsProvider = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<ISettingsProvider>(); var settings = settingsProvider.Get(section); settings.SomeValue = newValue; await settingsProvider.CommitAsync(new[] { section.CreateWrite(settings) }); SettingsSectionWriter (Low-level) For direct section writes, the settings provider delegates to SettingsSectionWriter: public sealed class SettingsSectionWriter : IDisposable { public SettingsSectionWriter(string settingsPath); public Task CommitAsync( IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default); } App composition supplies the base directory and the absolute AppPaths.SettingsFile to SettingsSectionReader, and supplies that absolute settings file path to this writer. When a reader receives a relative user-file name, it resolves that name relative to the base directory. Each settings DTO has a source-generated JsonSerializerContext beside it. Supply its JsonTypeInfo<T> when constructing the section; SettingsSection<T>.CreateWrite(value) carries that metadata into the heterogeneous batch. The reader loads both layers fresh for each Get; the writer validates duplicate names before I/O, reads the existing document once, updates every supplied section while retaining unrelated sections, and performs one file swap. A validation or writer failure occurs before the swap and leaves baselines and the settings file unchanged. A baseline/default-application or warning-validation failure after the swap is reported as SettingsPostCommitException, whose operation and phase make the already-committed state explicit. Only an absent settings file starts a new document. An existing empty or whitespace-only file is corrupt and remains unchanged when a commit fails. Reset All applies the committed flag snapshot and attempts every committed pack default before warning validation. This keeps the editable settings state aligned with the durable batch even when later post-commit validation fails, and aggregates any default-application failures after all packs have been attempted. The Settings window asks for confirmation before Reset All or a pack Reset. Cancel leaves the current settings and feedback unchanged. Confirm runs the same persistence and warning-validation workflow and then shows the reset success banner. When settings cannot load, choosing Reset Settings in the load-problem alert already confirms the operation, so that path resets directly without a second prompt. The SettingsSectionWriter implementation ensures atomic, cross-process-safe writes: Hold an exclusive lock on the sibling file settings.{YEAR}.json.lock from the re-read of the settings document through its swap. A commit waits while another process holds the lock, and fails with an IOException if the lock stays held for more than 10 seconds. Cancellation while waiting leaves the settings file unchanged. The OS releases the lock when its holder closes the handle or exits, so a crashed process never leaves a stale lock. The lock file itself persists; it carries no content. Under the lock, re-read the current document and replace only the committed sections Write to a per-commit staged file .{guid}.tmp in the settings directory Publish with an atomic File.Move(source, destination, overwrite: true); no backup artifact is retained Serialize in-process publications. Retry sharing, lock, and publication access-denied failures at most six times; reject known read-only destinations immediately. Surface publication access denial as IOException with its original cause. Attempt to remove the staged file after publication or failure, including cancellation. Cleanup must preserve the original failure. Same-year Revit processes share one settings file. Because every commit merges into the document that the previous lock holder published, concurrent commits from separate processes preserve each other's sections: a commit replaces only the sections in its own batch. Within one process, the writer instance also serializes its own commits. Settings UI Integration View Location Settings pack views are rendered in the Settings window under their assigned panel. The panel is determined by the manifest's required panel field through ToolManifestExtensions.GetRequiredPanel(): Manifest panel value Panel Settings DB Tools Settings Common DB Tools Common Structural DB Tools Structural Testing DB Tools Testing Services DB Tools Services Design-Time AutoUpdateView Core keeps a simple toggle + description view for the settings-window designer sample. Production settings packs should define their own tool-owned settings view: <UserControl x:Class="DBTools.Presentation.Settings.DesignTime.AutoUpdate.Views.AutoUpdateView"> <Border Style="{DynamicResource FeatureCard}"> <Grid> <ToggleButton IsChecked="{Binding AutoUpdateEnabled, Mode=TwoWay}" IsEnabled="{Binding ToggleEnabled}" Style="{DynamicResource SwitchToggleButton}" ToolTip="{Binding ToggleToolTip}" /> <TextBlock Text="{Binding Title}" /> <TextBlock Text="{Binding Description}" TextWrapping="Wrap" /> </Grid> </Border> </UserControl> Custom Views For complex settings, create a custom view in your tool's Settings/ folder: <UserControl x:Class="DBTools.Structural.FoundationTags.Settings.FoundationTagsSettingsPackView"> <StackPanel> <!-- Auto-update toggle --> <CheckBox IsChecked="{Binding AutoUpdateEnabled}" IsEnabled="{Binding ToggleEnabled}" /> <!-- Tag pattern list --> <ItemsControl ItemsSource="{Binding TagFamilyPatterns}"> <ItemsControl.ItemTemplate> <DataTemplate> <TextBox Text="{Binding Pattern, UpdateSourceTrigger=PropertyChanged}" /> </DataTemplate> </ItemsControl.ItemTemplate> </ItemsControl> <!-- Add/Remove buttons --> <Button Command="{Binding AddTagPatternCommand}" IsEnabled="{Binding CanAddTagPattern}" /> </StackPanel> </UserControl> Warning Integration How Warnings Work Warnings are conditions that disable tool functionality: Warning activates: Validation fails (e.g., invalid path) Tools disabled: Ribbon buttons grayed out, commands rejected User notified: Warning card appears in Settings window User fixes: Corrects settings, clicks "Clear Warning" Tools re-enabled: Ribbon buttons active again Warning Registration In RegisterSettingsPacks(), set the public registration's Warning property: new SettingsPackRegistration<TSettings, TContext> { // Required pack registration members omitted for brevity. Warning = new SettingsPackWarningRegistration<TContext> { Id = "core.structural.combined_tags", Title = "Combined Foundation Tags Disabled", Message = "Combined foundation tag updates are disabled due to a warning...", ToolInternalNamesToDisable = new[] { "DBTools.MyCommand" }, FlagGetter = context => context.HasWarning, FlagSetter = (context, active) => { context.HasWarning = active; if (active) context.AutoUpdateEnabled = false; } } } AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition(...) creates the internal warning definition from this registration. Use the complete registration pattern above when declaring the pack. Source: src/DBTools.Core/Settings/Composition/SettingsPackServiceCollectionExtensions.cs Warning Service ISettingsWarningService manages warning state across the application: public interface ISettingsWarningService { IReadOnlyCollection<ISettingsWarningDefinition> Definitions { get; } bool IsWarningActive(string warningId); SettingsWarningStateChange SetWarning(string warningId, bool active); } Full-state publication and active-id enumeration are internal responsibilities of the single concrete SettingsWarningService; tools receive only the narrowed interface above. Validation-Triggered Warnings Implement ISettingsWarningContext to automatically trigger warnings on validation: public sealed partial class TdvSettingsPackContext : ObservableObject, ISettingsPackContext<LibrarySettings>, ISettingsWarningContext // <-- Key interface { public string WarningId => _warningId; // From constructor public async Task<SettingsValidationResult> ValidateAsync(CancellationToken ct = default) { var options = BuildOptionsSnapshot(); var invalidEntries = options.Files.Where(f => !IsValid(f)).ToList(); HasWarnings = invalidEntries.Count > 0; if (HasWarnings) return new SettingsValidationResult(false, new[] { "Invalid library path" }); return SettingsValidationResult.Success; } } Startup Evaluation (Validate-Aware Packs) Validate-aware settings packs are evaluated during addin startup (after ribbon composition and before the initial warning publish) so ribbon tools are disabled immediately when underlying configuration is invalid, without requiring the user to open Settings. The startup evaluator: Receives the validated SettingsCatalog used by the settings shell and warning service Creates bound pack runtimes without constructing WPF views Loads options from ISettingsProvider Runs ValidateAsync only for runtime contexts implementing ISettingsWarningContext Activates warnings on invalid results Does not activate warnings on validation exceptions (exceptions are treated as runtime errors and should surface via normal error flows/logs) Does not proactively clear warnings on startup Disposes every created runtime, retries a failed cleanup once, records persistent cleanup failures with pack identity, and preserves cancellation even when cleanup also fails Real Examples Example 1: JoistGirderWeight (Auto-Update + Regex Matching) Use case: Toggle auto-calculation and configure regex matching for family/load resolution. Settings model: public sealed class JoistGirderWeightSettings : IAutoUpdateSettings { public bool AutoUpdateEnabled { get; set; } = true; public bool HasWarning { get; set; } public List<string> FamilyNamePatterns { get; set; } = new() { "^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$" }; public List<string> LoadParameterPatterns { get; set; } = new() { "^(?:Panel Point Load|Panel Load - User Defined|Panel Load|Point Load - User Defined|Point Load|Total Load - User Defined|Total Load|Joist Load|BG Joist Girder)$" }; } Registration: Uses custom JoistGirderWeightSettingsPackContext and JoistGirderWeightSettingsPackView with +/- regex row controls (max 3) and save-time validation. Manifest: settingsPacks: - key: structural.joist_girder_weight title: "Joist Girder Weights" warnings: - id: core.structural.joist_girder title: "Joist Girder Weights Disabled" disableTools: - DBTools.UpdateJoistGirderWeights Example 2: FoundationTags (Custom Patterns) Use case: Configure regex patterns for family matching. Settings model: Includes List<string> for patterns. Context: Custom FoundationTagsSettingsPackContext with pattern editing commands. View: Custom FoundationTagsSettingsPackView.xaml with pattern lists. Example 3: TDV Library (Complex Validation) Use case: Configure library file paths with validation warnings. Settings model: public sealed class LibrarySettings { public IList<LibraryFileEntry> Files { get; set; } = new List<LibraryFileEntry>(); } Context: TdvSettingsPackContext with file picker, tree view, and validation. Key features: IOwnerAwareContext for file dialogs ISettingsPackSaveState<LibraryOptions> for the committed baseline ISettingsWarningContext for automatic warning activation Best Practices Do Use IAutoUpdateSettings for tools with view-activated auto-update Clone settings in context to detect HasPendingChanges Fire StateChanged when any bindable property changes Implement validation that returns meaningful error messages Use existing patterns - check JoistGirderWeight for simple, FoundationTags for complex Don't Don't save directly from context - let SettingsWindowViewModel.Save() and SettingsPersistenceWorkflow.SaveAndValidateAsync() handle persistence Don't bypass warnings - respect HasWarning in command availability Don't block UI thread - use async for file I/O in validation Don't ignore CancellationToken - validation can be cancelled Testing Settings Build artifacts tests verify settings structure Integration tests can mock ISettingsProvider Manual testing in Revit validates UI binding Related Documentation Creating New Tools - Complete tool creation guide Feature Warnings - Deep dive on the warning system Core Infrastructure - DBTools.Core project reference Summary Settings Packs provide a unified way to expose tool configuration: Declare in manifest.yml with settingsPacks Model settings as a typed class (optionally implementing IAutoUpdateSettings) Register via RegisterSettings() and RegisterSettingsPacks() in your tool module Access through the registered SettingsSection<T> using ISettingsProvider.Get(section) Persist automatically through the Settings window or manually via one ISettingsProvider.CommitAsync(...) batch built with SettingsSection<T>.CreateWrite(...) Warn users when validation fails, disabling affected tools until resolved The system provides fresh layered reads, batch-atomic persistence, and consistent UX across all DBTools tools.

developer-guide/developing/test-refactor.title: Test Refactoring Strategy | DB Tools
developer-guide/developing/test-refactor.summary: Test Refactoring Strategy This page records the current test-refactoring direction for DBTools. The older GM/SGT Both / Local / DA-compatible strategy has been superseded by the current-dev Revit test taxonomy plan. Core Rule Tests must be labeled by the host they truly require: Marker Meaning plain [Test] Pure/off-Revit test [RevitLocal] Local Revit-hosted execution [RevitDA] True Autodesk APS Design Automation WorkItem execution The old Category("Both"), TestCategories.Both, Category("DA"), and TestCategories.DA markers have been removed. .DA.Tests project names are not routing truth and do not prove DA execution unless the selected tests submit and validate a real APS WorkItem. Refactoring Priorities Move pure logic to plain [Test] and remove Revit/WPF/add-in-host closure from those projects. Rewrite tests that use Revit API types only as convenient data carriers into native C# DTO/value/snapshot tests. Keep [RevitLocal] only for tests that genuinely require local Revit UI/session/add-in-host behavior. Use [RevitDA] only for tests that execute through APS Design Automation WorkItems and assert real outputs. Delete fake, mock-call-only, redundant, stale, or misleading tests instead of preserving old coverage names. Keep owner tests colocated under the owning Tests/ directory, but keep pure, local, and DA execution hosts separated by positive project membership until a single project can preserve those host contracts without dependency leakage. Split test directories before they exceed roughly 12 files, delete empty test directories, and avoid placeholder folders. Local Revit test projects must disable default compile items and explicitly include only the [RevitLocal] fixtures plus local-only support files they own. App and Core project-suite local projects follow the same rule as tool-owned local projects. They must not use broad default globs with large Compile Remove lists to subtract pure tests. If a local project needs a pure support helper, move the helper to a shared neutral location or duplicate no behavior; do not pull pure-only fixtures into the local assembly. GM Direction GM pure kernel, persistence, saved-mapping, similarity, usage-normalization, usage projection, usage-pane selection clearing, and planning tests should become plain [Test] after their Revit/WPF/App closure is removed. Nested family object-style/material projection is now covered through FamilyMappingOptionProjector without constructing the shell or usage pane view model, and usage-pane preview state flows through native values before WPF presentation is applied at the pane edge. Real document adapter, shared parameter, deep-scan, shell/window, owner wiring, and active view/document tests remain [RevitLocal] unless rewritten around native snapshots. DA coverage must wait for true WorkItem execution and must avoid WPF, UIApplication, UIDocument, selection, and interactive add-in-session assumptions. SGT Direction Most SGT package-mirrored unit tests are pure and should stay plain [Test]. The current pure set includes feature tests under Unit/Features/*, shared-domain tests under Unit/Shared/*, and undo/redo history plus file-backed UI-state persistence because those assert native service outcomes, not Revit host behavior. Tests that currently use Revit DB types for geometry or document state must be rewritten to native geometry/value snapshots where practical. UI smoke, parity harness, preview rendering, remaining shell command/view-model behavior, active-document, and selection behavior remains [RevitLocal] until each fixture proves it can be split. SGT DA coverage needs a product DA entry and a WorkItem test of its own, like the Sentinel's, and the test must obey DA host constraints. Validation Use canonical commands only: bash build.sh BuildAll dotnet test --list-tests # static discovery via the daemon adapter dotnet test --filter "TestCategory=GM" --list-tests dotnet test --filter "TestCategory=GM" dotnet test --filter "TestCategory=SGT" dotnet test discovers tests statically and dispatches [RevitLocal] work to the dbtools-daemon fleet; pure [Test] fixtures run in-process. APS WorkItem tests never go through the daemon. The one such test, the DA Sentinel, runs on the operator's host with the operator's APS credentials, and agents never run it; see APS Design Automation Sentinel.

developer-guide/developing/testing-tools.title: Testing Tools for DBTools Development | DB Tools
developer-guide/developing/testing-tools.summary: Testing Tools for DBTools Development This guide covers the complete testing infrastructure for DBTools, including test categories, running tests, writing effective tests, and using the TestSupport library. Overview: Testing Philosophy DBTools follows a production-first testing philosophy: Fix production code before changing tests - When a test fails, investigate production code first Assert outcomes, not interactions - Tests must verify real results, not just that mocks were called Stub only true externals - Mock the Revit API, filesystem, and network; never mock your own services No fake tests - If a test passes regardless of production correctness, delete it What Makes a Test Legitimate Legitimate (KEEP) Illegitimate (DELETE) Revit API stubs Your own service mocks File system stubs PlacementExecutionService/handler mocks Network stubs Test doubles with domain behavior Time/Random stubs for determinism "Mock was called" assertions only Test Categories DBTools has pure, local Revit, and a Revit 2026 Design Automation Sentinel lane. The Sentinel is an HTTP client of Autodesk's cloud. test.sh --scope da runs it on the invoking host with dotnet test, never through the daemon. See APS Design Automation Sentinel. 1. Non-Revit Project Tests Tests that run without Revit. Use plain dotnet test for daemon-backed Pure entries; test.sh remains the coordinator route and Linux-native BUILD/DIST route: Build Tests - Linux-native BUILD suites verify DBTools build output structure and metadata; run them on Linux, not the Windows broker App Tests - Verify DBTools.App host queue and resource-contract behavior without launching Revit; this lane still needs the Windows Desktop runtime because it references the WPF app assembly Core Tests - Verify DBTools.Core runtime behavior without launching Revit Owner Pure Tests - Tool-owned pure logic tests in .Pure.Tests projects DA Sentinel Tests - One real APS Design Automation WorkItem test that only the operator runs, plus network-free unit tests of its client # Run build validation tests ./test.sh test --tool BUILD # Run app host tests ./test.sh test --tool APP # Run core runtime tests ./test.sh test --tool CORE # Run the DA Sentinel's network-free tests; the WorkItem test itself is operator-only ./test.sh test --tool DA-SENTINEL --scope da -f 'TestCategory!=RevitDA' # Run GM pure owner tests without launching Revit ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure # Scope to one tool (pure runs in-process; Revit-hosted dispatches to the fleet) ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure GM pure tests are for production behavior that can run over native DTOs, filesystem/cache contracts, and explicit true-external stubs. StatePersistenceTests, UIStateCacheTests, and UIStateLifecycleTests are pure because they exercise UI-state and saved-mapping persistence directly; MappingIntentStoreTests, SharedParameterTreeProjectorTests, SavedMappingRestoreWorkflowTests, FamilyMappingSelectionNavigationWorkflowTests, OperationRowProjectorTests, SessionOperationGateTests, and ProjectStateStoreTests are pure because they exercise native services directly, including persisted mapping-intent restoration, shared-parameter tree projection, saved-mapping restore, family-details navigation, commit-review operation and error rows, the session operation gate and overlay lifecycle, and project-state replacement. StatePersistenceRegistrationTests remain [RevitLocal] because AddGm validates the production service graph. 2. Revit Integration Tests Tests that require a running Revit instance. Plain dotnet test on a daemon Hosted entry submits [RevitLocal] fixtures through the VSTest adapter. The coordinator continues to use test.sh, which submits through the daemon CLI. Both routes execute on the daemon fleet (the daemon boots Revit + NUnit + the add-in there): UI Tests - ViewModel integration tests Document Tests - Tests requiring Revit documents with elements Adapter Tests - Tests verifying Revit API interactions # Primary developer route: plain dotnet test, selecting the year through the # documented daemon environment override. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS=2026 dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/GM.Hosted.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FamilyDeepScanTests.GM_DeepScan_Smoke" # Coordinator route (the coordinator owns fleet admission). ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 # Run the App-owned local Revit-hosted suite ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 Test Host Markers Revit-hosted tests must never display a blocking modal. The daemon probes visible Revit-process windows every second and rejects the whole run for a #32770 dialog, a disabled window anywhere in the native owner chain, or a Revit Unhandled Exception window. A short-lived dialog is still a violation. Show real sessions modelessly with Show and use the shared bounded DispatcherDrain or DispatcherFaultScope pump. Keep Revit API, runtime ALC, theme, and real main-window owner identity checks hosted. Move ShowDialog results, modal-loop exit, native owner disable/restore, and modal-child refusal checks to Windows-VSTest Pure tests using real WPF windows and stand-in owners. Audit indirect calls, including owner-disabling presenters and alert/file-picker paths. ToolWindowDialog rejects the Revit process and Revit routing categories before it touches the session. Ad-hoc NUnit metadata cannot bypass the process check. Its watchdog remains available to Windows Pure tests, including a beforeShow callback for sessions deliberately closed before their modal loop. The shared hosted assembly setup installs the runtime modal tripwire on Revit's UI dispatcher. It records an entering WPF ShowDialog and posts a Send-priority close of that exact dialog. The assembly action fails the test even if the body later calls Pass, Ignore or Inconclusive. The tripwire does not permit a modal: the daemon can still detect it before the close executes. CommonDialog can raise the same event without a WPF Window; the tripwire records the violation and does not guess which unrelated window to close. Native message boxes, TaskDialog, disabled owners and tests with their own STA dispatcher remain outside that backstop. The daemon's visible-window probe is the final authority. The current implementation uses explicit attributes for execution routing: using DBTools.Tests.Shared; [TestFixture] [RevitLocal] public class MyLocalRevitTests { [Test] public void Test_LocalRevitBehavior() { // Runs in local Revit. } } plain [Test] for pure/off-Revit tests [RevitLocal] for local Revit-hosted tests [RevitDA] for true APS Design Automation WorkItem tests [RevitDA] marks a test that runs a real APS WorkItem. [RevitLocal] marks a test that runs in the Revit daemon; neither category implies support for the other host. Owner test projects stay under the owning tool's Tests/ directory. Pure and local execution are separated by project membership, but project compile items separate Pure and hosted source sets. A plain [Test] fixture belongs in the owner pure project. [RevitLocal] fixtures belong in the owner local project. [RevitDA] fixtures belong in a DA project with a real WorkItem execution route before they claim DA coverage. Host selection follows each test's own metadata rather than a flag: a plain [Test] runs in-process and a [RevitLocal] fixture runs Revit-hosted on the fleet. A [RevitDA] fixture is an APS WorkItem test. It runs on the invoking host as an HTTP client; the daemon never runs it. Revit-hosted tests classify every missing prerequisite before deciding whether a skip is honest: Repository-controlled inputs and expected production behavior are required. A missing staged model or asset, canonical element/view/style/material/link baseline, failed production outcome, or failed rollback/cleanup step must fail with the requested and observed state, resolved path, and running Revit year where relevant. A skip is valid only when the current supported Revit runtime actually lacks a required API capability. The test must probe the current API and report the exact missing member or capability plus the running year; an owner-declared year range is not evidence. Arbitrary exceptions remain failures. Tests must not catch and relabel them as inconclusive, search alternate models, repair fixture data dynamically, or swallow cleanup failures. When both test work and owned cleanup fail, preserve both exceptions. Teardown must attempt every owned document close, UIDocument disposal, logging shutdown, transaction-group finalization, and window/session disposal step before reporting the aggregate failure. For production window-composition smokes, calling Window.Close() is not closure proof. The test must use the same production session owner as the command and await its failure-bearing completion through actual Closed, command/view-model cleanup, and scope disposal before closing the host document. Every session must likewise await its exact startup task and its attempts to persist UI state, release preview/Helix/effects, finalize the transaction group, close the window, detach handlers, and dispose the view model before disposing the App run scope; actual Closed is asserted separately from the cleanup-attempt marker. Startup Failed, Cancelled, or absent outcomes always select rollback. Once startup succeeds, persistence or cosmetic cleanup failures do not change the requested model outcome; failed transaction-group health still selects rollback. Exceptional dispatcher closure must exercise the Core-owned per-window error boundary rather than attach a tool-specific dispatcher handler. Contracts must prove that a classified failure notifies only the exact attached window after Core presentation and is marked handled, while a foreign failure is neither notified nor handled. They must also prove explicit unsubscribe and boundary detach remove the observer. The hosted session consumes that exact handled-error signal through a bounded modeless pump, surfaces the original primary failure after finalization, and orders cleanup and broken-lifetime assertions after it. Modal-frame behavior belongs to Windows Pure coverage. Hosted launch smokes must prove rollback and actual closure through the production session owner. UI-state persistence logs and propagates its contextual failure to the session owner without invoking a window-affine notification from its background continuation. An incomplete dispatcher-affine task is not awaited after its window/pump lifetime is known to be gone; the broken-lifetime assertion is retained and the model outcome is downgraded to rollback while safe cleanup continues. The session still aggregates every persistence, preview, window, handler, view-model, transaction-finalization, notification, and logging failure, and the command's safe-execution boundary owns user-facing reporting. The old Local, Both, and DA execution categories are invalid. The taxonomy guard fails if they reappear. A true DA test must execute through APS WorkItem infrastructure and assert real output/log/model artifacts. Attribute blocks may combine NUnit and routing metadata, such as [Test, RevitLocal]; discovery treats that the same as separate [Test] and [RevitLocal] attributes. Non-routing categories such as [Category("Integration")] remain allowed only as orthogonal facets like external service dependency markers. Test Project Structure Tests live in two locations: 1. In-Tool Tests (src/Tools/<Tool>/Tests/) Tool-specific tests embedded alongside the tool code: src/Tools/ ├── Common/GM/Tests/ │ ├── App/Sessions/UIStateChange/ │ │ └── UIStateChangeReactionTests.cs │ ├── Features/CommitReview/Planning/Plan/ │ │ └── CommitReviewPlanBuilderTests.cs │ ├── Features/Duplicates/Detection/ │ │ └── DuplicateDetectionWorkflowTests.cs │ ├── Integration/Revit/Features/CommitReview/Planning/ │ │ └── CommitReviewPlanningWorkflowTests.cs │ └── Support/ │ └── LoggingSetup.cs └── Structural/SGT/Tests/ ├── App/Persistence/ │ └── UIStateStoreTests.cs ├── Domain/Extents/ │ └── ExtentResolverTests.cs ├── Domain/MemberResolution/Runtime/ │ └── MemberResolutionSpanIndexTests.cs └── Integration/Revit/Features/Placement/ └── PreviewPlacementParityTests.cs 2. Standalone Test Projects (testing/) Infrastructure and cross-cutting tests: testing/ ├── DBTools.ArtifactContracts.Tests/ # Assembly/output verification (non-Revit) ├── TestSupport/ # Shared test utilities │ ├── Execution/ # Revit execution routing attributes │ ├── Logging/ # Shared test logging bridge │ ├── Paths/ # Repo-root and model path resolution │ ├── TestDoubles/ # Shared behavior-neutral doubles │ └── TestHost/ # Local Revit host context helpers └── RevitTestModels/ # Canonical Revit 2026 test models └── 2026/ src/ ├── DBTools.App/Tests/ # App-owned project suite ├── DBTools.Core/Tests/ # Core-owned project suite └── DBTools.Sandbox/Tests/ # Sandbox-owned suite Current repo truth after the direct App/product-tree migration: App/Core/Sandbox project suites now live beside their owners under src/ build and distribution contract projects live under testing/; the App/Core pure and local projects live under src/ the App-owned suite is Revit-hosted because direct App entry and ribbon fixtures require Revit UI assemblies; its [RevitLocal] fixtures dispatch to the fleet DBTools.App.Tests contains the plain App pure fixtures, while DBTools.App.Local.Tests explicitly names only the Addin/Ribbon fixtures that require the full App/Revit host dependency graph DBTools.Core.Tests contains the plain Core pure fixtures, while DBTools.Core.Local.Tests explicitly names Core [RevitLocal] fixtures, including contextual-ribbon hook fixtures that need the full hooks compile surface owner .Pure.Tests projects carry tool pure tests and have no Revit add-in host closure matching .Local.Tests projects remove fixture files owned by .Pure.Tests so plain [Test] fixtures are not also executed inside Revit; the App local project derives its test count from explicit local project membership every current *.Local.Tests.csproj declares an output AssemblyName ending .Local.Tests; file-backed UI dependency closure follows that output identity, while only local projects that explicitly declare DBT_RequiresWpfTestRuntime=true and directly reference Core receive the Core-backed WPF bootstrap Local and DA test projects receive the centrally versioned Newtonsoft.Json reference even when they disable transitive pinning for APS or Roslyn. Each Local and DA graph build checks its completed outputs: primary file names and managed assembly names must be unique, and adjacent files with the same name must have identical SHA256 hashes. Comparisons stay within one lane and Revit year because Local (net10) and the DA client (net8) use different framework assets. BuildTests -y 2026 and BuildTests -y 2027 check the full Local closures before grouped submission. test.sh routes pure suites to dotnet vstest and hosted suites to the daemon CLI so fresh CI and local runs use the same selector contract DBTools.App.Pure.Tests links the BCL-only idle gate and routes Windows Pure execution through the daemon relay DBTools.App.Local.Tests is reachable through ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local, runs Revit-hosted on the fleet, and receives the staged product root with Tools/ Tool test suites stay fully contained under their owner Tests/ directory, but execution hosts stay split by project. Do not consolidate pure, local Revit, and true DA tests into one project unless the build can preserve all three host contracts without pulling the Revit add-in host or APS dependencies into plain [Test] execution. Today the accepted shape is: owner .Pure.Tests.csproj for plain [Test] fixtures owner .Local.Tests.csproj for [RevitLocal] fixtures WorkItem-backed DA project/manifest ownership only when [RevitDA] tests exist for that owner Directory organization rules: keep test files beside the owning tool/project under Tests/ split directories before they grow past roughly 12 test/support files remove empty test directories do not create placeholder folders with no files place shared or test-only collaborators under Support/, and only when they stub true externals or construct native DTO state Setting Up a New Test Project Create the test class in the appropriate Tests/ directory Add NUnit attributes: [TestFixture] and [Test] Reference TestSupport: Add using DBTools.Tests.Shared Add [RevitLocal] or [RevitDA] only when the test needs that execution host TestSupport Library The TestSupport library provides shared utilities for all tests. Execution/ owns the Revit execution attributes: [RevitLocal] routes daemon jobs, and [RevitDA] marks the Sentinel's APS WorkItem test. Paths/ owns repository-root and Revit test-model path resolution. Logging/ owns the shared bridge from NUnit output to DBTools logging. The bridge explicitly initializes shared App paths, then passes the side-effect-free AppPaths.LogsDir value to standalone logging. TestDoubles/ owns behavior-neutral shared doubles used by multiple tool suites. TestHost/ owns local Revit context helpers. Source: testing/TestSupport/Logging/TestLoggingBridge.cs:27-70 Source: src/DBTools.Core/Paths/AppPaths.cs:7-28 Core Test Doubles Shared doubles live in testing/TestSupport/Fakes under the DBTools.Tests.Shared.Fakes namespace. RecordingErrorNotifier Records error, warning, success, and info banner calls for verification: var notifier = new RecordingErrorNotifier(); // ... run code that triggers notifications ... Assert.That(notifier.ErrorCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); Assert.That(notifier.LastTitle, Does.Contain("Error")); Assert.That(notifier.AllBanners, Has.Count.EqualTo(2)); RecordingProgressOverlay Records progress overlay interactions: var overlay = new RecordingProgressOverlay(); // ... run code using progress overlay ... Assert.That(overlay.ShowCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); Assert.That(overlay.CurrentTitle, Is.EqualTo("Processing...")); Assert.That(overlay.StepUpdates, Has.Count.GreaterThan(0)); InlineSafeExecutor Runs ISafeExecutor actions inline (no async dispatch) and records each run's options: var executor = new InlineSafeExecutor(); // ... inject into ViewModel ... Assert.That(executor.RunCount, Is.EqualTo(1)); Assert.That(executor.OptionsHistory, Has.Count.EqualTo(1)); InlineTransactionRunner Executes transactions inline without actual Revit transactions: var runner = new InlineTransactionRunner(); // ... inject into service ... Assert.That(runner.RunCount, Is.EqualTo(2)); Assert.That(runner.TransactionNames, Contains.Item("Apply Mappings")); GM Test Utilities GM Project State GM Pure tests construct the exact ProjectState records the scenario needs. There is no shared fluent state builder or pre-built standard state; each fixture states its own inputs (from DuplicateDetectionEngineTests): var projectState = new ProjectState { Families = new Dictionary<long, ProjectStateFamilyRecord> { [100] = new ProjectStateFamilyRecord { ElementId = 100, Name = "Generic Model" }, [101] = new ProjectStateFamilyRecord { ElementId = 101, Name = "Generic Model 1" } } }; var result = await engine.DetectAsync(projectState); Use ProjectStateFingerprint.ComputeFingerprint(state) from testing/TestSupport/GM/Assertions to assert that a project state did not change. GM Source-Linked Support Reusable GM test infrastructure is owned under testing/TestSupport/GM in the DBTools.Tests.Shared.GM namespace tree. These files are source-linked into the existing GM projects through explicit compile items; there is no new assembly and no broad support glob: Fakes/ provides GM-only inline executors, progress overlays, lifecycle and alert stubs, usage-index doubles, and owner-handle providers. Assertions/ provides project-state fingerprints and model baselines keyed by 64-bit element ids. FamilyMapping/, Mapping/, Composition/, Duplicates/, and Usage/ provide reusable construction graphs and scenarios extracted from fixtures. Revit/ and WindowRuntimeSetup.cs are Local-only host/setup support. Pure-only sources are linked only by DBTools.GM.Pure.Tests; Local-only Revit sources are linked only by DBTools.GM.Local.Tests; lane-neutral helpers are linked by both. Keep executable fixture namespaces and Support/LoggingSetup.cs in place so fixture FQNs and NUnit setup scope remain stable. SGT Test Utilities SGT local harnesses use shared RecordingProgressOverlay for progress recording and keep repo-owned placement, writing, plan-building, and dialog collaborators as explicit unexpected-call sentinels when a composition/sync test should not exercise those flows. Tests that need real placement or planning behavior should use the production services through the appropriate Revit-hosted harness instead of configuring canned service outcomes. Test Path Resolution Resolves test model paths from the test runner environment: daemon-hosted Revit runs use DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_MODELS_DIR, which points at the daemon-staged model directory for the current job; the resolver evaluates this override on every call and does not cache it in the test process the submitted model tree keeps its relative paths below that staged root; ResolveTestModelPath(...) validates the requested relative path and preserves its year, tool, shared-directory, and file-name segments a model below <year>/Regression/ is an operator's working copy whose linked models are not staged; DocumentLease sets the staged copy's Revit links not to load before it opens one, and refuses a regression path outside the staged root Pure fixtures use DBT_TEST_REPO_ROOT; hosted tests use the daemon-staged model root there is no Windows-accessible repo-root metadata path and no %APPDATA% model cache Revit-local tests that create transient fixture families use RevitFamilyTemplateResolver; it derives the exact current-year root from CommonApplicationData/Autodesk/RVT <Application.VersionNumber>/Family Templates, considers only the requested template file names, and orders English-Imperial candidates first with a deterministic path tiebreaker each candidate is accepted only when BasicFileInfo.Extract(...).Format exactly matches the running Revit version; if none match, the fixture is inconclusive with every observed candidate format or extraction error reported The family-template resolver is a capability probe because the template installation is owned by the current Revit host. In contrast, files requested below testing/RevitTestModels are repository-controlled staged inputs and their absence is a failed fixture, not an inconclusive case. // Get base test models directory var modelsDir = TestPathResolver.ResolveTestModelsDir(); // Get specific model path var gmModel = TestPathResolver.ResolveTestModelPath("2026", "GM", "gm_test_model.rvt"); Source: test.sh:1320 Source: testing/TestSupport/Paths/TestPathResolver.cs:37 Source: testing/TestSupport/Paths/RevitFamilyTemplateResolver.cs:11 Writing Pure and Revit-Hosted Tests Plain [Test] is the target marker for pure/off-Revit tests. A pure test should run in a normal NUnit/VSTest process without Revit API references, WPF/window behavior, the Revit add-in host, or APS Design Automation infrastructure. Use [RevitLocal] only when the test genuinely requires local Revit-hosted execution. Use [RevitDA] only when the test executes through a real APS WorkItem path and asserts real WorkItem output, report, model, or sentinel artifacts. The old phrase "DA-compatible" is no longer precise enough for new work. DA coverage requires actual WorkItem execution and output validation. Example: Unit Test for Service Logic Excerpt from src/Tools/Common/GM/Tests/Features/Duplicates/Detection/DuplicateDetectionEngineTests.cs: [TestFixture] public sealed class DuplicateDetectionEngineTests { [Test] public async Task DetectAsync_DetectsFamilyDuplicates_WithSameStemAndParameterOverlap() { // Arrange: real project state with 64-bit element ids var projectState = new ProjectState { Families = new Dictionary<long, ProjectStateFamilyRecord> { [100] = new ProjectStateFamilyRecord { ElementId = 100, Name = "Plate" }, [101] = new ProjectStateFamilyRecord { ElementId = 101, Name = "Plate1" } } }; SetFamilyParameterDiscovery(projectState.Families[100], "Width", "Height"); SetFamilyParameterDiscovery(projectState.Families[101], "Width", "Height"); // Real matchers; only the Revit name query is a stub for the true external var names = new StubElementQuery(new Dictionary<long, string> { { 100, "Plate" }, { 101, "Plate1" } }); var svc = CreateService(names); // Act var res = await svc.DetectAsync(projectState); // Assert: real outcome var famGroups = res.Groups.Where(g => g.Kind == DuplicateKind.Families).ToList(); Assert.That(famGroups.Count, Is.GreaterThanOrEqualTo(1)); var anyPair = famGroups.SelectMany(g => g.Pairs).Any(p => p.FromId == 100 && p.ToId == 101 && p.Score >= 90.0); Assert.That(anyPair, Is.True, "Expected high-score pair between 100→101."); } private static DuplicateDetectionEngine CreateService( IElementNameQuery names, IMaterialCatalog? materials = null, IGraphicsStyleCatalog? styles = null) { var naming = new NamingSimilarity(); return new DuplicateDetectionEngine( new FamilyDuplicateMatcher(naming, new DuplicateParameterSimilarityEvaluator()), new StyleDuplicateMatcher(styles ?? new StubStyleService()), new MaterialDuplicateMatcher(materials ?? new StubMaterialService(), naming), new SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher(naming), names, NullLogger.Instance); } } Example: Build Test DistributionContractTests is a [Category("Build")] fixture over the assembled distribution candidate; SupportedYears comes from the candidate's build metadata: [TestCaseSource(nameof(SupportedYears))] public void DBTools_DoesNotBundleHostAssemblies(int year) { RequireArtifacts(year); var yearPath = GetYearPath(year); var bundledHostAssemblies = Directory .GetFiles(yearPath, "*.dll", SearchOption.AllDirectories) .Select(Path.GetFileName) .Where(fileName => fileName != null) .Select(fileName => fileName!) .Where(fileName => ForbiddenHostAssemblyFiles.Any(forbidden => forbidden.Equals(fileName, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))) .Distinct(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) .OrderBy(fileName => fileName, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) .ToArray(); Assert.That(bundledHostAssemblies, Is.Empty, $"Year {year}: dist output must not bundle Revit host assemblies ({string.Join(", ", bundledHostAssemblies)})"); } DBTools.dll is expected to reference Revit host assemblies; Revit supplies them at runtime. The artifact contract rejects copying those host DLL files into the shipping distribution. Writing Revit Tests Revit integration tests run through test.sh hosted submissions: the daemon CLI dispatches them to the dbtools-daemon fleet, where Revit + NUnit + the add-in host them. A fixture opts into Revit hosting with [RevitLocal] (and receives the ambient UIApplication as shown below). Example: Revit-Hosted Test CategoryTabClassifierTests (src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Tests/Integration/Revit/Features/Comparison/Revit/Extraction/CategoryTab/) classifies real categories from an opened test model: [TestFixture] [RevitLocal] public sealed class CategoryTabClassifierTests : RevitTestBase { protected override string ModelTool => "SGT"; protected override string ModelFileName => "sgt_test_model.rvt"; [Test] public void GetTab_classifies_built_in_model_and_annotation_categories() { var doc = EnsureModelOpen(); var walls = Category.GetCategory(doc, BuiltInCategory.OST_Walls); var textNotes = Category.GetCategory(doc, BuiltInCategory.OST_TextNotes); Assert.Multiple(() => { Assert.That(CategoryTabClassifier.GetTab(walls), Is.EqualTo(SettingTab.ModelCategories)); Assert.That(CategoryTabClassifier.GetTab(textNotes), Is.EqualTo(SettingTab.AnnotationCategories)); Assert.That(CategoryTabClassifier.GetTab(null!), Is.EqualTo(SettingTab.ModelCategories)); }); } } Using RevitHost for Context For tests requiring Revit context: [Test] [RevitLocal] public async Task MyTest_WithRevitContext(UIApplication app) { await RevitHost.RunAsync(app, async () => { // Code runs within Revit context var doc = app.ActiveUIDocument?.Document; Assert.That(doc, Is.Not.Null); }); } RevitHost is the shared local-test contract for Revit-hosted execution. It now does more than just queue into the host: initializes the Revit year from UIApplication.Application.VersionNumber enters the ambient call-gate scope used by daemon-hosted local tests initializes the owned App host through AppRuntimeHostLifecycle.InitializeHost installs the test-host runtime assembly context so WPF name-only DBTools.* loads resolve in the same ALC as DBTools.dll carries the daemon-provided UIApplication as data; DBTools-owned native callback entries use a short main-thread RevitCallGateApiContext scope for their synchronous prefix, while continuations after an await use the product probe or queue and never retain that scope enters RevitAmbientScope for both inline and queued execution; that scope is the sole owner that publishes and restores the ambient UIApplication That means local fixtures should use RevitHost.RunAsync(...) instead of duplicating their own host/add-in/gate checks. Revit-hosted tests that bypass RevitHost can end up depending on ambient driver or desktop startup side effects rather than the shared test-host contract. A fixture releases only the runtime, task host, window owner, static runtime, and exact window overlay host it created; the daemon terminal owns the active Autodesk document's final release. For Revit-hosted runs on the fleet, the dbtools-daemon test driver provides a DBT_TEST_RUN_ID. DBTools uses that test-run identity to keep startup failures headless in automation instead of blocking the job behind a modal DBTools error dialog. Test Doubles: Guidelines When to Use Test Doubles Scenario Approach Revit API dependency Stub it File system access Stub it Network/cloud services Stub it Time-sensitive logic Stub with deterministic time Your own services Use the real implementation Orchestrators/handlers Use the real implementation Anti-patterns to Avoid // BAD: Mocking your own service to make test pass var mockEngine = new Mock<IDuplicateDetectionEngine>(); mockEngine.Setup(e => e.DetectAsync( It.IsAny<ProjectState>(), It.IsAny<IProgress<DuplicateKind>?>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>())) .ReturnsAsync(new DuplicateDetectionResult()); // BAD: Asserting only mock interactions mockService.Verify(s => s.DoSomething(), Times.Once); // Missing: actual outcome assertion! // BAD: Test double that adds domain behavior internal sealed class FakeDuplicateDetectionEngine : IDuplicateDetectionEngine { public Task<DuplicateDetectionResult> DetectAsync( ProjectState projectState, IProgress<DuplicateKind>? progress = null, CancellationToken ct = default) { // WRONG: Reimplementing duplicate matching in the test double var groups = GroupFamiliesBySimilarName(projectState.Families); return Task.FromResult(new DuplicateDetectionResult { Groups = groups }); } } Correct Pattern // GOOD: Use real services, stub only true externals var naming = new NamingSimilarity(); // Real var engine = new DuplicateDetectionEngine( new FamilyDuplicateMatcher(naming, new DuplicateParameterSimilarityEvaluator()), // Real new StyleDuplicateMatcher(new StubStyleService()), // Stub: wraps Revit API new MaterialDuplicateMatcher(new StubMaterialService(), naming), // Stub: wraps Revit API new SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher(naming), // Real new StubElementQuery(testNames), // Stub: wraps Revit API NullLogger.Instance); // GOOD: Assert real outcomes var result = await engine.DetectAsync(projectState); Assert.That(result.Groups, Has.Count.GreaterThan(0)); Assert.That(result.Groups[0].Pairs, Contains.Item( Has.Property("FromId").EqualTo(100) .And.Property("ToId").EqualTo(101))); Running Tests Available route: plain dotnet test Daemon entry projects use the vendored 0.20.9 adapter. Hosted entries generate per-year Sources with their matching Models and Includes. The runsettings set RequiresInteractiveDesktop from the selected Pure source assemblies; the daemon always runs test code on its private hidden desktop. This route is validated for hosted and Pure. A true value routes UI rendering to a worker with an interactive private desktop; it never permits a test on the user's visible desktop. Hosted sources build as plain NUnit libraries, because Revit runs NUnit in-process. Pure sources keep Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, because the daemon runs each Pure source in its own VSTest testhost. The DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REQUIRES_INTERACTIVE_DESKTOP environment variable overrides the generated value. The package pin (DBT_DaemonTestAdapterSha256) is checked by dotnet test only; IDE runners and vstest.console do not run it. Set DBTOOLS_DAEMON_RELAY_URL to the configured relay URL. test.sh reads the same environment variable (or accepts --relay); credentials remain daemon-owned. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_MACHINE_ID pins a machine in either route. Leave it unset for daemon AUTO selection. # The coordinator supplies this same variable to test.sh and the adapter. : "${DBTOOLS_DAEMON_RELAY_URL:?Set the configured daemon relay URL}" # Run one hosted fixture against Revit 2026. DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS=2026 dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/GM.Hosted.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FamilyDeepScanTests.GM_DeepScan_Smoke" # Discover tests without submitting a request. dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/GM.Hosted.Entry.csproj --list-tests # Run a Pure net10.0-windows fixture through windows_vstest. dotnet test testing/Daemon/Pure/GM.Pure.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~UIStateCacheTests.SetAsync_WritesTheStableCamelCaseGoldenFormat" Use one route per run. The coordinator uses test.sh below; it does not launch these adapter entries, so one invocation produces one daemon submission. Coordinator route: test.sh test.sh is the coordinator's repository test route. Its current submission path uses the published dbtools-daemon-cli 0.20.9. It resolves the requested project lane, runs pure [Test] fixtures locally when the host supports them, and submits daemon-routed Pure and Revit-hosted [RevitLocal] fixtures as a job to the dbtools-daemon relay; the daemon boots Revit + NUnit + the add-in on the fleet. Auth is daemon-owned; the repo entrypoint does not accept or persist relay tokens. The wrapper resolves project ownership before building. It builds each selected lane/year as one graph and finishes all requested graphs before the first submission. Each graph produces daemon input metadata and a prepared-artifact receipt containing source content identity, the selected project set, and output hashes. The receipt uses repository-relative paths and is keyed by lane, year, and project set. Compiling one tool does not overwrite another tool's receipt. A second edit to an already-dirty file invalidates the receipt. A source edit during compilation refuses the receipt. Normal test builds the current selection; --no-build is an explicit strict consumer for matching prepared artifacts and fails before routing when source, selection, or output bytes differ. Git's configured filters preserve source identity across tracked LFS model hydration. Receipt hashes still verify the selected model payload bytes. Use repeatable --project PATH[,PATH...] with test, validate-request or list to intersect tool, scope and fixture selectors with repository-relative test project paths. Use forward slashes. Unknown paths and paths outside the requested tool/scope fail with exit 2. For Linux CI acceptance without Sandbox's Windows runtime, use: ./test.sh test --tool BUILD --scope pure --project testing/DBTools.Build.Tests/DBTools.Build.Tests.csproj,testing/DBTools.Distribution.Tests/DBTools.Distribution.Tests.csproj ./test.sh list --projects <selectors> prints only sorted scope<TAB>project.csproj rows. Paths are repository-relative with forward slashes. Every resolved project appears, even when static discovery finds no methods. This mode cannot be combined with --summary. An empty selection fails with exit 2. CI consumes these rows directly and rejects an explicitly requested scope absent from the listing. After the product-only BuildAll step, CI invokes test --compile-only per Windows scope, building each selected test graph itself and using that scope's --project CSV and the original selectors. It saves the exact list --projects rows used for the producer selection and writes a schema-2 prepared-artifact receipt after the selected assembly, dependency, model, and include closure is built and hash-matched. Pure is year-free. Local receives the selected year; DA is always 2026. Transfer each selection's build-record-*.json and the union of its recorded output files, models, and includes to the same relative paths in a clean checkout. Windows CI consumes its prepared artifacts with test --no-build and the same scope, project set, selectors and hosted year. Receipts require the exact project set. A source or output mismatch fails without rebuilding. Linux native CI uses the ordinary test route and builds its selected graph. validate-request accepts the consumer's --no-build argv without reading test results and validates model metadata without copying model payloads. The wrapper stores verified output bytes in the hash-addressed ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dbtools-test-inputs/<worktree-sha256>/objects/<sha256> cache and stages them into a private run directory on that filesystem before any submission. It rechecks the hash before reuse and uses a hard link or copy fallback, so later builds cannot change the frozen bytes. Local execution and daemon upload use that frozen copy. Local Pure runs execute the frozen assembly through dotnet vstest. For Pure fixtures, the wrapper exports DBT_TEST_REPO_ROOT for repository and restore-graph lookup in relocated outputs. Direct Pure callers can use embedded DBTools.RepoRoot metadata. The testhost working directory does not select restore inputs. Local jobs use the daemon-staged model root and temporary work directories without requiring a worker checkout. On Windows, the two Linux-native BUILD projects are skipped before compilation with a notice; the separate closed DIST acceptance suite remains daemon-routed. Explicit --project selection of only native projects fails before building on Windows. A changed selection with no runnable Windows projects and no explicit projects skips with a notice. Repeat --fixture to select several exact classes. Attribute lists, separate attribute lines, qualified NUnit attributes and implicit fixtures are supported. Local filters end the fixture FQN with a dot, so similarly named fixtures are not included. Daemon submissions use repeatable --fixture-fqn arguments restricted to the submitted project. SGT Pure selects both projects. The Local scope submits one request per selected year with the existing selected assembly and model contract. Two selected years remain separate requests so their reports and model closures stay independent. Pure daemon execution submits one request per selected project; each request carries only its own fixture selectors. All selected projects run even when one fails, and the aggregate returns a nonzero exit if any failed. DBT_PURE_CONCURRENCY sets the maximum number of concurrent daemon Pure submissions; it defaults to 2. Native Linux Pure suites execute serially. Signal and EXIT cleanup terminates in-flight submit process groups on Linux. TERM also stops graph builds and local test processes there. Windows waits for command status without Bash job control. Independent scopes continue after a failed execution. A fixture selects only requested scopes that own it. DBT_MSBUILD_MAX_CPU_COUNT controls graph build parallelism and defaults to 2. ./test.sh rerun --request REQUEST_ID reruns failures from previously submitted bytes. It does not compile or test edited source. Use a normal test invocation for new bytes. Source: test.sh:1 Basic Usage # Run everything (pure in-process; Revit-hosted on the fleet) ./test.sh test --scope all --years 2026,2027 # Scope to one tool ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure # Scope to several tools ./test.sh test --tool GM,RecordSet --scope pure # Run a project suite directly ./test.sh test --tool BUILD ./test.sh test --tool APP ./test.sh test --tool CORE # Run the direct App Revit-hosted suite (the wrapper builds the selected current artifacts) ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 # A single test or fixture ./test.sh test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DuplicateDetection" ./test.sh test --fixture GirtPaneViewModelReactiveSyncTests # Several fixtures; the regular test invocation builds the current selection ./test.sh test --fixture FixtureOne --fixture FixtureTwo # Prepare selected artifacts without executing tests, then consume them strictly ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 --compile-only ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 --no-build # Recheck failures from a previous daemon request, or select changed owners ./test.sh rerun --request REQUEST_ID ./test.sh test --scope pure --changed-since HEAD # Several exact hosted tests in one daemon request ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope local -y 2026 \ --fqn DBTools.SGT.Tests.Integration.Revit.Features.WallAnalysis.Revit.Geometry.WallGeometryBuilderTests.BuildGeometryContext_builds_explicit_host_and_linked_targets_with_truthful_layers \ --fqn DBTools.SGT.Tests.Integration.Revit.Features.WallAnalysis.Revit.Geometry.WallGeometryBuilderTests.WallContextAndGeometryResolvers_report_missing_wall_and_null_context Each --fixture resolves one exact fixture class from current project membership and narrows compilation to its owning project. Local Pure execution ORs the fixture FQNs with FullyQualifiedName~; the daemon receives one exact --fixture-fqn per class. A longer fixture whose name contains the requested name is not selected by the ownership resolver. Daemon Timeouts For hosted test and submit requests, the published dbtools-daemon-cli 0.20.9 contract uses --queue-timeout HH:MM:SS to bound the wait for a Revit lease and --execution-timeout HH:MM:SS to bound execution after the lease is acquired. The wrapper forwards the two values independently. The retired single --timeout option is not accepted. ./test.sh validate-request --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 \ --queue-timeout 00:05:00 \ --execution-timeout 00:30:00 Source: test.sh:33 Source: test.sh:231 Source: test.sh:848 Host selection follows each test's metadata: a plain [Test] runs in-process, and a [RevitLocal] fixture runs Revit-hosted on the fleet. Hosted local runs use -y/--year to select the Revit model and binary year; --keep-open is not supported because the daemon owns the fleet Revit lifecycle. The only [RevitDA] test is the Sentinel; no owner tool has WorkItem-backed tests. Output test.sh prints the underlying execution summary: dotnet test output for pure suites and daemon CLI job output for hosted suites. Apply the repository test-pipeline failure collection policy: preserve independently valid failures and cleanup evidence, stop only when a prerequisite invalidates later work, and use the smallest affected fixture or suite while iterating. Run the complete required gate on the settled exact candidate or when changed inputs invalidate earlier evidence. Test Discovery Discovery is static and project-membership based: local fixtures must be compiled into a tool's *.Local.Tests.csproj, Pure fixtures into a matching *.Pure.Tests.csproj or an unsuffixed standalone project under testing/<project-directory>, and true DA fixtures must be compiled into *.DA.Tests.csproj with [RevitDA] WorkItem tests (the current target is DBTools.DesignAutomation.Sentinel.DA.Tests). test.sh list exposes the request-side view without launching Revit; hosted execution discovery is owned by the daemon job after submission. # List discovered tests without running them ./test.sh list --scope all # List the discovered tests for one tool ./test.sh list --tool GM --scope all Parallel Agent Safety build.sh and test.sh take no lock. Run one build or test command per worktree at a time; agents run heavy commands through .agents/work/worktree_guard.sh, which holds a per-worktree lock. The wrapper does not take a local Revit process lock: pure tests run in-process, and Revit-hosted tests dispatch to the dbtools-daemon fleet, which serializes and provisions Revit hosts on its side. There is no longer a user-global add-in config to quarantine. CI CI runs the same test.sh entrypoint so semantics stay identical between local and CI: # Build / app / core suites ./test.sh test --tool BUILD ./test.sh test --tool APP ./test.sh test --tool CORE The CI workflow validates its dispatch inputs on an Ubuntu preflight job, then runs the same test.sh request on the self-hosted runner. CI holds no APS credentials, so a CI request that selects --scope da fails at the Sentinel. APS Design Automation Sentinel Source: test.sh (run_da_scope) Source: testing/DBTools.DesignAutomation.Sentinel.DA.Tests/ LightweightSentinel_ExecutesRealDesignAutomationWorkItem is the one real APS Design Automation test. It zips the Sentinel appbundle, uploads it and the seed model, and runs a Revit 2026 WorkItem in Autodesk's cloud. The test project targets plain net8.0 and loads no Revit or Windows API, so it runs on Linux or Windows with dotnet test. The daemon never runs it. Only the operator, or the coordinator agent with the operator's standing permission, runs it. Sub-agents, CI and the daemon hold no APS credentials. Run it from the repository root with the APS app credentials in the shell: APS_CLIENT_ID='<client id>' APS_CLIENT_SECRET='<client secret>' ./test.sh test --tool DA-SENTINEL --scope da APS_CLIENT_ID and APS_CLIENT_SECRET are required. When either is missing, the test fails with a message that names both variables. It never skips. APS_BUCKET optionally selects the OSS bucket (default dbtools-tests). The WorkItem part takes 5–12 minutes. The test stops waiting after 12 minutes. Each run spends APS processing time for one Revit 2026 WorkItem. Monthly allowance: the operator's Autodesk account includes 300 free APS processing minutes per month (APS product details, noted 2026-11-05). Billing counts compute time, not the wall-clock wait. The first two Sentinel runs (2026-11-05) used 30,540 compute milliseconds together, about 15 s each. Use the allowance to keep APS support working, and spend it carefully: run the smallest test that answers the question, and do not repeat a run whose result is already known. test.sh builds the Revit 2026 DA graph and runs the frozen test assembly on this host. It writes result.trx and the NUnit work files (the uploaded bundle zip and the downloaded WorkItem output) to .artifacts/test-results/<run>/DBTools.DesignAutomation.Sentinel.DA.Tests/. For --scope da it rejects submit, rerun, --result-json and daemon options. A da-only request rejects every year other than 2026; a request that also selects pure or local must include 2026. Each run creates its own appbundle version and activity version, binds a new run alias (run<32 hex digits>) to each, and writes to an output object named with the same id. The activity loads the appbundle version that this run uploaded. The test asserts the RevitVersion that Revit reports from inside the WorkItem. After the run, pass or fail, the test deletes all but the newest two versions of the Sentinel activity and of the Sentinel appbundle, and the aliases that point at them, at most 25 versions of each resource per run: Activities go first. An appbundle alias that a remaining activity version loads is kept, with its version, even when the two resources have different version counts. An activity or appbundle that does not exist yet has nothing to prune; each resource is pruned even when the other fails. When the activities' references cannot be read, every appbundle alias is kept and only versions that no alias names are deleted. A version or alias that is already gone counts as deleted. A cleanup failure is reported together with the run's own failure. Text from APS (error bodies, SDK exception messages and the WorkItem report) is redacted before it reaches a log line, an exception or the TRX: the client id and secret, every issued token, bearer tokens, Authorization/Cookie headers and credential fields are replaced, and long text is truncated. The other tests in the project need no credentials and make no network calls: a fake HTTP handler covers version binding, pagination, token renewal, redaction, pruning and cleanup, run identity, the bundle layout and the credential failure. Agents run only these: ./test.sh test --tool DA-SENTINEL --scope da -f 'TestCategory!=RevitDA' Debugging Test Failures Common Issues 1. "Missing required test params file" Cause: Running a fixture without its declared model input. Both the adapter entry and the coordinator route stage model inputs declared by the test project. Fix: Use the primary adapter entry or the coordinator route: DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS=2026 dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/GM.Hosted.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FamilyDeepScanTests.GM_DeepScan_Smoke" ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 2. "Source files appear newer than build artifacts" Cause: Source code was modified since the last build. Fix: Run the selected suite through the wrapper; it rebuilds the exact current test project and required runtime before submission: ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 Note: Hosted submission no longer consumes a pre-existing assembly opportunistically.
