The selected build and artifact resolution are one required wrapper workflow. 3. Revit host issues Cause: Revit-hosted ([RevitLocal]) tests no longer launch Revit locally; the dbtools-daemon fleet owns the Revit host. Fix: Run through the adapter entry or coordinator route and let the job dispatch to the fleet: DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_YEARS=2026 dotnet test testing/Daemon/Hosted/GM.Hosted.Entry.csproj \ --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FamilyDeepScanTests.GM_DeepScan_Smoke" ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 4. Test passes in isolation but fails in batch Cause: Shared state pollution between tests Fix: Ensure [SetUp] and [TearDown] properly isolate state: [SetUp] public void SetUp() { _notifier = new RecordingErrorNotifier(); _overlay = new RecordingProgressOverlay(); // Reset any shared state } [TearDown] public void TearDown() { _notifier.Reset(); _overlay.Reset(); } 5. BUILD artifact prerequisite failure Cause: Required build outputs are missing. Artifact tests fail instead of silently creating prerequisites or reporting an inconclusive result. Fix: Build the required years explicitly. On the shared Linux host, prefix each command with host-gate: ./build.sh BuildTests -y 2026 ./build.sh BuildTests -y 2027 ./test.sh test --tool BUILD --scope pure --fixture ResourceAssemblyVersionContractTests Candidate-consuming fixtures additionally require AssembleDistributionCandidate on a clean, committed source tree. The wrapper does not infer that prerequisite from a test filter. Viewing Test Logs DBTools writes the most recent log file to %APPDATA%/DBTools/Logs/; for Revit-hosted jobs those logs come back through the daemon job output. Real Examples from the Codebase GM: Duplicate Detection Tests DuplicateDetectionEngineTests (src/Tools/Common/GM/Tests/Features/Duplicates/Detection/) tests the real duplicate detection algorithm with minimal stubs: [Test] public async Task DetectAsync_DetectsFamilyDuplicates_WithSameStemAndParameterOverlap() { var projectState = new ProjectState { ... }; var names = new StubElementQuery(...); // Stub: Revit element names var svc = CreateService(names); // Real matchers; stub material and style catalogs var res = await svc.DetectAsync(projectState); // Assert on actual detection results Assert.That(famGroups.Count, Is.GreaterThanOrEqualTo(1)); Assert.That(anyPair, Is.True, "Expected high-score pair between 100→101."); } Build: Host Assembly References DistributionContractTests (testing/DBTools.Build.Tests/Distribution/) inspects the assembled distribution candidate for every requested Revit year: [TestCaseSource(nameof(SupportedYears))] public void DBTools_ReferencesRequiredHostAssemblies(int year) { RequireArtifacts(year); var path = Path.Combine(GetYearPath(year), DistributionContract.PrimaryAssemblyDll); Assert.That(File.Exists(path), Is.True, $"{DistributionContract.PrimaryAssemblyDll} not found for {year}"); var refs = GetReferencedAssemblies(path); var requiredReferences = new[] { Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(DistributionContract.RevitApiUiDll), }; foreach (var required in requiredReferences) { Assert.That(refs.Any(r => r.Equals(required, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)), Is.True, $"Year {year}: DBTools.dll should reference {required} for Revit host integration"); } } Cross-References Test Pipeline Architecture: ../architecture/test-pipeline.md New Tool Guide: new-tool-guide.md Build System: ../architecture/build-pipeline.md Verification Status Check Status Source anchors for all new claims Yes UNVERIFIED markers where needed No (all verified) Cross-references added Yes Examples tested N/A (documentation) No assumptions without evidence Yes Verified by: BUILDTEST_Session 04-15-26-0543am Date: 2026-04-15 Summary Checklist When writing tests, ensure: Tests use real service implementations where possible Only true externals (Revit API, filesystem, network) are stubbed Tests assert on outcomes, not just mock interactions Tests are marked with appropriate categories (RequiresRevitUI, etc.) [SetUp] and [TearDown] properly isolate test state Test doubles don't add domain behavior Failing tests trigger production code investigation first

developer-guide/index.html.title: Developer Guide | DB Tools
developer-guide/index.html.summary: Developer Guide This guide describes how DBTools is built, structured and tested, and how to develop its tools. Section Contents Architecture Components, startup, build and test pipelines, assembly loading, themes Projects The Core, App, Sandbox and Presentation projects Tools (Technical) Implementation of each tool Developing Creating tools, settings packs, hooks, warnings, Sandbox integration, testing Troubleshooting Common errors and the logs Requirements the .NET SDK pinned in global.json; build.sh and build.ps1 install it when it is missing; Python 3.10 or later on Linux and WSL; Desktop Revit 2026.5 or later, or Revit 2027, to run the add-in. Building does not need Revit. Building ./build.sh # BuildAll: build, validate and publish both years ./build.sh BuildApp -y 2026 # product assemblies for one year ./build.sh AssembleDistributionCandidate -y 2026 pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 BuildAll # native Windows BuildAll, ValidateDistributionCandidate, PromoteToDist, BuildBundle and BuildInstaller always build every supported year; a -y that omits one fails. See Build Pipeline. Testing ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure # one tool, without Revit ./test.sh test --tool APP --scope local -y 2026 # in Revit, through the daemon ./test.sh test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SomeTestName" ./test.sh test --scope all Revit-hosted tests run on the dbtools-daemon fleet. See Test Pipeline. Architecture Revit └─ DBTools.addin → DBTools.dll (App: entry, lifecycle, ribbon) ├─ DBTools.Core.dll (execution, transactions, settings, logging, tool registry) ├─ DBTools.Presentation.dll (stable WPF resources and shells) │ └─ DBTools.HandyControl.dll └─ Tools/DBTools.<Tool>.dll (one assembly per tool) Manifests. Each tool declares its assembly, module, ribbon commands, availability types, settings and Sandbox windows in manifest.yml. App embeds all manifests and loads each declared tool from Tools/ by explicit path. Product tree. Each supported year is one directory with DBTools.addin, the four top-level assemblies and Tools/. Third-party libraries are merged into their owner assemblies. Window-scoped themes. Each window merges the theme into its own resources, not into Application.Resources, so DBTools does not change other add-ins. See Architecture Overview. Writing documentation The wiki is built with DocFX from wiki/. Write developer and user pages in the style of Unix reference documentation (Debian and GNU manuals, man pages): State what a component is, what it does, how it works, how to use it and its limits. Put the main point first. Use plain declarative sentences in the present tense and the active voice; use the imperative in procedures. Use the names the code uses, one term per concept. Use lists for steps and parallel items, tables for tabular data, and code blocks for commands, paths and literal values. Document commands as a synopsis, options and examples. Describe the current behavior only. Leave out change history, status and verification notes, dates, issue numbers, and the vocabulary of the process that produced a change. Keep a history note only for a migration step or compatibility break the reader needs. Leave out filler, hedging and repeated summaries. State each real limitation once, where it applies. Verify every technical claim against the current code, scripts and configuration before you write or keep it. The same rules apply to source comments, CLI help and messages. A comment explains a reason, an invariant or a non-obvious API behavior, not what the code already says. CLI help uses man-page form: a synopsis, then one line per option with its default. An error message names what failed, the relevant value or path and, where useful, what to do.

developer-guide/projects/app.html.title: DBTools.App | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/app.html.summary: DBTools.App DBTools.App builds DBTools.dll, the direct Revit add-in entry and App runtime. It targets net10.0-windows for Revit 2026.5+ and 2027. Ownership App owns the public parameterless Revit entry, daemon idle acknowledgement, non-inlined startup/shutdown boundary, startup fallback diagnostics, lifecycle, hooks, ribbon composition, settings host, shutdown, and centrally embedded manifests. Tool assemblies own SGT, Settings, and DialogSuppression. The first startup branch checks DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_ROLE and the exact AssemblyLoadContext.Default owner. The idle copy records DBToolsDaemon.IdleAddin:DBTools with its actual location and returns before normal App startup. Active startup enters ToolWindowCallbackScope and starts the App lifecycle. The BCL-only fallback writer records DBTools.Fallback.log under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs. Tool registration and ribbon AppToolModuleRegistrar asks Core's ToolModuleCatalog to discover embedded manifests. Each tool manifest names its owner, loaded by explicit path from the product year's Tools/ directory in the active owning context. Ribbon planning builds PushButtonData directly from each ToolRegistration: the command assembly's file-backed Location, command full name, and optional concrete command availability full name. There is no App command lifecycle registry, generated bridge, or command fallback resolver. ToolCommand.Execute and IsCommandAvailable enter the stable Presentation callback scope so command callbacks cannot capture an owning context through ExecutionContext. Project contract Item Value Project src/DBTools.App/DBTools.App.csproj Assembly DBTools.dll Target net10.0-windows Direct product references DBTools.Core, DBTools.Presentation Merge owner Generic declared merge mechanism folds ricaun.Revit.UI into App Manifest ownership Embedded centrally in App The App project must not add a loose-copy target for merged ricaun runtime files. The product output stages App at the year root and tool owners below Tools/. Tests App Pure tests cover the idle gate, direct ribbon planning, settings, and startup state. App Local tests cover real Revit ribbon composition and App lifecycle. Hosted staging supplies the complete direct product tree. The coordinator must run both-year Local fixtures and installed/Dev Mode entry proofs; this page does not claim those runtime results. Owner tree The App source tree follows the responsibility owners below: src/DBTools.App/ ├── Addin/ # Revit entry and installed-copy idle acknowledgement ├── Composition/ # DI and manifest-facing registration ├── Host/ # failure, test-run, and window-owner boundaries ├── Lifecycle/ # publication, cleanup, and lifecycle state ├── Logging/ # App logging-window integration ├── Ribbon/ # planning, Revit effects, state, and startup styling ├── Runtime/ # App runtime and local Revit task ownership ├── Settings/ # App settings host and integration ├── Shutdown/ # synchronous shutdown workflow └── Startup/ # preparation, deferred work, effects, and runtime boundary Tests mirror these owners. Pure tests compile only the source slices needed for platform-neutral behavior; Local tests reference the real App project and retain the Revit/UI integration boundary. Startup and shutdown phases AddinEntry has a public parameterless constructor for Revit. Its first OnStartup action checks the daemon role and the entry assembly's actual load context. Only a file-backed entry in AssemblyLoadContext.Default acknowledges the installed idle copy; the acknowledgement key is DBToolsDaemon.IdleAddin:<simple-name> and its value is the entry location. The idle branch returns success without touching ribbon, events, or other startup work. ProductLoadContext, DevModeLoadContext, null contexts, and all other contexts take normal startup. Normal startup enters the non-inlined AppStartupBoundary, initializes the App runtime, validates themes, composes the ribbon, starts the Revit call gate, and publishes deferred startup work. Failure cleanup is synchronous at the owning Revit API boundary and combines primary and cleanup failures. Startup, shutdown and ribbon-runtime failures that cannot reach the normal log use the BCL-only %APPDATA%/DBTools/Logs/DBTools.Fallback.log path so a missing Core/UI dependency does not suppress the diagnostic. OnShutdown follows the same boundary and returns only after the lifecycle cleanup result is complete. An idle installed entry has no owned runtime and returns success directly. The App runtime host lifecycle (ShutdownHost) sub-step, dispatcher-registry retirement, and cleanup summary are recorded to the fallback file after logging is disposed. The Revit task host sub-step still records failures through the live logger. Runtime and composition details AppRuntimeFactory builds the service root once. AppServiceProviderFactory registers logging, settings, UI ownership, Revit call gates, safe execution, command preflight, hooks, alerts, and ribbon composition. AppToolModuleRegistrar discovers embedded manifest resources once, instantiates module owners, captures settings/services/hooks in temporary registration state, validates module responsibilities, and merges the state into the App container. Tool manifests resolve their module, command, availability, and icon owner from the product year's Tools/ image through Core's ToolAssemblyResolver; AppHooks stays in App. It uses the active owning load context, checks the declared PE identity, rejects a loaded same-name image from another path or identity, and does not probe a fallback directory. The command preflight creates the concrete command availability type before execution. ToolCommand.Execute and IsCommandAvailable enter the Presentation callback scope for the owning App/tool assembly, while ExecutionContext flow is suppressed across callbacks so host dispatchers and timers cannot retain a generation context. Ribbon contract Ribbon planning builds controls directly from ToolRegistration. A button's PushButtonData contains the command assembly's file-backed location, command full name, and optional concrete availability full name. Grouped controls preserve manifest order and use the same direct definitions. Existing buttons are reused only when their assembly path and class binding still match; a stale owner fails loudly rather than silently routing to a different generation. On a Dev Mode reload, a retained button can receive a changed availability class. Clearing an existing class requires a Revit restart. Removing, reordering or retyping retained items, or adding to a retained stack, fails and asks for a restart. A change to retained stack placement, membership, or boundaries also fails and asks for a restart. New panel items and grouped-button children can be appended after the retained items. Settings, SGT, and DialogSuppression follow the same registration path as every other manifest-declared tool, and their module/command assembly is the corresponding Tools/ image. Resources App embeds central tool manifests. Each tool owner embeds its icons, raw views, and manifest-declared design-time ViewModels. Presentation owns stable themes and compiled WPF controls. App has one desktop compilation; Pure tests reference that same image. Test and evidence ownership App Pure tests cover role/context decisions, direct planning, settings, and startup-state contracts. App Local tests cover direct entry behavior, real ribbon composition, command availability, lifecycle cleanup, and Revit window ownership. The coordinator runs both supported years and separately proves installed Default-context idle and Dev Mode reload behavior. Documentation and source-level tests do not claim those native results. Build and source maps DBTools.App.csproj emits DBTools.dll and references Core and Presentation. The generic assembly merge folds ricaun.Revit.UI into App; the App project must not add a loose-copy target for that merged implementation. ProductOutput stages App at the year root and standalone tools under Tools/. src/DBTools.App/MAP.md is generated from the current live tree and manifest fields. When an owner directory or test path changes, run python3 .agents/work/canon_source_maps.py; do not hand edit the generated map. Hosted test boundary Local App and tool tests compile against the APIs they exercise, but runtime ownership comes from the staged product tree. Tool project references remain compile references and do not create competing flat product images in the test dependency closure. Hosted inputs include the complete year root with Tools/ preserved, while test assemblies, NUnit files, and companions remain separate inputs. The daemon's ProductLoadContext forwards product references to the same declared product instances used by the App. The App test marker and Revit host support live at the test owner boundary. A hosted test must initialize the selected Revit year and use the shared call gate; a pure test references the normal App and must not run Revit startup or load Revit-typed members. The two lanes share behavior fixtures only when their runtime dependencies are genuinely the same. Project references and release checks App references Core and Presentation directly. Tool projects own all fourteen tool assemblies, including SGT, Settings, and DialogSuppression. Revit API references are compile-only for product output and are never staged as product runtime files. The declared merge props own ricaun.Revit.UI folding and its determinism evidence. Release checks validate App's direct entry identity, embedded manifest ownership, command and availability owners, stable Presentation resources, source-map freshness, and exact year-tree placement. They do not prove installed Revit startup, daemon ProductLoadContext sharing, or Dev Mode reload; those remain coordinator-owned runtime proofs. See Assembly Loading Contract, Project References, and Test Pipeline.

developer-guide/projects/core.html.summary: DBTools.Core DBTools.Core is the foundational library providing shared infrastructure for all DBTools components. It contains Revit execution abstractions, transaction management, safe execution patterns, logging infrastructure, settings management, tool module system, and shared UI components. Overview DBTools.Core serves as the central infrastructure layer, abstracting away Revit API complexities while providing consistent patterns for error handling, logging, and dependency injection across all tools. Test ownership DBTools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests is the Linux-runnable net10.0 suite for portable Core behavior. It owns the Guard, strict JSON enum, safe-execution name, and monotonic-progress cases and references Core directly. DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests is the desktop net10.0-windows suite for normal Core and merged-owner behavior, including collectible composition activation. DBTools.Core.Local.Tests owns Revit-local fixtures, including the physical Progress Overlay fixture; it has a test-only direct reference to DBTools.Presentation because that control remains Presentation-owned. LoggerWindowDispatcherRouterSmokeTests runs real WPF dispatcher routing against desktop Core in the separate Windows VSTest Pure process, not inside Revit. Its nonparallel fixture checks recorded SelfLog fallback, ordered triple-failure propagation, and the posting-caller rejection path without replacing the Revit process's diagnostic writer. The Local logger-window fixture remains responsible for actual window ownership and session behavior. Property Value Assembly Name DBTools.Core.dll Target Framework Desktop net10.0-windows (Revit 2026.5+ and 2027); portable net10.0 WPF Support Desktop target only (UseWPF=true) Nullable Enabled Normal/default Revit-year Core builds emit an evaluated compile/reference assembly under the artifact locations selected by the shared build props. Local tests consume the evaluated Core TargetPath, so pruning the product staging tree does not remove their project-reference input. Responsibilities Revit Execution Abstraction - Thread-safe API access via call gates and run scopes Transaction Management - Unified transaction/subtransaction handling with automatic rollback Safe Execution - Centralized error handling with user notification and logging Logging Infrastructure - Serilog-based structured logging with UI sink Settings System - Type-safe options pattern with persistence and validation Tool Module System - Discovery, registration, and lifecycle management for tools Shared UI Components - Window bases, alert dialogs, progress overlays, and behaviors Manifest validation Embedded YAML is deserialized only into parser-private nullable DTOs. The parser immediately promotes each resource into immutable, constructor-validated public manifest values; partially populated public manifests are not a supported state. ToolManifestValidationPolicy then validates cross-resource rules over all successfully promoted entries: duplicate manifest and module identities, plus every warning-disable target against the complete ordinal set of declared ribbon-tool names. Parse, promotion, and cross-resource errors retain the declaring resource and original cause. Key Components Revit Execution Layer ElementIdConverter.ToLong preserves Revit element identities. ToInt remains a checked conversion for actual integer contracts, including built-in category IDs. SGT framing diagnostics and TDV failed-element warnings retain full-width IDs so diagnostic formatting cannot replace the original outcome with an overflow. IRevitCallGate The unified entry point for executing Revit API callbacks, supporting both inline (modal) and queued (modeless) execution modes. public interface IRevitCallGate { bool InGate { get; } Task<T> RunAsync<T>(Func<UIApplication, T> work, CancellationToken ct = default, RevitCallGateMode mode = RevitCallGateMode.Auto); Task RunAsync(Action<UIApplication> work, CancellationToken ct = default, RevitCallGateMode mode = RevitCallGateMode.Auto); } Call-gate admission is synchronous by construction. Async-state-machine Action<UIApplication> delegates and generic Task, Task<T>, ValueTask, and ValueTask<T> result shapes are rejected before context resolution or queue scheduling. Nullable ValueTask result types are rejected as well. Reference-typed multicast result delegates are rejected before invocation, and all reference-typed results receive a runtime awaitable check after invocation to catch interface-erased Task and boxed ValueTask values. Custom awaiter structs are outside this check. QueuedRevitCallGate and the host's RevitCallGateTask each require an ILogger from their composition owner (App passes its runtime logger to AppLocalRevitTaskLifecycle.Start). A missing logger is a construction error; production does not substitute a null logger for queued Revit work. RevitCallGateTask runs every queued call that was waiting when a native Execute turn starts, in order, within a 50 ms budget after the first call; calls queued during the turn wait for the next one. A call that leaves a transaction open, or that creates a transaction group (its owner calls RevitCallGateTurnBoundary.EndAfterCurrentCall()), is the last call of its turn. Every raise is posted to the Revit dispatcher, also from the dispatcher thread, so the raise for leftover work runs after Execute returns. The task logs a throttled Debug [CallGate/Turns] summary of turn count, queue depth, Raise-to-Execute gap and Execute duration. A queued gate call costs one Revit round trip when it waits alone. A caller that needs several reads for one user action makes them in one RunAsync body, or starts independent calls together so one turn runs them all. See Revit execution for the scheduler contract. Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Execution/CallGate/CallGateDelegateValidator.cs:14-43 Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Execution/CallGate/InlineRevitCallGate.cs:26-64 Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Execution/CallGate/QueuedRevitCallGate.cs:38-100 Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Execution/CallGate/RevitCallGateTask.cs Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Execution/CallGate/RevitCallGateTaskQueue.cs Execution Modes: Mode Description Auto Use the current ambient gate when one exists; otherwise queue through the owned ExternalEvent host ForceQueue Always queue through the owned ExternalEvent The active UIApplication, queued-gate depth, and Revit-test depth are internal, scoped ambient state rather than public mutation points. QueuedRevitCallGate owns queued ambient and test scopes, while RevitRunScope owns its application context token. Every scope restores the exact previous value, and repeated disposal is harmless. IRevitRunScope Represents a single Revit run scope (command, modeless session, or test). Owns UIApplication, call-gate, document access, and disposal. Transaction services are scoped registrations resolved through IAppRunScope or ICommandContext with Resolve<T>(). public interface IRevitRunScope : IDisposable { UIApplication UIApplication { get; } IRevitCallGate CallGate { get; } UIDocument GetActiveUiDocument(); Document GetActiveDocument(); Document GetVerifiedActiveDocument(Document expectedDocument, string? context = null); } IAppRunScopeFactory is the App-composed construction boundary for the concrete AppRunScope, which owns scoped service resolution, its IRevitRunScope, and disposal. Scope construction and disposal preserve the primary failure, attempt every owned cleanup step, and report any additional cleanup failures in order. IAppRunScope exposes Resolve<T>() and RevitRunScope directly; there is no separate command-runtime interface. AppRunScopeProfile selects the inline or queued call gate while preserving the manifest InlineUi and QueuedModeless values. GetVerifiedActiveDocument(...) rejects invalid expected or active documents and verifies matching DocumentSessionKey values before returning the active document. Core logging keeps the active file writer and its path in LogFileSink. A file cutover publishes the replacement writer and path before retiring the previous writer; a retirement failure is contextual diagnostic data and does not roll back the committed path. Run Scope Profiles: Profile Use Case Implementation InlineUi Modal commands and daemon-hosted Revit automation InlineRevitCallGate + scoped ITransactionRunner QueuedModeless Long-running/modeless tools QueuedRevitCallGate + scoped ITransactionRunner InlineRevitCallGate Call-gate implementation that executes delegates inline on the Revit UI thread using a supplied UIApplication. Used for modal command execution. public sealed class InlineRevitCallGate : IRevitCallGate { public InlineRevitCallGate(UIApplication uiapp) { ... } public bool InGate => _inGate.Value; public Task<T> RunAsync<T>(Func<UIApplication, T> work, ...) { ... } } Transaction Management ITransactionRunner Provides a unified API for executing Revit model modifications with automatic transaction management. public interface ITransactionRunner { Task RunInActiveDocumentAsync(string name, Action<RevitTransactionContext> action, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<T> RunInActiveDocumentAsync<T>(string name, Func<RevitTransactionContext, T> action, CancellationToken ct = default); Task RunInDocumentAsync(Document doc, string name, Action<RevitTransactionContext> action, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<T> RunInDocumentAsync<T>(Document doc, string name, Func<RevitTransactionContext, T> action, CancellationToken ct = default); } Transaction-runner entrypoints apply the same synchronous admission before entering the call gate or starting a transaction. Reference-typed results also receive a runtime awaitable check inside the transaction body, including interface-erased Task values, so failure rolls the transaction back before commit. TransactionFailureException is the public diagnostic contract for a transaction that did not reach Committed. Its constructors remain Core-internal; callers read the transaction name, terminal status, warnings, blocking failure text and failure-definition identities from the public properties. Tool write boundaries map this exception and Revit refusal exceptions to their tool-specific typed failure while preserving the original exception as the inner cause. Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Transactions/TransactionRunner.cs:26-101 TransactionRunner The primary implementation that wraps all Revit API calls in properly managed transactions: Auto-selects transaction type: Uses SubTransaction if doc.IsModifiable (already in transaction), otherwise creates new Transaction Cross-document protection: Prevents starting transactions on Document B while Document A is modifiable Failure handling: Attaches TransactionFailurePreprocessor from Revit/Transactions to suppress non-critical Revit warnings TransactionFailurePreprocessor.AttachToTransaction sets clear-after-rollback before failure processing starts. A warning is reported as suppressed only after Revit deletes it; a blocking failure or failure-accessor fault records a blocking diagnostic and requests rollback. An accessor fault also keeps the caught exception, which becomes the InnerException of the TransactionFailureException (an AggregateException when several accessors failed). Attachment faults propagate before commit instead of attempting to change rollback options inside the failure callback. The preprocessor also keeps one TransactionFailureRecord per message it reads: severity, description, failure definition GUID, failing element ids and whether the message rolled the transaction back. A fault while reading the failing element ids joins AccessorFaults but never changes how the message resolves. A runner built with new TransactionRunner(gate, logger) logs every record (and every accessor fault) at WARN after the commit, so a log names what Revit objected to; the one-argument constructor logs nothing. GM's apply runners opt in. TransactionFailureProcessingTests keeps the raw Revit failure-preprocessor checks and exercises the runner boundary in a RevitLocal host: a posted blocking failure rolls back a runner-managed transaction and raises TransactionFailureException with the transaction name and blocking diagnostic. The transient document is nonmodifiable afterward and is closed by the fixture. Source: src/DBTools.Core/Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/Transactions/TransactionFailureProcessingTests.cs:53-113 Source: src/DBTools.Core/Revit/Transactions/{TransactionRunner.cs,TransactionExecutor.cs,TransactionBoundary.cs} Usage Example: // Basic modification with automatic transaction await _transactionRunner.RunInActiveDocumentAsync("Create Wall", context => { Wall.Create(context.Document, curve, levelId, false); }); // Get a result from a transaction var wallId = await _transactionRunner.RunInActiveDocumentAsync("Create Wall", context => { var wall = Wall.Create(context.Document, curve, levelId, false); return wall.Id; }); ITransactionGroupService Manages transaction groups for operations requiring multiple undoable transactions to appear as a single undo item. public interface ITransactionGroupService { bool IsActive { get; } Task BeginAsync(string name, CancellationToken ct = default); Task FinalizeAsync(TransactionGroupFinalization finalization, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<bool> IsGroupHealthyAsync(CancellationToken ct = default); } Note: The transaction-group surface is intentionally manual and active-document scoped. Finalization accepts only the explicit Commit and Rollback enum values; unsupported values fail before inactive-session handling. RunAtomicAsync*, BeginAsync(Document, ...), RunAsync(string, Document, ...), and the later RunAsync(Document, string, ...) convenience wrapper were removed as dead or Revit-type-leaking public contract. Callers that need guaranteed cleanup must pair BeginAsync(...) with FinalizeAsync(...) in their own workflow. Revit rolls back a transaction group that is still open when the Revit API callback that started it returns. A modeless GM apply on Revit 2027 showed this on 2026-11-05: under QueuedModeless every call-gate call is its own callback, so a group begun by one call was already closed for the next, and the apply committed outside it. BeginAsync and FinalizeAsync in separate calls therefore keep one group only on an InlineUi gate inside one callback, as SGT's and TDV's modal commands do. Queued modeless work uses IAtomicTransactionGroup.RunAsync, which TransactionGroupService also implements: it begins the group, runs the work, then assimilates the group when keep accepts the result or rolls it back otherwise, all in one gate call. An exception, or cancellation seen at any point before finalization (including after the work returns), rolls the group back and propagates. A document that already has an open transaction is refused before any work, because the group would own nothing to roll back. The work must complete inside that callback, where its gate calls run inline; work that is still pending when the callback returns is cancelled and the group is rolled back. Every outcome is classified by the group status Revit reports after the attempt, not by how many failures were thrown: only a confirmed RolledBack status counts as discarded and only Committed as kept. Anything else throws TransactionGroupOutcomeUnknownException, and the caller must not report the work as discarded. Finalization always clears the active group state and attempts owned disposal. When the requested operation and cleanup both fail, the operation failure stays primary and cleanup failures follow it in an ordered aggregate. Safe Execution ISafeExecutor The central error handling service. All tool entrypoints must execute within ISafeExecutor. public interface ISafeExecutor { Task RunAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IErrorNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<SafeExecutionResult> RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IErrorNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default); } SafeExecutor Implementation Provides comprehensive error handling: Correlation IDs: Each execution gets a unique GUID for log correlation Timing: Tracks elapsed milliseconds for performance analysis Exception logging: Logs full exception details including inner exceptions and XAML parse context Cancellation admission: Checks the supplied token immediately before invoking the caller action inside the protected execution boundary, so pre-cancelled work returns a canceled result without admitting the action Diagnostic ownership: SafeExecution/Runtime/ExceptionDiagnosticsLogger owns exception, cancellation, XAML, and notifier-failure log formatting; SafeExecutor retains execution policy and failure presentation User notification: Shows error banners via IErrorNotifier Failure surfacing boundary: Calls the execution-owned ISafeExecutionFailureSurface on fatal errors; App composition adapts the UI-owned log surface's show action without a Logging-to-SafeExecution dependency Notification presentation: Owns safe-execution banner success/error presentation and notifier-failure logging inside the retained execution boundary Explicit failure policy: RunAsync(...) is fail-fast, while RunWithoutThrowingAsync(...) is the opt-in path for event/UI callers that intentionally suppress propagation after logging/notifying Delayed-hide ownership: ProgressOverlayDelayedHideScheduler retains the dispatcher operation it posts, observes every terminal outcome, and clears pending state only when the completing operation owns the current cancellation token; an aborted or faulted stale operation cannot retire a replacement hide. Source: src/DBTools.Core/SafeExecution/Runtime/SafeExecutor.cs:59-103 Source: src/DBTools.Core/SafeExecution/Runtime/ExceptionDiagnosticsLogger.cs:11-211 Source: src/DBTools.Core/Progress/Overlay/Runtime/ProgressOverlayDelayedHideScheduler.cs:113-139 SafeExecutionOptions (own file in SafeExecution/Domain/): public sealed class SafeExecutionOptions { public enum Mode { SuccessAndError = 0, ErrorOnly = 1, SuppressAlways = 2 } public enum FailureSurfacePolicy { Surface, Suppress } public SafeExecutionOptions(string name); public string Name { get; } public bool LogStart { get; init; } = true; public bool LogCompletion { get; init; } = true; public bool LogFailure { get; init; } = true; public Mode BannerMode { get; init; } = Mode.SuccessAndError; public FailureSurfacePolicy FailureSurface { get; init; } = FailureSurfacePolicy.Surface; public Guid? CorrelationId { get; init; } public static SafeExecutionOptions ErrorBanner(string name, ...); public static SafeExecutionOptions SuppressFailurePresentation(string name); } SafeExecutionOptions owns banner, failure-surface, and logging policy directly. Its required constructor establishes the operation name; all optional policy and properties are immutable after initialization. ToolCommand Base Class Abstract base class for Revit commands that enforces ISafeExecutor usage, run-scope creation, runtime preflight, and centralized error notification. The public IExternalCommand.Execute(...) remains a thin Autodesk adapter: it validates the Autodesk arguments, extracts the non-null UIApplication, and delegates to the package-visible ExecuteCore(...) orchestration seam. That seam resolves ISafeExecutor, ILogger, and IErrorNotifier from the live in-process IAppRuntime, calls the narrow CommandPreflight contract, and creates one CommandContext owning its IAppRunScope before invoking RunAsync(...). Command subclasses use ICommandContext, which is the single command adapter over the scope plus captured command UI/document state. ToolCommand exposes no pass-through service resolution, call-gate, or owner-aware tool-window helpers. A command that owns a window composes its ToolWindowFactory and invokes the resulting IToolWindowSession. public abstract class ToolCommand : IExternalCommand { public Result Execute(ExternalCommandData commandData, ref string message, ElementSet elements) { // Validates Autodesk inputs and delegates to ExecuteCore. } internal Result ExecuteCore(UIApplication uiApplication, ref string message) { // Wraps execution in ISafeExecutor and owns command-scope lifetime. } protected abstract Task RunAsync(ICommandContext context); } Command Preflight Command runtime preflight is exposed to ToolCommand through CommandPreflight; the command entrypoint no longer imports or resolves ToolRegistry directly. Contextual edit ExternalEvent flows also declare the registered command type on their ContextualRibbonInjector implementation and call the same preflight contract before RunEditFlow(...). The concrete CommandPreflight adapter lives in the Core tool command package and coordinates the preflight sequence: resolve an enabled registration, delegate Revit availability through the supplied availability callback, then validate active settings warnings. Registry metadata lookup, ribbon panel flag policy, and settings warning blocking stay inside that adapter so command execution does not mix sequencing with policy checks. internal sealed class CommandPreflight { internal CommandPreflight(ToolRegistry registry, ISettingsProvider settings, Action<RegisteredCommand, UIApplication> validateAvailability, ISettingsWarningService warnings); internal RegisteredCommand ResolveRegisteredCommand(Type commandType); internal Task<RegisteredCommand> ValidateAsync(RegisteredCommand command, UIApplication application, CancellationToken ct = default); } Tool Context ICommandContext Ambient context provided to DBT tool commands, wrapping the current Revit run scope, DI scope, and shared services. public interface ICommandContext : IAppRunScope { UIApplication UIApplication { get; } UIDocument UIDocument { get; } Document Document { get; } ILogger Logger { get; } IWindowOwnerHandleProvider OwnerHandleProvider { get; } void ShowBanner(string title, string message); } Runtime AppRuntimeAccessor Static accessor for the current IAppRuntime. Provides global access to services when DI is not available (e.g., Revit's parameterless constructor requirement). public static class AppRuntimeAccessor { public static bool IsInitialized { get; } public static void Initialize(IAppRuntime runtime); public static void Reset(); public static IAppRuntime RequireInProcessRuntime(string consumerName); public static ILogger Logger { get; } public static ILoggerFactory LoggerFactory { get; } public static ILogger CreateLogger(string categoryName); public static ILogger CreateLogger<T>(); public static T Resolve<T>() where T : notnull; } IAppRuntime Interface for the application runtime container. public interface IAppRuntime { ILogger Logger { get; } ILoggerFactory LoggerFactory { get; } T Resolve<T>() where T : notnull; } IAppRunScope Scoped DI container for per-command lifetimes. public interface IAppRunScope : IDisposable { IRevitRunScope RevitRunScope { get; } T Resolve<T>() where T : notnull; } Logging Infrastructure Logging runtime The logging runtime owns Serilog setup, the UI sink, active log-file path, and manual in-session file rollover. LoggingRuntimeFactory.Create(LoggingOptions) remains the public construction boundary for general consumers and returns ILoggingRuntime. That contract combines ILoggerFactory, lifecycle, current log-path access, debug-level control, and console mirroring. App composition requires the existing internal LoggingRuntime, which implements every required narrow capability. Registration exposes that same host through its interfaces, not as a concrete DI service. The sink, file-session, and instance-metadata capability contracts remain internal to Core. // Public surface (Core): public static class LoggingRuntimeFactory { public static ILoggingRuntime Create(LoggingOptions options); } // Internal implementation: internal sealed class LoggingRuntime : ILoggingRuntime, ILoggingDebugLevelController, ILoggingSinkSource, ILoggingFileSession, ILoggingInstanceMetadata { /* Serilog setup, UI sink, file rollover, metadata */ } The logger window (LoggerWindowHost, LoggerWindowSurfaceSession, LoggerWindowViewModel) depends only on the narrow internal capability contracts, registered inside Core logging composition; nothing outside Core references the concrete host. The view model owns one bounded raw-entry sequence as its retention authority and derives the grouped/expanded Items collection as a presentation projection. Display filters affect only that projection; Copy All and Export enumerate retained raw entries once in arrival order. Logger export treats path selection, retained-entry formatting, and file writing as one operation: a canceled picker is silent; a picker or write failure records the diagnostic without losing a visible export-specific Error entry. File reload reads the active log through LogFileSession.ReadCurrentLogTail while its writer is open. The bounded UTF-8 reader drops only an incomplete first physical line when the byte window starts inside a line; an exactly aligned final line remains. Continuation lines are separate entries. They inherit metadata from a parsed header only when that header remains inside the selected physical-line window. LoggingRuntime.CreateLogger(...) is valid only while the runtime is live. Calling it after disposal throws ObjectDisposedException; it never returns a silent null logger. Logging runtime implementation Features: Serilog integration: Uses Serilog with structured logging UI sink: Feeds log entries to the Logger Window File sink: Custom TextFileSink avoids version conflicts with Serilog.Sinks.File Notification banner logging: User-visible banners are written through the currently configured WindowDiagnostics category logger; error banners are Error, warning banners are Warning, and info/success banners are Information. Notification banner boundaries: Notifications/Composition owns IErrorNotifier construction. NotificationBannerService keeps the public banner API, logging policy, explicit ShowError error route, action-free ShowToast route, sole action-bearing ShowToastActions route, and action-failure surfacing. Banner actions expose one cancellation-aware asynchronous callback; the action command awaits completion, closes only after successful completion when requested, and keeps the banner open on failure or cancellation. NotificationBannerHostRegistry owns dispatcher resolution, owner HWND selection, host creation, top-warning replacement, dismissal, and terminal all-host cleanup. Only an explicit zero owner HWND or the absence of a usable anchor position suppresses a banner. WindowOwnerHandleProvider resolves a closing or closed window to the registered default owner (Revit's main window), so a banner queued by a tool whose window closes before delivery still shows; dialog and file-picker owners resolve the same way. ModalWindow and ModelessWindow start lifecycle tracking in their constructors, before callers can register close handlers. A raw WPF window first seen after it closes uses the default owner only when it was not tracked from construction and has no HWND after EnsureHandle fails; other failures propagate. The window lifecycle record lives in stable Presentation (WindowOwnerHandleLifecycle), so a retained shell never keeps a retired Core generation reachable. Calls already on the UI thread resolve the owner and show synchronously. Worker-thread requests queue owner resolution and banner creation together without waiting for the dispatcher. Their returned handle can cancel delivery before it starts or dismiss the banner after it binds. Queue and callback failures are logged with the request title and kind, and disposed, reset, or retired requests identify the reason they were dropped. Host construction and showing occur outside the registry lock; generation validation and registration are rechecked before presentation. A worker request uses normal dispatcher priority, so a UI-thread request made while it is queued may be presented first; this ordering is intentional. Default-owner registration captures the actual existing UI dispatcher without invoking the HWND supplier, refreshes stale entries, and never creates a dispatcher implicitly. A registry reset invalidates pending requests. Synchronous owner resolution, banner addition, and new-host cleanup failures propagate, with an add failure ordered before a cleanup failure when both occur; later timer and window-close cleanup callbacks remain logged best-effort. Terminal reset snapshots and clears registrations first, attempts each host, and reports cleanup failures after all attempts. WpfDispatcher.Invoke is synchronous; WpfDispatcher.Post always queues and returns an owned completion task. A callback failure faults that task with the original exception without rethrowing to the dispatcher error boundary. An aborted dispatcher operation cancels the task. Direct dispatcher callbacks still use the existing dispatcher error boundary. Banner dismissal explicitly observes/logs the completion task. NotificationBannerWindowViewModel owns banner item state, visible-item projection, overflow state, action commands, expanded/collapsed state, and per-item auto-close cancellation. NotificationBannerTimingController owns every delayed close/auto-close task under one window-lifetime cancellation source, uses required TimeProvider.System at the sole production construction site, retains only in-flight operations, retires each operation when observation completes, dispatches callbacks to the owning dispatcher, and observes/logs callback failures; virtual-time tests use the official FakeTimeProvider and disposal cancels the lifetime before the window can receive late callbacks. Notification host lifecycle: Host construction remains outside the registry lock. Each host rechecks its disposed state around the final AddBanner presentation steps, while reset closes hosts on their owning dispatchers. WpfDispatcher.Invoke and file-picker/alert return-value APIs are synchronous and may wait for their owning dispatcher; worker notification delivery uses WpfDispatcher.Post and does not wait. Manual in-session rollover: Logger UI can force file logging to switch to a new file path on demand Thread enrichment: Adds thread ID to all log entries Instance identification: Uses the runtime-owned RevitInstanceIdentifier for the current process identity and Revit year Log rotation: Automatic cleanup of old log files by age, count, and total size Logger Window Composition LoggerWindowHost owns the logger-window error relay and registers it through the narrow ILoggingSinkSource contract (not the concrete logging runtime) during host startup, and toggles debug level through ILoggingDebugLevelController. It implements the UI-owned IWindowErrorLogSurface, not the SafeExecution contract. At the App composition root, SafeExecutionFailureSurface adapts that surface's Show action to ISafeExecutionFailureSurface, so SafeExecution owns failure policy while Logging remains unaware of it. Error-boundary banners depend on IWindowErrorBanner; App composition supplies that surface through the concrete notification package, so DBTools.Core.UI.Windows does not import logging composition or notification packages. The host receives the UI-owned IFilePicker and passes it to LoggerWindowSurfaceSession; the session owns owner-window-aware save-path selection and LoggerWindowViewModel raises an internal export-path request instead of storing a WPF Window or file-picker service. The host still supplies ILogger<LoggerWindowViewModel> to the view model, so the logger window does not use lazy service-location or static runtime logging to build its view model and low-level path ownership stays separate from WPF file dialogs. LoggerWindowViewModel keeps buffered log ingestion in Logging/ViewModels/LoggerWindowViewModel.Buffering.cs, filtering in Logging/ViewModels/LoggerWindowViewModel.Filtering.cs, and file reload/export operations in Logging/ViewModels/LoggerWindowViewModel.FileOperations.cs. Posted logger-window operations have one router that observes rejection, abortion, and callback failure exactly once. Terminal host/session cleanup attempts every owned resource in order and preserves one original failure or an ordered aggregate. Core primary-failure boundaries use the internal contained-diagnostic helper so a failed ILogger write falls back to Serilog SelfLog without replacing the primary exception or skipping later cleanup. ContainedDiagnostic.TryWrite(...) returns null after a successful requested write. After a write failure, it attempts contextual Serilog SelfLog reporting. If SelfLog returns (including when disabled), it returns the original diagnostic exception. If SelfLog also throws, it returns an AggregateException whose inner exceptions are ordered as the requested-write failure, then the SelfLog failure. It never throws that aggregate. Callers may ignore the returned diagnostic. WindowErrorPresenter retains it as secondary presentation-failure data. LoggerWindowDispatcherRouter runs inline work on the owning dispatcher and propagates its action failure to that caller. For posted work, it reports an action, posting, or cancellation failure to the supplied handler at most once. If that handler throws, the router attempts to write both failures through Serilog SelfLog (which writes nothing when disabled). If the diagnostic write also throws, one AggregateException preserves the reported failure, handler failure, and diagnostic failure in that order. The aggregate escapes the reporting context: the target dispatcher for a queued action, the posting caller for a rejected or already-aborted operation, or the thread raising Aborted (including dispatcher shutdown). This preserves causes at the router boundary; it does not guarantee a WPF error handler is registered or that shutdown continues. LoggerWindowSurfaceSession retains its existing contained-diagnostic policy for synchronous failures. Core file picking exposes cardinality-specific contracts: FilePickerPathRequest owns single-file, folder, and save-file requests, while FilePickerPathsRequest owns multi-file requests. IFilePicker accepts the corresponding request type for each result cardinality, so cross-cardinality dispatch is unrepresentable. The concrete FilePicker keeps path admission and file-type mapping private, and uses WPF's built-in OpenFolderDialog for owner-aware folder selection. Workflow-specific text and defaults stay with their owners: the logger window owns export-log naming, TDV settings owns library/fallback RVT picker titles, and RecordSet owns target-folder, host-file, and DWG picker titles. Core does not carry TDV, RecordSet, or log-export convenience factories in the shared request contract. AppPaths.LogsDir is the single log-directory path contract. Designer builds (DBT_IsDesignerBuild): Revit sources excluded for XAML designer wpftmp builds: Special handling for temporary projects during BAML compilation Source: src/DBTools.Core/DBTools.Core.csproj InternalsVisibleTo The runtime assembly and these test identities have access to Core internals: DBTools DBTools.App.Pure.Tests, DBTools.App.Local.Tests DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.Local.Tests, DBTools.ElevationTags.Local.Tests DBTools.FoundationTags.Local.Tests, DBTools.FramingJoins.Local.Tests DBTools.GM.Local.Tests, DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.Local.Tests DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes.Local.Tests, DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests, DBTools.Core.Local.Tests DBTools.DialogSuppression.Local.Tests, DBTools.ERFT.Local.Tests DBTools.RecordSet.Local.Tests, DBTools.TDV.Local.Tests, DBTools.VTC.Local.Tests Core test projects use explicit <Compile> membership. DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests owns sandbox-safe pure fixtures such as Tools/Hooks/ContextualRibbon/ContextualRibbonInjectorBaseTabTests.cs; DBTools.Core.Local.Tests owns local/Revit-capable fixtures plus local support stubs under Support/, including the Autodesk.Revit.UI.IExternalCommandAvailability compile stub. Folded Core test mirrors use owner folders under Tools/*, Settings/*, Progress/, Revit/*, and UI/Windows/*; the explicit compile links in the pure and local projects are updated in lockstep with those moves. Current identity-focused mirrors include Settings/Alerts/SettingsAlertRequestBuilderTests.cs, Settings/Catalog/SettingsCatalogTests.cs, Settings/State/Warning/WarningChangedEventArgsTests.cs, Progress/Overlay/Runtime/ProgressOverlayDelayedHideSchedulerTests.cs, Tools/Hooks/ContextualRibbon/SystemSelection/ContextualRibbonSystemSelectorTests.cs, and UI/Theming/Window/WindowThemeApplicatorTests.cs. developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.title: DBTools.Presentation | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.summary: DBTools.Presentation DBTools.Presentation.dll is the WPF assembly that stays loaded for the life of the Revit process. It is staged at the root of each product year, beside DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Item Value Project src/DBTools.Presentation/DBTools.Presentation.csproj Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Target framework net10.0-windows (Revit 2026.5 and later, Revit 2027) References WPF, DBTools.HandyControl; Helix, Serilog and the logging and DI abstractions are merged in Contents Presentation holds only types that must live for the whole process: theme dictionaries, resource keys, styles, converters and pack resources; controls whose code-behind is limited to binding, dependency-property, routed-event, input and lifecycle mechanics; the ModalWindow and ModelessWindow base types with their owner-handle contracts, and the modal and modeless ToolWindowSession shells; tool-specific behaviors, converters and controls under Tools/<TOOL>/; the structural 3D viewport (see Structural Preview). Production source is under src/DBTools.Presentation, with namespaces DBTools.Presentation.* that follow the folder tree. The project also compiles four tool settings views linked from their tool folders; these keep their tool namespaces and do not make Presentation depend on the tool assemblies. Presentation does not reference DBTools.dll, Core, tool types, view models, commands, services or the Revit API. App, Core and the tools may reference Presentation. ColorPickerPopup exposes and binds dependency properties by property path, and popup dismissal updates the stable IsPopupOpen property. ProgressOverlayControl binds to the command that the host supplies. Tool windows Tool views are raw embedded XAML. ToolWindowHost creates a modal or modeless shell, parses the view inside ToolWindowReflectionScope and sets the tool's view model. Core's ToolWindowFactory runs WindowInitializer on the shell first, which installs owner, theme, progress and error handling, and then registers the session. Hosts call session.ShowDialog() or session.Show() and get named controls with session.Require<T>(name). When a session closes or is retired, Presentation tears down bindings, automation roots, resources and callbacks. See Theme System. UI Automation item lifetime Retirement does not clear cached automation peers. In WPF 10.0.0, item peers hold reference-type rows weakly (ItemAutomationPeer._item uses ItemWeakReference, and DataGridCellItemAutomationPeer._item is weak), and teardown cuts the strong column, row-item and DataContext references. ToolWindowCollectibleReleaseTests (Windows Pure) and ToolWindowHostReleaseTests (Revit), both through ToolWindowHostReleaseHarness, drive DataGrid, ListBox and TreeView with a real UI Automation client, retire without pumping messages, and check that every tool item, type and the collectible context can be released. Rows are held strongly, and a collectible tool assembly stays loaded, in these cases: the first item cached by a peer store has an unreliable hash code (for example ComponentResourceKey); the store switches to list mode and holds every later key strongly; the items are boxed value types; the ItemAutomationPeerKeepsItsItemAlive switch makes _item strong; a UI Automation client holds an item element, which keeps its control alive through ElementProxy._peer. Enumerating ItemPeersStorage or _WeakRefElementProxyStorage materializes the weak keys, so their contents do not show an owning reference. Resource URIs /DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Theme.xaml Raw and reloadable XAML declares stable namespaces with assembly=DBTools.Presentation. XAML compiled inside Presentation uses the form without assembly=. See Theme System for URI rules and Assembly Loading Contract for the distribution layout.

developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.title: DBTools.Sandbox | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.summary: DBTools.Sandbox DBTools.Sandbox is a standalone executable that validates one product year and hosts tool windows for UI development without Revit. It targets net10.0-windows for Revit 2026.5 and later and for Revit 2027; build/Distribution/RevitYearContract.cs defines the supported years. Source layout Path Contents App/Startup/ SandboxEntry (BCL-only entry point), CLIOptions, SandboxCandidate, the SandboxMode enum (Interactive, Headless) App/ The WPF application Composition/ Sandbox runtime services and SandboxWindowFactory Features/WindowCatalog/ The window catalog shown in interactive mode Runtime/ Sandbox logging and window runtime configuration Validation/ Candidate, manifest, metadata and window validators Tests/ DBTools.Sandbox.Pure.Tests Runtime Sandbox starts a new default-context process for each candidate year. The entry point checks the year directory before any Core, Presentation or WPF type loads, loads the candidate's top-level assemblies and Tools/ assemblies from their paths, and then starts WPF. The candidate files are the only product assemblies in the process; the project compiles against Core, Presentation and HandyControl without copying their runtime files. Sandbox reads window specifications from the tool manifests through Core's SandboxCatalog and hosts them in the stable Presentation window shells. At startup it calls DBTools.Core.Sandbox.SandboxMode.Activate, so SandboxMode.IsActive is true in this process; tool code checks it to avoid Revit-only services. Building real windows and checking their cleanup requires the Windows process. For the options, the validation steps and the manifest rules, see Sandbox Validator. See also Sandbox Integration and Assembly Loading Contract.

developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.summary: Elevation Tags Elevation Tags aligns spot elevation text relative to leader endpoints in floor, structural, and ceiling plans. Manual alignment runs on the active view. Automatic alignment runs when a supported view activates. Use and settings Open a FloorPlan, EngineeringPlan, or CeilingPlan view. Configure Elevation Tags in Settings. Run Align Elevation Tags, or enable automatic updates. The command requires an active view. An unsupported view produces a warning toast without running alignment. The settings preview redraws as per-type offsets change. Settings use configuration section Tools.ElevationTags and pack key common.elevation_tags. Property Default Meaning AutoUpdateEnabled true Run on supported view activation TagNamePatterns Empty list Regex patterns. An empty or all-blank list uses the static defaults TypeOffsets Empty dictionary TypeAlignmentOffsets keyed by spot elevation type name The default pattern is: ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$ The UI permits up to three patterns and validates their syntax. At least one nonblank pattern is required to save settings. Runtime compiles nonblank patterns case-insensitively. Invalid patterns log warnings and are skipped. With no valid compiled patterns, no tags match. TypeAlignmentOffsets contains AlongLeaderOffset and PerpendicularOffset. Both default to zero for an unconfigured type. Runtime multiplies these values by view.Scale / 12. The signs follow the computed text side relative to the leader endpoint. Filtering AutoUpdater collects non-type OST_SpotElevations elements from the active view as SpotDimension instances. A match against any configured regex includes the spot. Candidate strings include the spot name, spot type and family names, and resolved marker-symbol type and family names. The matcher tests these strings separately. A failure reading a spot's names increments FailedCount. The first such failure in a run logs its exception. Leaderless spots, missing types, and Relative-base spots require no update. Alignment algorithm Read the origin, leader end, current text position, and spot type. Resolve elevation and format its text using document units and the type's unit options. Measure the text with GDI+ using font, text size, width scale, and display DPI. Compute placement relative to the leader end and current above/below text side. Apply the configured per-type offsets. Write TextPosition when X or Y differs after rounding to two decimal places in internal coordinates. Z remains the existing text Z. The view factor is view.Scale / 12. The measured horizontal half-width receives margins of 2 * factor / 128 + factor / 8. The vertical margin is factor / 64. Placement below the leader also accounts for measured text height. The elevation base uses the type's displayed SPOT_ELEV_BASE value: Display value Calculation Project Base Point Subtract project base point Z only when project and survey point positions differ by at least 1e-9 on an axis Relative Skip alignment Other values, including Survey Point Use spot origin Z These comparisons use English display strings with ordinal matching. An Elevation Indicator becomes the prefix only when Elevation Indicator as Prefix/Suffix equals Prefix and the indicator is nonblank. Otherwise the measured prefix is EL. . The calculation does not append a configured suffix. Font defaults to Arial and width scale defaults to 1 when their parameters are absent. A units-format lookup failure logs once and uses default formatting. Results and errors AutoUpdater.Run() returns ElevationTagRunResult with: Field Meaning TotalSpotsInView Collected spots PatternMatches Spots accepted by name patterns UpdatedCount Spots whose position changed FailedCount Name-reading or per-spot update failures Candidate updates share DB Tools - Autoupdating spot elevations. The updater catches per-spot update faults, counts them, and continues. The first update fault logs its exception. Collection, layout preparation, and transaction-level failures can propagate. The manual workflow shows a Warning toast when failures exist, Success when tags change, and Info for no spots, no pattern matches, or matching spots requiring no changes. The last case includes already aligned, leaderless, and Relative-base spots. Counts do not distinguish those cases. Automatic updates log a summary warning for partial failures. Uncaught automatic-update failures reach Core's view-activation handling, which shows a runtime-failure banner and skips that task for the document session. This runtime failure does not set a persistent settings warning. Warning core.structural.elevation_tags disables DBTools.AlignElevationTagsInView and automatic updates. The settings context exposes the warning state and disables its automatic-update toggle while the warning is active. Ownership and registration Source: src/Tools/Structural/ElevationTags/. The manifest places the tool on the Common panel. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/ElevationTagsCommand Ribbon entry point and active-view availability App/Composition/ElevationTagsToolModule Settings and pack registration App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions Feature registration App/Composition/SettingsPackContextFactory Settings context and live type snapshots Features/AlignElevationTagsWorkflow Manual validation and completion toasts Features/ViewActivatedTask Supported-view automatic execution Features/ElevationTagsUpdater Shared inline call gate, transaction runner, and updater construction Features/AutoUpdater Filtering, layout, mutation, and counts Features/SpotElevationSymbolResolver Spot marker-symbol resolution Features/SpotElevationTypeProjector Live type snapshots for settings Settings/SettingsPackContext Pattern, type, and preview wiring and validation Settings/PatternContext Core RegexPatternListContext adapter Settings/TypeContext, TypeSelection Type filtering, navigation, and offsets Settings/PreviewContext Preview formatting and image state Settings/Views/ElevationTagsSettingsPackView.xaml Settings layout The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.ElevationTags. The module type is DBTools.ElevationTags.App.Composition.ElevationTagsToolModule. Command and availability both use DBTools.ElevationTags.App.Composition.ElevationTagsCommand. The button uses InlineUi, icon key align_elevation_tags, and order 20. The icon asset is Assets/align_elevation_tags_icon.png. Troubleshooting and tests Symptom Check No matches Compare patterns with spot, type, family, and marker-symbol names Automatic updates absent Check the toggle, warning state, supported view type, and runtime log Matching spots unchanged Check leader presence, elevation base, and rounded position Partial alignment Inspect the first filtering or update exception in the DBTools log Pure tests cover the runner, symbol resolution, settings state, preview, and manual summaries. Hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover the command, module, workflow, view activation, live updater, and type projection. See architecture and themes.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.title: Global Mapper architecture specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.summary: Global Mapper architecture specification Global Mapper (GM) collects Revit content, builds mapping intent, and executes reviewed replacement plans. This specification describes its state, execution, persistence, and lifetime contracts. Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. GM describes entry points and test surfaces. Composition and document scope App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory captures the launch UIDocument and Document, creates a QueuedModeless App run scope, and binds its concrete GmSessionDocumentGate once before resolving modeless work. The gate compares ordinal DocumentSessionKey values on each callback. The key uses the document hash code for session scoping. It does not guarantee collision-free identity. The persistence key is the nonblank document path, or that captured session key for an unsaved document. Unsaved documents do not load legacy title-keyed data. AddGm() registers the concrete GM gate without replacing shared IRevitCallGate registrations. GM Revit readers, writers, family batches, transaction runners, and Commit Review consume the concrete gate. RevitMappingPlanExecutor rejects an invalid document or session-key mismatch before writers begin. RunCleanupAsync uses the underlying gate with CancellationToken.None so owned documents can close after authority or work cancellation ends. Commit Review uses the bound parent gate to create an InlineUi child scope. It binds the child gate once to the expected document before running apply services. One outer Revit callback contains planning, modal review, apply, finalization, and refresh. During that modal session, forced-queue, off-thread, or second-callback work is refused. AppSessionProjectionBuilder receives a host-neutral MappingProjectionContext, workspace/dialog state, a required IViewOps implementation, and feature services. The runtime wraps that same projection in MappingExecutionContext with its ExpectedDocument. The bound gate carries the session authorization key. Host-neutral panes and rows receive the projection context. Commit Review receives the execution context. Authorization identity and persistence identity have separate consumers. WindowSessionServices supplies the attached owner and progress overlay. ErrorNotifierFactory uses that owner. GmWindowAttachment supplies feature dialogs with a late-bound getter for the attached window. Design-time composition uses explicit host-neutral collaborators, including DesignTimeViewOps. AppSessionBuilder constructs startup, initialization, Deep Scan, preference clearing, background prewarm, Family Mapping commands, pane lifecycle, and disposal workflows. RowRefreshFactory builds one row collaboration graph per session. Its outputs include CrossPaneRowRefresh, RowRefreshCoreServices, CommitReviewRowServices, UIStateFactory, and OptionRenderingRefresh. App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences Usage rows, Family Mapping refresh, selected-family state, indicators, live-update suppression, row locks, and workspace events. It implements feature-owned ICommitReviewRowRefresh, IFamilyMappingCrossPaneCommands, and IDeepScanUsageRefresh. FilterRefreshWorkflow, StartupRowWorkflow, and PageActivationWorkflow consume that runtime. App/Sessions owns session records and runtime lifetime. Composition owns construction. Feature implementations do not import DBTools.GM.App. FamilyMappingFactory returns FamilyMappingViewModel, FamilyMappingScanWorkflow, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, FamilyMappingTypeCreation, and one MappingRowSet spanning family/type and supplied Usage rows. FamilyMappingScanStateApplier belongs to scan sequencing. The row builders and refresh owners receive the same row set. Session operations and shutdown Domain/SessionOperation/ISessionOperationGate exposes serialized work, overlay progress, busy state, and UI cancellation. App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate implements admission and cancel-and-drain. MappingUpdateSuppression separately controls nested live-plan suppression. SessionOperationProgress carries operation progress or the Hidden no-display value. The Domain/Workspace IWorkspaceSignals port carries feature requests for whole-window refresh. App/Sessions/WorkspaceSignals implements that port, alongside WorkspaceState implementing IWorkspaceState. An operation failure remains primary. Caller cancellation propagated through the linked work token is translated back to the caller token. Teardown independently attempts stopped-step logging, busy-state reset, and busy-text reset. The resets run directly or in one dispatcher call. An aborted or unscheduled dispatcher call produces one teardown failure. The linked cancellation source is always released. One failure propagates unchanged. Multiple failures aggregate in primary-first order with contextual teardown wrappers. A failing StateChanged subscriber cannot hide the work failure or skip the other reset. BackgroundPrewarm and OptionRenderingRefresh retain their transitive task and cancellation source. Replacement cancels and drains the active pair before starting the next. The session refuses ordinary close while Commit Review or Type Mapping owns an interaction. The first admitted close publishes closing state, cancels Mapping/startup, observes startup, and retains one terminal shutdown task. Repeated closes join that completion. The shutdown workflow independently attempts prewarm drain, option-rendering drain, confirmed preference-clear drain, session-operation cancel-and-drain, close persistence, and synchronous graph disposal, in that order. It then issues one terminal Close. Closed performs idempotent view-model cleanup and App run-scope disposal. Failures retain lifecycle order and do not skip later cleanup. Pane and scope collaborators remain alive until running work drains. Dev Mode retirement is synchronous and requires Idle for immediate collection. Commit Review reports Busy, so reload waits for Keep, Roll back, X, or cancellation followed by close. Revit shutdown can force ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll. Retirement diagnoses pending work, aborts owned dispatcher operations, cancels without draining, rolls back an open apply group through the inline commit gate, disposes child/session scopes, and skips close persistence with a log entry. It opens no dispatcher frame. An existing normal-close task stops before its next stage when retirement takes over. DevModeStatus exposes Idle or Busy: <operations> in the root UI Automation ItemStatus. It includes name lookup, navigation, both auto-zoom debounces, duplicate rebuilds, Type Mapping, Commit Review, cache posts, and pending page selection. App, Family Mapping, and Shared Parameters navigation use Mapping-owned NavigationLifetime leases. Leases start inside admitted callbacks or around awaited execution. Both feature auto-zoom debounces use 200 ms and the lease token. Disposal cancels outside the lifetime lock and prevents later selection, activation, or zoom. Core alerts use observed nested modal loops and diagnose reload during a dialog. Domain and feature contracts Project state Domain/ProjectState owns ProjectState, family/type records, reference index/values, project parameters, scan state, projection, and the scoped ProjectStateStore. The store imports no feature or App namespace. CurrentProjectState and CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identify the loaded snapshot and its category in one replacement operation. IProjectStateBuilder and ProjectStateBuildRequest are inward contracts. App/State/ProjectStateBuilder queries Families, Usage, Shared Parameters, and Previews and projects their results into those values. Family-only refresh retains loaded Usage and Shared Parameters sections and invalidates derived usage caches before preparing rows. A failed build preserves published state. Commit Review planning builds the selected category plus pending-intent owner families without publishing. CarryForwardInto supplies loaded sections and unchanged-family Deep Scan evidence to that planning state. Duplicate detection also stays unpublished. CarryDeepScanEvidenceInto supplies only unchanged-family evidence to its fresh full state. The ProjectStateStore retains evidence across category-filtered state replacement. A rebuild restores it only when the family's type set and per-type instance counts remain unchanged. After commit, ReplaceProjectStateAfterCommit discards directly changed families and containing ancestors across all categories. Direct changes include mapped/owning families, families of mapped types, and material/object-style families found by AffectedFamilyResolver. Commit Review planning uses that same resolver. Its plan context owns planning identity and evidence. Discarding evidence removes scan state, type payloads, DeepScanResults, and fast parameter discovery together. Element names and categories Domain/ElementNames owns IElementNameQuery, ElementNamesCache, and ElementNameLookupKind. Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQuery implements the Revit adapter. App registers it with state/cache wiring. Categories registers curated-category services. Strict name loading requires a nonblank cached name for every requested ID. Blank entries are queried again. Omitted/blank provider values stay unresolved. GetResolvedFamilyName prefers cache, then project-state family name, and throws if neither exists. Display getters retain explicit ID/unavailable-name fallbacks. WorkspaceState.SelectedCategory is the single typed CategoryOption value exposed by IWorkspaceState. CategoryFilter derives its display label. Null and Id zero select every family. Other signed IDs select exactly that category, including negative built-in Revit IDs. Both IFamilyQuery methods use those rules. GetFamiliesAsync reuses state only when category identity matches, families exist, and all family names are nonblank. It still filters the reused result by the requested category. WorkspaceState.SortMode uses MatchingOptionSortMode through mutation, persistence, restoration, and option projection. CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identifies loaded state. FamilyMappingState.AppliedCategoryId identifies applied rows. Applying a different category resets category-scoped rows before application and records the category only after rows apply. Cancellation between state publication and row application therefore causes a reset on retry. Mapping intent, rows, and conflicts Features/Mapping/Domain owns immutable intent, conflict, operation, plan, and host-free execution values. It does not import mutable Rows types. MappingIntentKey validates its nine-field shape through named factories and FromPersisted. It rejects invalid zero identities while retaining signed category IDs such as -2000011. The Rows package owns row-to-intent translation, projection, origin mutation, and family-apply behavior. Conflict/Rows owns row conflict matching. Detection consumes an immutable MappingSelectionSnapshot. MappingConflictWorkflow hydrates returned MappingIntentKey values into loaded rows. MappingConflictTarget defines three closed variants: a positive element selection, a type-parameter policy, or a display-only message. Resolution chooses an original side or an explicit MappingConflictBulkAction. Display labels and sentinel IDs do not encode executable policy. Duplicates implements Mapping-owned neutral selection/resolution contracts without exporting its own selection types. Mapping owns projection/execution contexts, row signals, navigation values/lifetimes, MappingUpdateSuppression, and OriginClearSuppression. Mapping Domain/Planning owns nested-family, style, and type-reference plan language. Commit Review's CommitReviewDocumentEditBuilder owns mutable family-batch assembly. Mapping's neutral composition registers MappingPlanVerifier and MappingIntentStore. Revit/Composition registers mutation adapters, attached by App's AddGm root. Shared Parameters implements Mapping's focused embed port and uses Mapping operation identities. Domain/Parameters/FamilyParameterDiscoveryResult carries normalized ScopedParameterName values, complete/partial state, and contextual read errors.
