Family Mapping and Shared Parameters publish choices only from complete discovery. Duplicate parameter scoring requires complete discovery on both sides. Instance/Type suffixes are display labels. Parameter mappings retain scope and require equal source/target scope. Element identities Revit family, type, instance, material, style, view, and category IDs use long. Revit boundaries use ElementIdConverter.ToLong and FromLong. Saved-mapping and UI-state JSON retain their property names and accept older integer-valued number tokens. Family-document materials resolve by name rather than host numeric ID. Int remains appropriate for counts, indexes, depths, enum/order casts, synthetic duplicate group IDs, SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher sequence IDs, and MappingOption.StableStringId hashes. SharedParameterValueCopier rejects Map From values outside Int32 for Revit Integer storage. ElementId parameter destinations parse Map From text as long. Persistence and saved mappings Domain/Cache owns tool-wide cache paths, metadata, and recovery policy. App/Persistence owns document UI-state storage and session persistence sequencing. StatePersistence requires both IUIStateCache and ISavedMappingStore in production. Design-time projection does not construct unused persistence. JSON writes flush a unique sibling temporary file and publish it atomically. Cancellation or I/O failure preserves the last good snapshot. Only confirmed missing files/directories count as absent. Access, sharing, invalid-path, and other I/O faults propagate. UI-state and Deep Scan snapshots are disposable caches: malformed, invalid, or old snapshots are discarded and logged. Saved mappings are user data and use strict nullable-ingress validation with contextual failures. Cache results are immutable hit/miss values. Hits always contain data. IUIStateCache serializes asynchronous writes and clears across scoped instances with a process-wide mutation gate. StatePersistence serializes document loads, clears, and saves and tracks separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. An older open session cannot restore either snapshot after another window clears it. A freshly loaded window can persist new state. UIStateLifecycle attempts enabled close writes independently, retains failures in write order, and resets one-shot suppression even on failure. Confirmed clears drain before close persistence and disposal. PaneStateProjector supplies SavedAt. Saving preserves the supplied timestamp. Saved Mappings validates exact document identity and every persisted key before admission. Parameter mappings retain ScopedParameterName scope. The persistence port exposes load, save, and clear. MappingIntentStore owns merging. Commit Review constructs the restore workflow, merges persisted intent, and reapplies through row owners. Clearing saved mappings follows this order: Remove saved origins/selections from loaded rows. Clear mapping intent, duplicate intent, and the in-memory persisted list. Clear storage. Run the required App-bound refreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear operation. CrossPaneRowRefresh rebuilds loaded Usage rows, refreshes Family Mapping rows, reconciles indicators under suppression, releases suppression, refreshes locks, and publishes cache status. Reapply calls Usage, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, Shared Parameters, and row locks directly. Option cache and similarity MappingOptionCache keys candidates by mapping kind, source ID, category, ordered target ID/name pairs, and source label. Category lookup does not fall back to general entries. Prewarm uses the same identity. Candidate snapshots use private read-only lists, so replacing entries cannot mutate earlier results. NamingSimilarity.Normalize and numeric-suffix stem comparison retain letters/digits in invariant lowercase. Numeric-suffix siblings with equal cleaned stems score 1.0 before Dice evaluation. Dice uses lowercased raw-name bigrams, including punctuation and whitespace, with multiplicities. Its score is twice the multiset intersection divided by the sum of raw lengths minus two. For a raw length below two, equal raw lengths score 1.0 only with equal nonempty cleaned stems. Other short-name pairs score zero. Each scoring pass owns its immutable name-profile cache. Deep Scan Deep Scan owns family scans, projection, usage resolution, feature cache, and refresh workflow. A user scan collects a complete family batch and finishes cache preparation before one validated ApplyBatch admission. Usage refresh data is prepared before completed scan state publishes. Cancellation or required failure before admission preserves the prior projection. Host lookup completeness is separate for styles, materials, and families. An item failure marks only its domain incomplete and prevents partial singleton-name resolution or resolver-cache reuse. Other complete requested domains remain usable. Affected families retain warning diagnostics and incomplete usage. Unexpected collector/category traversal failures abort construction. Partial parameter discovery invalidates fast choices, is omitted from duplicate scoring, and removes prior reusable cache entries before admission. A later complete query can repopulate choices. Partial usage remains visible but cannot become reusable complete cache data. DeepScanCacheCoordinator removes prior reusable entries for incomplete parameter discovery or usage scans before admission. Failure to resolve a removal identity or remove an entry propagates and prevents admission. A cache write failure without required removals logs a warning. Cache operations use a local persistence gate plus an exclusive per-file process lock. Each batch reloads authoritative disk state once while holding both. Startup hydration reads eligible families against one load. User scan removes/writes its family batch with one load and one atomic save. This serializes owners across Revit processes. Disposal drains persistence before releasing the DI-root owner. Snapshot admission validates entries and parameter/usage completeness flags as a whole. It discards incompatible snapshots rather than salvaging entries. Clear Cache holds a session-lifetime registration through deletion, projection/UI refresh, and completion. It shares session-operation admission with scans. Shutdown drains it before disposing collaborators. A confirmed clear increments DeepScanOrchestrator's generation after disk deletion and before projection clearing. Hydration rejects its whole candidate batch if that generation changes or the captured ProjectState reference changes during reading. It never replaces an already completed family scan. CrossPaneRowRefresh implements IDeepScanUsageRefresh: apply Usage data, rebuild loaded rows when needed, reconcile Family Mapping state/indicators under suppression, then refresh locks. DeepScanRefreshWorkflow invalidates options and awaits the App-bound Shared Parameters authoring rebuild. That rebuild evicts authoring snapshots and rebuilds the loaded tree with pending intent and selection. Completion events describe changed cache state and publish even when rebuilding faults or cancels. The outcome then propagates to the operation boundary. Eligible-cache hydration finishes only after its queued UI refresh runs. AuthoringRebuildWorkflow serializes rebuild and application. If evidence invalidates during a build, including the first build, it builds again before applying. Disposal cancels held/queued rebuilds and prevents later application. Duplicates The Duplicates feature owns detection, selections, rows, resolution, tree, pane state, and type mapping. Detection/DuplicateDetectionEngine calls the family, style, material, and shared-parameter matchers, assigns aggregate group IDs, and returns DuplicateDetectionResult. The feature's Domain, Selection, Rows, Resolution, Tree, Pane, and TypeMapping folders own their respective contracts and behavior. SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher lives beside family/style/material matchers under Detection/Matching. CurrentDuplicateDetection owns the last fully completed artifact. Detection collects its unpublished full state, executes stable DuplicateKind stages, hydrates names, then publishes and returns the same artifact reference. Earlier failure/cancellation preserves the prior artifact. Family-row counts use that same detection state. The immediate rebuild receives the artifact explicitly. Other readers inject CurrentDuplicateDetection. Cached refresh waits for cross-dispatcher rebuilds. A reentrant request replaces the queued request. The outer refresh runs the latest queued rebuild before returning, including propagating its failure. PreviewDuplicateMatcher matches style/material candidates only when both resolve to the same signature. Unavailable previews never match, including each other. Duplicates imports neither Shared Parameters nor Commit Review. Families and Family Mapping Families' neutral composition registers FamilyQuery and IFamilyQuery. Its Revit composition registers FamilyDocumentService, FamilyScanner, and scanner ports. FamilyDocumentService owns document lifecycle/query, not Mapping material preparation. Families consumes its own IFamilyInstanceCountQuery, implemented by Usage's live source. A thrown Document.Close or false result is a cleanup failure under the shared strict close policy. FamilyMappingViewModel owns binding state and interactions. FamilyMappingScanWorkflow owns asynchronous scan/cache/post-commit sequencing and its private scan-state applier. FamilyMappingRowRefresh owns symbol projection, row build/refresh, saved-mapping reapply, and usage reconciliation. Ordinary category navigation reuses a category snapshot or matching loaded state. RescanFamiliesAfterCommitAsync discards every category snapshot and rebuilds from the document, including when category identity stays unchanged, so newly created types reach rows. Cross-pane sequences remain in App's CrossPaneRowRefresh. Usage Usage owns indexing, matching/options, preview cache/versioning, rows, selection, traversal, and pane state. AppSessionProjectionBuilder constructs one UsageIndexLoader and FamilyUsage after session state, names, and operation gate exist. The loader retains those collaborators. It is not a context-free service. RebuildPlanningUsageIfNeededAsync returns Task and builds only a missing index when usage intent exists. RebuildUsageAfterCommitIfNeededAsync returns true only when it builds the index. UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder starts and drains five catalog/index tasks, aggregates non-cancellation faults, and creates an unpublished candidate without touching the match index. Name resolution, project-state usage storage, and Deep Scan refresh preparation precede publication. Index publication aligns the match index, target universe, hydration generation, and option cache. UsageMatchIndex shares one in-flight family hydration among concurrent callers. An index publication invalidates hydration started against the prior generation. UsageIndexPublished runs synchronously on the publishing thread, including workers. RowRefreshPublicationWiring dispatches row projection to the UI thread. Rows track publication version. Detect suppresses publication-driven duplicate rebuild and rebuilds once after scanning, retaining the keep target. Passive option projection suppresses intent capture. An unavailable saved target remains disabled for review. An explicit edit can clear or replace it. UsageViewModel owns target selection and bound collection/preview mutation. Selection-family flow performs one family lookup, name hydration, and row population. UsagePreviewService owns calculation, caching, and request-version order. UsageWorkflow consumes IUsageIndexLoader and its own rows without App/Family Mapping imports or row locks. App PageActivationWorkflow suppresses live-plan updates across loading, reconciliation, and indicators, then refreshes locks and cache state after suppression. Shared Parameters and UI execution Shared Parameters owns domain values, authoring, formulas, Revit adapters, rows, tree, views, and pane state. SharedParameterDuplicateReconciler owns stateful duplicate-row mutation and reentrancy. SharedParameterConflictProjector performs stateless tree/Commit Review projection. Map From reads numeric formula inputs at the Revit boundary. The preview evaluator does not parse displayed parameter text. Measured values use Revit's display unit. Preview output uses 15 significant digits. Numeric preview accepts signed/unsigned E/e exponents, including substituted invariant G15 values. Unresolved identifiers/functions produce preview-unavailable. Revit still validates authored formulas. Formula mode returns zero from the value copier without target resolution or writes. The embed applier counts authored formulas separately from value updates: one formula has authored=1, updated=0, affected=1. MapFrom retains copied-value counts. Detached Usage selection-preview and authoring property notifications use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync. The shared boundary owns logging/banners without rethrowing into WPF dispatch. Shared-parameter group/category/authoring work and contested overlay admission retain the UI context before collection mutation. Preview failures propagate to their owning command/tree-selection boundary for one report. Commit Review planning and continuation Commit Review planning resolves names, builds planning state, loads parameter groups, and prepares rows/usage inside one ISessionOperationGate operation. Collaborators do not reacquire that non-reentrant gate. The gate releases before the review dialog opens. Refresh takes a separate operation. Planning cancellation remains control flow. Other faults can produce invalid-plan state. Commit Review receives closing state and MappingSessionContext with IWorkspaceState rather than mutable App state. Planning/DocumentEdit owns mutable batch assembly. Report/OperationRows/OperationRowProjector produces family, pending, result, and error rows. Workflow owns apply/finalization. Revit/CommitReviewSessionFactory composes the child scope, planning, transaction groups, and modal presenter through the bound document gate. CommitReviewRowServices is feature-owned and constructed by App's row composition. Commit continuation uses ICommitReviewRowRefresh, implemented by CrossPaneRowRefresh. It returns Refreshed, Canceled, or NoSelectedCategory. Only a successful family scan proceeds to usage preparation, family reconciliation, and row locks. Canceled stops through cancellation. NoSelectedCategory skips refresh without a success log. Committed mappings remain persisted in either case. The refresh workflow consumes ISessionOperationGate for busy state. Commit-and-continue invalidates authoring snapshots, duplicates, and cached family views before rescanning. Returned outcomes rebuild the applied Shared Parameters tree. A successful continuation rescans Duplicates immediately when that page is active. View operations and catalogs ViewOps owns navigation. A positive missing element ID returns false without changing view or selection. Nonpositive IDs are argument errors. Unexpected Revit faults propagate. Previews owns cross-feature material/style catalogs and preview values. Mapping execution RevitMappingPlanExecutor validates document identity and supplies document operations to MappingPlanExecutor. Production apply and Pure tests use the same stage loop, capture boundaries, and result builder. Result accounting The MappingApplyResult constructor validates and snapshots recorded operation results. Succeeded operations require positive affected counts. Skips require zero. Failed operations can retain counts for writes completed before failure. Root succeeded/failed/skipped and affected totals derive from one recorded-result snapshot. Caller collections cannot mutate the completed result. Family success requires changed work and a successful reload. Failed-rule totals and fatal operation diagnostics must agree. Exception-backed diagnostics retain the original exception internally. MappingApplyResultBuilder logs each exception reference once with operation context. Commit Review receives stable operation text, codes, IDs, and family context. Exception types, messages, and stacks stay in logs. Writer exceptions are attributed to every unrecorded operation owned by that writer. Family cleanup always attempts close and retains close diagnostics after primary errors. Cancellation plus cleanup failures propagate primary-first through family-batch and outer writer containment. Skipped group-owned references produce Mapping warnings. An Edit Group restriction rejecting a line-style transaction at commit fails that pair. Successful sibling results retain their affected counts, but Commit Review rolls back an attempt with fatal mapping diagnostics. Writer failures A writer exception after all owned operations are recorded is a workflow failure. The result builder logs writer/stage context once and rethrows the original exception with its stack. Recorded operations alone cannot produce a successful final result in this case. With unrecorded owned operations, the executor records their failures and continues to later writers. Population capture Replacement capture precedes the first mutation that can change its population. ApplyContext captures the original symbol populations, target occupancy and type-parameter source values before the writer loop. Host material references are captured at the fixed boundary after Host recreation and before Nested Families or Type Replacements, including plans with no Host operations. They refer to recreated element IDs without consuming values introduced by later type-parameter migration or family reloads. Each family document captures all applicable material, object-style and nested-symbol references before its operation loop. Missing sources are explicit capture results. An absent source in a traversed family is zero work with a non-fatal reason. A missing host source or an ambiguous family material name remains an error. Apply never discovers an incoming population. Family material capture includes writable type parameters and the per-type defaults of instance material parameters. Revit does not allow formulas on Material data type parameters. Formula-determined parameters are outside this material replacement population. Reference kinds are explicit. Blank type names are valid and match ordinally. Capture does not change FamilyManager.CurrentType. Transactional apply restores the captured type. Object-style capture identifies the actual subcategory parameter or boundary curves of each filled region. Family-owned execution uses BatchOperationSet keyed by MappingOperation.OperationId and FamilyBatchResult.ResultsByOperationId. Style and prepared-material payloads use the same IDs. Nested, style, material, and embed dispatch uses canonical operation types and direct appliers. Intermediate counts must be nonnegative, and succeeded plus failed documents cannot exceed attempted. Invalid producer output fails validation. Family document lifetime Family-owned batch execution discovers the complete applicable family tree and captures each original population before applying any family mutation. FamilyBatchDocuments retains one edit document for each family identity through capture, apply, and reload. Discovery spans the whole commit. Its peak open-document count therefore grows with the discovered tree. After discovery, documents with no applicable work in themselves or their descendants are closed before apply. Remaining documents close after their last root-batch use. Final cleanup closes anything left, including after cancellation. Each release closes in reverse open order and reports individual close failures. Discovery logs the peak and retained counts and reports progress per root. Cleanup uses the underlying Revit gate without requiring the launch document to remain active or the work token to remain uncancelled. EditFamily creates independent copies, so no captured element key is carried into a second edit session. Family element references use UniqueId within their retained document plus parameter identity. Family type references use explicit reference kind, family type name, and family parameter name. Built-in parameter identity uses the typed Revit enum without narrowing its underlying 64-bit value. Document-local ElementId values remain diagnostics and population indexes only. Missing keys produce a diagnostic and do not trigger a live rescan. Shared family identity and reload Shared nested families use a name/category identity. Nonshared copies include their embedding path. Discovery opens the project's shared definition when one exists, so a parent's stale embedded copy cannot become the original population for another root. If the same shared family is reached through several roots, applicable operation populations are merged and each normalized operation is applied once. An equivalent alias receives a merged notice. If its representative fails, the alias is reported as failed as well. Conflicting targets for the same source fail preflight. After a nested or root reload, the load allowlist selects FamilySource.Family only for shared identities changed by that target traversal. Unchanged shared children use FamilySource.Project, which preserves the target document's existing child instead of reloading a stale source copy. Parent material capture excludes shared-symbol projections: the child owns those values and only surviving writes count. Before reload, project-owned shared material projections are restored from the target document explicitly. Revit can otherwise propagate those type values even when the shared-family load callback selects Project. Nonshared symbol overrides remain part of the parent population. Family results Family-document success requires both changed work and a successful reload. A failed family traversal or reload marks every operation actually executed in that traversal as failed, including merged aliases. An affected count can show writes made before the failure. The original exception remains attached to the diagnostic for logging and review. Family-document attempt/success/failure counts include every examined root and child document, including zero-work captures. A reload or close failure keeps the completed affected counts and marks the affected document operation results failed. Material projection ownership A parent FamilySymbol's material type value is a projection of the child's authored FamilyType value. When that child has the same planned material operation, the child owns the write and its count. For nonshared children, root-only operations and traversal-depth leaves retain their parent-side references. Shared projections are always child-owned. Missing captured host references produce a nonfatal diagnostic. Line-style verification Line-style query snapshots retain curve IDs and per-source offered intersections, not Revit element wrappers or target sets per curve. A line-style apply performs one fresh discovery sweep, then verifies actual styles by reading the captured IDs. Complete original-source intersections are regrouped under the final source styles. Unexpected population splits or missing curves fail verification for the committed pairs. Their operation results retain the committed affected counts, and the writer returns the errors instead of throwing away those operation results. Commit Review and the subsequent accepted Usage refresh share this result. A rollback does not publish it. CommitReviewLineStyleLifecycle exports it once, and only while the session's query cache still holds the snapshot that was current when post-apply verification succeeded. Explicit Detect and Usage refresh boundaries invalidate prior snapshots. The hosted sweep fixture compares target intersections with an independent Revit API query. Object-style attribution identifies the family returned by LoadFamily, its retained name, and its ownership of original instances. A Detail Items fixture does not establish the same style availability for every Generic Model, annotation, or in-place family. Post-apply verification Commit Review checks operation identity and successful operation results for all replacement kinds, including runtime replacements created by Create Type. Symbol and line-style counts can be checked against incoming populations. Family material and object-style Usage count families while operation results count references. An overlapping successful target is therefore checked through its operation result and writer readback, not by equating those different quantities. Commit Review results and finalization Result Contract Completed Requires MappingApplyResult and derives success from Outcome Canceled Contains neither Mapping result nor failure prose WorkflowFailed Requires a nonblank reason. Can retain a rolled-back Mapping result for diagnostics Warnings can complete successfully and remain committable. Only positive succeeded operations without fatal diagnostics project applied or persistable intent. Verification requires no planned type, host, style, or material source references to remain. Otherwise the verifier's four-field failure summary blocks mapping projection. One Global Mapper: Apply session group stays open through modal review. Apply and Retry Apply execute and verify inside an inner attempt group. Failure or cancellation rolls back the attempt and permits retry. Retry reuses the reviewed plan but constructs a new apply context and rereads the document. Keep + Continue and Keep + Close GM assimilate the session group into one Undo entry before recording mappings. Roll back, X's rollback answer, cancellation, and abnormal exit roll it back. An unknown rollback outcome propagates to the error banner rather than asserting that nothing was kept. Active-view refresh follows successful verification. A refresh warning does not disable Keep. After review closes, RefreshAfterReviewAsync refreshes GM after any admitted attempt, including failed or rolled-back attempts. Type replacements retain their selecting intent key, so acceptance records intent for its actual owner. Apply transactions log each Revit failure at Warning with definition ID and failing elements. Pre-commit issues retain their validation label. Family-document material replacement resolves source and target by material name. Errors retain planned operation ID and host source/target IDs. Family-document material IDs and affected elements are diagnostic details. Report grouping uses the owning operation even when operations share a host pair or family documents assign different IDs. Reloaded family identity Family-owned apply retains the family ID returned by Revit reload. Accepted mappings use that identity, including existing saved and pending mappings for the same family. Rollback leaves mapping identities unchanged. MappingApplyResult.ReloadedFamilyIds snapshots changed root identities. Finalization remaps applied/persistable family keys and targets before merging. MappingIntentStore also remaps existing saved/pending intents, manual family-apply state, and usage links. One replaced identity must not retain a second saved mapping. Host replacement Each host replacement is atomic per instance. Placement and required facing, hand, and point-rotation transfer must finish before source deletion. Ordinary parameter copies use best-effort transfer. A failed replacement becomes an item error only after its subtransaction reports a completed rollback. If rollback throws or reports any other status, the primary and rollback failures escape together so the enclosing transaction aborts instead of committing an uncertain document state. ParameterValueTransfer reads the target after Parameter.Set returns false. It accepts the copy as a no-op only when its storage type and value exactly match the requested source value. It applies no numeric tolerance to Double values. A remaining mismatch becomes a nonfatal HostParameterCopyWarning with the source instance, parameter, and reason. Setter exceptions remain failures. These warnings appear only after the replacement subtransaction commits. A later required-state failure rolls back and retains the fatal replacement error. Commit Review preserves each distinct diagnostic, opens the operation diagnostics section, and reports Completed with Warnings. It counts nonfatal diagnostics. Within each diagnostic-code group, it includes distinct messages in first-seen order. Code groups sort by descending diagnostic count, then by code ignoring case. Host parameter transfer treats a writable instance Phase Created value as instance-owned even when the family symbol exposes the same built-in parameter ID. Generated IfcGUID remains excluded by the type-bound rule. Revit read scheduling GmSessionDocumentGate validates Action callbacks as synchronous before wrapping their launch-document check. It rejects async void before Core can see only the synchronous decorator. Generic results also undergo synchronous-result validation. Independent reads for one action start together and are awaited in original order, so the first read's failure/cancellation remains primary. Startup starts family-category, shared-parameter-category, and parameter-group reads together. Family expansion starts view and parameter-name reads together. Selected-type instance examples are read once through type selection. Core's queued-turn policy determines which waiting calls share a callback. Line-style eligibility The shared line-style query checks the capability required by Revit commit. A grouped curve is restylable only when its group and every enclosing group have exactly one placed instance of their type. Attached detail groups also check their parent model group. Multi-instance groups are excluded before capture with their type name, placed count and Edit Group reason. GM never enters Edit Group mode and never ungroups elements. A style used only by those excluded members has no selectable source targets, even when the style remains available as a target for other sources. The writer captures every pair's population before the first pair mutates the document. Curves with no alternate Lines projection style, no resolvable projection or a non-Lines current style are also excluded. The query retains scalar curve IDs and per-source target intersections for restylable curves. It does not retain Revit wrappers for excluded members, and readback never revisits them. Each successful pair's affected count equals its pre-apply Usage quantity. A defensive group-edit failure at commit rolls back only that pair and surfaces the reason. Public surface and resources GM production payload types default to internal. Manifest activation requires public GmToolModule and GmCommand. Public conflict projection values retain their public binding properties. Dependency objects, converters, selectors, and attached behaviors are stable public Presentation types. The design-time view models are internal with public binding/fragment properties. Sandbox and production consume the same raw resources and fragments. Compiled resource validation checks manifest logical names. Source reference Paths below are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Contract Source Launch and document gate App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory.cs, Revit/Document/GmSessionDocumentGate.cs Session graph App/Composition/Revit/AppSessionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/AppSessionProjectionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/RowRefresh/RowRefreshFactory.cs Modeless lifetime App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSession.cs, App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate.cs State and names Domain/ProjectState/ProjectStateStore.cs, Domain/ElementNames/ElementNamesCache.cs Persistence App/Persistence/StatePersistence.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateLifecycle.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateCache.cs Scan admission Features/DeepScan/DeepScanOrchestrator.cs, Features/DeepScan/Refresh/DeepScanRefreshWorkflow.cs Usage publication Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexLoader.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageMatchIndex.cs Options and similarity Features/Mapping/State/MappingOptionCache.cs, Features/Similarity/Naming/NamingSimilarity.cs Execution Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingPlanExecutor.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingApplyResultBuilder.cs, Features/Mapping/Revit/Execution/Batch/FamilyBatchExecutor.cs Review Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewApplyWorkflow.cs, Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewFinalizer.cs Intent identity Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentKey.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentStore.cs

developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.title: Global Mapper (GM) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper (GM) Global Mapper finds duplicate or related Revit content, captures mapping intent, and previews and applies replacements through Commit Review. Its main window is modeless. Commit Review is modal and keeps a reversible apply group open until the user keeps or rolls back changes. The architecture specification defines state, capture, execution, and lifetime contracts. The user guide describes mapping workflows. Source and registration Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.GM. manifest.yml registers: Surface Value Module DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmToolModule Command and availability DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmCommand Run profile QueuedModeless Ribbon Common panel, Global Mapper, order 30, icon key gm Main raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmWindow.xaml, Modeless Commit Review raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmCommitReviewWindow.xaml, Modal Sandbox uses internal design-time view models with public binding properties: DBTools.GM.App.DesignTime.GmWindowDesignTimeViewModel and DBTools.GM.Features.CommitReview.DesignTime.GmCommitReviewWindowDesignTimeViewModel. CANON governs naming and placement. Generated src/Tools/Common/GM/MAP.md lists current files and manifest values. Regenerate the maps with python3 .agents/work/canon_source_maps.py. Do not hand-edit MAP.md. The pre-push/CI map check rejects stale generated maps. Product builds do not run that check. Ownership Owner Responsibility App/Composition Service registration, session and row graph construction App/Sessions Workspace implementations, attachment, close, shutdown, modeless lifetime App/Startup, App/Navigation Initialization, page activation, prewarm, pending navigation App/Persistence, App/State UI-state sequencing and feature-to-domain state construction Domain Project state, identity, element names, parameters, categories, workspace, cache and operation contracts Features/Categories Curated categories Features/Families Family inventory and document lifecycle Features/FamilyMapping Family/type rows, nested usage, scan, selection, and type creation Features/Mapping Intent, row-to-intent translation, conflicts, plans, and replacement execution Features/CommitReview Review planning, modal workflow, reports, verification, finalization, refresh port Features/DeepScan Family scanning, completeness, cache, hydration, refresh Features/Duplicates Detection, matching, selections, tree, and type mapping Features/Usage Indexing, options, matching, preview, selection, and usage rows Features/SharedParameters Authoring, formulas, parameter operations, rows, and tree Features/Similarity Name scoring and score presentation Features/Previews Material/style catalogs and preview values Features/SavedMappings Strict persistence envelope, clear, and reapply Features/ViewOps View and element navigation Revit Tool-wide document and name adapters Feature packages own their local domain, planning, execution, Revit, views, and workflow where present. App composes cross-feature sequences through feature-owned ports. Features do not import App. WPF presentation GmWindowPresenter loads App/Views/GmWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. Its binding source is App/ViewModels/GmWindowViewModel. Commit Review binds to Features/CommitReview/ViewModels/GmCommitReviewWindowViewModel. The runtime and design-time view models expose raw fragment bytes for six feature panes. Stable GmRawViewConverter parses those fragments. OneTime fragment bindings use the nearest categoryTabs ancestor. The host assigns shell and raw-root DataContext synchronously before the first dispatcher pump, so the first DataBind/layout pass can materialize each pane. OneTime retains it across tab switches. Feature panes bind to their feature view models. Parent commands, category selection, and empty-state labels address the shell DataContext. Stable WPF registrations, controls, converters, selectors, attached behaviors, and shared resources live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/GM/, namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.GM. Each raw view merges Presentation’s Resources/Theme.xaml and references stable dictionaries with versioned ResourceUri values. GmViewResources.xaml owns Mapping and Similarity styles without a second theme merge. Payload views have no code-behind, dependency properties, or implicit payload-type templates. Bindings use INotifyPropertyChanged sources or OneTime for immutable values. Raw templates use string keys with explicit fallbacks. GmViewXaml exposes embedded bytes for raw-XAML tests and hosted views. App Pure reads the GM assembly's fixed logical resources directly. Commit Review owns one Revit callback around planning, ShowDialog, finalization, and refresh. Core WindowOwnerModalityScope disables Revit and other top-level windows through that callback and restores only the windows it disabled. During planning, the GM owner remains available for its overlay and Cancel action. ShowDialog disables that owner while the review dialog is visible. User close returns the session finalization. Forced retirement returns none. IsRetired is true for both outcomes and cannot distinguish them. Keep triggered from WPF Closing queues the final Close because WPF rejects reentrant Close there. Duplicate Type Mapping uses a registered modeless shell owned by GM, with Manual startup and a taskbar entry. Commit Review also retains Manual startup, an explicit finalization decision, and a cleanup close gate. Cleanup requests cancellation, waits for a safe rollback boundary, and propagates cancellation, timeout, or rollback failures. A failed cleanup leaves the review window open. Row refresh and owner closure follow successful cleanup. Design-time shared-parameter composition uses the production feature/projection graph with explicit host replacements, including NoopFamilyParameterQuery. Authoring receives a registered parameter-signature provider. Startup performance Startup logs Information-level elapsed time for five overlay steps. Usage indexing logs each catalog/index source duration and completion state. Failure or cancellation records the interrupted step and elapsed time, including queued Revit-call time. Overlay visibility is not the timing source. Family population counts use one symbol-count sweep. Type IDs retain collector order and cache per project state. View-owned collection discovers owner IDs through a quick filter, then visits eligible owners with instances, retaining Revit view-visibility filtering. Style/material indexing share one capped sample and 25-instance chunks with separate geometry options. Family-dependent styles are visited once per usage build. Each option-building pass owns immutable name profiles and retains numeric-suffix and multiset-bigram scoring. Tests Pure tests mirror App, Domain, and Features owners. Test builders, external fakes, and assertions live in Tests/Support. Project-state and name-cache tests live under Tests/Domain. Duplicate projection tests live under Tests/Features/Duplicates. The root Revit name adapter mirrors its complete path at Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQueryTests.cs. CommitReviewPlanContextTests mirrors Features/CommitReview/Planning. Saved mappings, authoring, and usage matching also mirror their subjects. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSessionTests.cs launches the production session through its queued App run scope and GmWindowViewModelBuilder. It observes the raw view in the stable shell on the dispatcher. Normal-close tests overlap close requests and await shared completion, shutdown, one Closed event, cleanup, and scope disposal. Retirement tests wait for Idle, retire synchronously, and check collection without another dispatcher pump. ForcedRetirement_AfterApply_RollsBackTheOpenGroupAndReturnsWithoutHanging retires after a real apply and checks model restoration and group finalization before child-scope disposal in the same Revit turn. Hosted Commit Review tests use testing/TestSupport/GM/Fakes/HiddenCommitReviewDialogHost in place of ShowDialog to satisfy hidden-desktop window ownership. Its dispatcher frame ends on retirement. IToolWindowSession.Closed does not complete after forced retirement, so awaiting that event would retain the Revit callback until timeout. A 60-second deadline retires a session left open and fails the test. GM Revit-local fixture models, named views, family symbols, line styles, materials, and expected production outcomes are required repository baselines. Missing baselines and false production results fail with the model path and running year. Fixture teardown and transaction-group finalization failures also fail and are aggregated with a primary test failure when both occur. DBTools.GM.Pure.Tests.csproj contains only owner-local fixtures and shared test support, then references the normal desktop DBTools.GM.csproj. The production owner grants the pure assembly internal access. There is no second production-source map in the test project. Revit is compile-only, so a Pure test cannot load a Revit-typed member on the Revit-free Windows runner. Run the supported gates through the repository wrappers: ./build.sh BuildApp ./build.sh BuildTests ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 The Pure project targets net10.0-windows and requires Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App to execute. Linux compilation does not establish Windows test execution. RevitLocal tests run through the daemon fleet.

developer-guide/tools/common/recordset-s.title: Record Set technical specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/recordset-s.summary: Record Set technical specification Record Set builds a package from selected RVT host files and their file-based external references. It copies files, optionally processes DWG Xrefs, and rewrites references in copied RVT files through TransmissionData. The source is src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. Record Set describes application composition and window interactions. Data contracts Features/Domain owns these values: Type Contents SourceFile Read-only Name, Path, LinkType, and nullable 64-bit LinkId. Mutable Discipline, Building, CadHandlingMode, BindType. Manual child list HostModel HostFile and read-only Links collection ExternalReferenceKey NormalizedPath plus typed LinkType PlanOptions Nullable AutoDiscoverCadXrefs and AllowCadRepath PlanContext TargetFolder, SelectedHosts, Options, and computed CommonLinkKeys ExecutionPlan Ordered Items, TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes, Summary, Fingerprint PlanSummary Hosts, UniqueLinks, CopyBytes, PredictedOutputBytes, Items PlanMessage Info, Warning, or Block severity and text SourceFile.CreateHost, CreateDiscoveredLink, and CreateManualCadXref construct source values. Discipline defaults to empty. Building defaults to -. Blank building input normalizes to -. CAD mode defaults to Inherit and bind type defaults to Bind. Destination paths belong to immutable PreviewDestination projections, rather than mutable source-file properties. Enum Values LinkType Rvt = 0, Dwg = 1, Other = 2 CadHandlingMode Inherit = 0, AddXrefs = 1, BindAll = 2 BindType Bind = 0, Insert = 1 ExecutionStatus Ok, Cancelled Inherit resolves to AddXrefs during planning. A null PlanOptions flag follows Core Console availability independently for each preview. The UI initially shows unchecked flags, publishes their effective values after preview, and preserves explicit user choices for the window lifetime. These options are not persisted. Host import and reference reading FileSelectionWorkflow owns OS pickers. HostImporter normalizes picks, rejects existing or repeated hosts, and calls PlanningService.ScanHost with empty discipline and building -. A RevitOperationException or scan warning rejects that host and returns an ordered issue. Owner-token cancellation propagates. The application displays issues and adds only accepted hosts. RevitOperations implements IExternalReferenceReader and ITransmissionWriter. It strips long-path prefixes before passing paths to Revit. Missing TransmissionData or external-reference collections fail with operation and host context. Reference reading uses desired data when IsTransmitted is true and last-saved data otherwise. Library references (PathType.Content, including library-located keynote or assembly-code tables) are omitted. Absolute references retain their stored path. Relative references resolve against the source host folder. For a workshared local, the base is the file-system central folder from BasicFileInfo.CentralPath. Without a usable file-system central path, resolution uses the reference's saved absolute path. A moved package with intact relative structure therefore resolves its own files. The scan creates discovered links using their resolved paths and host metadata. It classifies RVT, DWG, and Other external references. It does not recursively scan linked RVT models. Destination rules PlanningService.BuildContext counts normalized source-path/type occurrences. Keys appearing at least twice become common links. Identity uses the complete normalized path and type, not just a filename. The count includes repeated references within one host. TargetPathRules computes intended paths: File Destination Host with building {target}/{building}/{discipline}/{name} Host without building {target}/{discipline}/{name} Noncommon link with building {target}/{building}/{discipline}/Linked Files/{name} Noncommon link without building {target}/{discipline}/Linked Files/{name} Common link {target}/Common Linked Files/{name} Blank or - building omits that segment. Empty discipline adds no directory segment. The destination allocator compares normalized paths. Reusing the same source/destination needs no extra copy. A different source colliding with a destination receives name (2).ext, then (3), and so on, with a warning. Allocation fails when the counter exceeds 10,000. Mappings and preview projections use the allocated destination. Plan construction and limits Features/Planning/Preview/PreviewPlanBuilder.BuildPlanAsync performs these stages: Find Core Console and resolve nullable CAD flags. Plan hosts and non-CAD links under the file policy. Plan each distinct DWG destination once, using its first occurrence's CAD options. Append Revit repath operations for copied hosts with allowed mappings. Check sources, count bytes, estimate bound output, enforce limits, and compute the fingerprint. Denied hosts or links produce warnings. Missing planned source paths produce Block messages. Directory copies count only policy-allowed files. TotalBytes counts each distinct source/destination copy pair, including repeated copies of one source to different destinations. PlanSummary.UniqueLinks is the number of distinct copy-source paths, including host paths. Hosts is the selected-host count. Items includes directory and message items. Limit Value Result when exceeded PlanningLimits.MaxTotalBytes 80 × 1024³ bytes Block PlanningLimits.MaxTotalItems 10,000 Block PredictedOutputBytes starts at TotalBytes. For Bind All, the estimate adds allowed discovered Xref sizes beyond the copied host DWG size. Estimate failure produces a warning and retains the existing estimate. These are preview limits, not guarantees of final package size. Plan items and progress Plan items are typed records. PlanAction supplies their dispatch identity. Record Data Fingerprint action Fingerprint keys Weight FsCreateDirItem Path fs_create_dir path 1 FsCopyItem Source, Destination fs_copy src, dst 3 CadCopyItem Source, Destination cad_copy src, dst 3 CadRepathItem Host, NewRoot cad_repath host, new_root 2 CadBindAllItem Host, BindType cad_bind_all host, bindtype as invariant numeric enum text 4 RevitRepathItem Host, SourceHost, Mapping revit_repath host, source_host, map:{source} per mapping 2 UIWarnItem Message ui_warn msg 0 UIInfoItem Message ui_info msg 0 Progress increases after an item completes, using its weight divided by the total weight, with a minimum denominator of 1. It is an operation estimate, not byte progress. Each item emits an action string and ordinally sorted key=value fields separated by |. Revit mappings use map:{source} keys. Fingerprinting hashes successive UTF-8 item segments with SHA-256, without an extra separator between segments, and keeps the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It records plan identity for the audit output. Execution does not use it as a content checksum. CAD planning For AddXrefs, the planner copies the DWG and allowed manual Xrefs beside it. With discovery enabled and Core Console available, it scans the tree and copies unique referenced paths beside the destination DWG, allocating collision suffixes when necessary. When repath is enabled, it appends CadRepathItem using the destination DWG directory as NewRoot. Discovery failure logs a warning and uses heuristic copying. Disabled discovery or unavailable Core Console also uses heuristic copying: copy existing sibling directories named xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg, or cad. Each source/destination directory pair is copied once. This path does not rewrite Xrefs and can leave broken references. The planner emits Info messages Auto-discover CAD Xrefs disabled. when discovery is disabled with Core Console present, or AutoCAD Core Console not found. DWG Xrefs copied by heuristic only. when Core Console is absent. Explicitly enabling both discovery and repath without Core Console produces Block. BindAll requires Core Console. Without it, preview produces Block and schedules no bind operation. With it, the plan copies the DWG and appends bind work, without manual or discovered Xref copy work. Selecting BindAll clears manual children. Bind and Insert select AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 and 1 respectively. Bind preserves Xref-prefixed names. Insert merges names and can produce naming conflicts. Core Console boundary CoreConsoleRuntime.FindCoreConsole searches: An existing path from ACCORECONSOLE. accoreconsole.exe in PATH order. AutoCAD 2026, 2025, and 2024 under C:\Program Files\Autodesk. DWG TrueView 2025 under the same directory. Each run extracts an embedded DBTools.ToolCad.RecordSet.* script to a unique temporary .lsp file and attempts deletion in finally. Deletion failures log a Warning. CoreConsoleRunner starts both redirected reads immediately and returns immutable standard output, standard error, and exit code. It creates a temporary .scr file that loads and invokes the extracted LISP script: accoreconsole.exe /i "<input.dwg>" /s "<temporary.scr>" Cancellation terminates the owned process tree and observes terminal stream completion. The runner attempts .scr cleanup on every exit and logs deletion failures. Execution rechecks Core Console availability for each CAD repath or bind item. If it is missing, the executor logs the affected DWG path and throws InvalidOperationException rather than using heuristic copying. Script and function Argument Behavior rs_list_xrefs.lsp, rs-list-xrefs Host DWG path Enumerates Xref blocks and emits nested JSON rs_repath_xrefs.lsp, rs-repath-xrefs host.dwg\|new_root Strips matching root prefixes from Xref paths and saves rs_bind_all_xrefs.lsp, rs-bind-all-xrefs host.dwg\|BIND or host.dwg\|INSERT Sets BINDTYPE, binds *, purges three times, quick-saves Discovery requires a zero exit code and parseable JSON between the first { and last } in output. The root requires an xrefs array. Every node requires a non-null children array with non-null nodes. Host, node name, and node path can be blank. Blank paths do not expand into copy work. The JSON fields are host, xrefs, name, path, overlay, and children. The shipped scanner emits overlay: false rather than detecting overlay state. The scanner calls vl-file-syst-exists-p before opening a referenced drawing. The shipped scripts define no such function. A scan fault takes the heuristic path described above. The repath script receives a root, not the planner's source-to-copy mapping. It only strips a case-insensitive matching root prefix. It does not resolve relocated or collision-renamed Xrefs. CadExecutor checks only the repath process exit code. Bind requires both a zero exit code and an output marker containing "ok":true. These contracts do not establish that every dependency in an arbitrary DWG package resolves. Revit repath RevitRepathItem.SourceHost preserves the source reference base while Host names the copied RVT. Mapping keys are normalized source paths and values are allocated output paths. The writer reads effective references, skips Content references, and matches against the source base. It sets desired paths while preserving effective loaded/unloaded state. TransmissionWriteResult.UpdatedCount is zero for no matching changes. The writer leaves the copied RVT untouched in that case. A positive count causes TransmissionData to be written with IsTransmitted = true. A rewritten workshared copy opens detached and cannot create new locals while transmitted. Reference failures preserve operation, host, reference ID, old/new path context, and original causes through RevitOperationException. Owner cancellation remains cancellation. Safety policy PolicyReader loads the embedded resource DBTools.ToolConfigs.RecordSet.recordset_policy.json from Policies/recordset_policy.json. It does not load a user-side policy file. JSON member Shipped value or rule allowed_target_roots Nonempty required list. Shipped root is \\fileserver\Projects verify_after_copy Required Boolean, shipped false min_free_bytes Required nonnegative number, shipped 10,737,418,240 denied_extensions .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk, .exe allowed_extensions Optional deny_globs Required list, shipped *backup*.rvt, *.old, ~$* paths.enable_long_paths Required Boolean in required paths object, shipped false delete_mode Defaults to quarantine. No plan action consumes it require_sentinel_for_delete Defaults true. No delete action consumes it Configured string entries must be nonblank. Roots must be absolute Windows drive-letter paths or complete UNC server/share paths. Relative, drive-relative, root-relative, and incomplete UNC roots fail admission. Malformed or incompatible policy throws. It is not normalized into valid data. Preview checks the target against admitted roots. Execution reloads policy and checks it again. The containment predicate admits equality with the root and descendants. Before acquiring the lock, execution checks every output-bearing plan path: directories, copy destinations, CAD repath hosts/roots, bind hosts, Revit hosts, and mapping destinations. Copy sources, mapping keys, and Revit source hosts remain source paths. Execution requires free space minus max(TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes) to meet MinFreeBytes. Safe filesystem operations resolve existing file and directory redirects before checking containment. Recursive copies carry destination checks into every nested operation. Lock, sentinel, and manifest mutations repeat containment checks. These checks do not make validation and mutation atomic against concurrent path replacement. Copies overwrite existing destination files and preserve the source file's UTC creation, last-access, and last-write timestamps. Optional verification compares SHA-256 hashes, including every allowed file in a copied directory. It verifies copied bytes before later CAD/Revit mutations. Execution, cancellation, and audit files ExecutionPlanExecutor.ExecuteAsync validates preconditions, creates runtime metadata, acquires the lock, writes the sentinel, executes items in order, and writes an outcome manifest. It always attempts lock release after successful acquisition. The UI passes CancellationToken.None and shows a non-cancelable overlay. Lower owners honor supplied cancellation at work boundaries. Execution is not dispatched to a worker thread. Outcome Result Successful execution ExecutionStatus.Ok, ok manifest Owner cancellation before lock acquisition Cancelled, empty run ID and manifest path Owner cancellation after acquisition Cancelled, cancelled manifest, lock release Unexpected fault or foreign cancellation Attempt failed manifest, release lock, propagate failure Manifest-write, diagnostic, or lock-release failures remain visible with the primary failure. A cancellation-manifest failure preserves both cancellation and write exceptions. Preflight failures fault the returned task and create no manifest. The UI displays (none) when no manifest exists and preserves known sentinel state for pre-lock cancellation. Runtime paths are: {target}/.recordset.lock {target}/.recordset_sentinel {target}/_recordset_manifests/{run_id}.json Run IDs use UTC yyyyMMdd-HHmmss plus four random lowercase hex characters. The lock uses FileMode.CreateNew, FileShare.None, and UTF-8 contents: run_id={run_id} fingerprint={fingerprint} Acquisition invokes no external log callback after creation. A write/dispose failure attempts partial-lock deletion before propagating. After acquisition, logging and all later work are inside the release boundary. The sentinel is opened or created and remains after completion. There is no package deletion or quarantine plan action. SafeOperationRuntime.TrashRoot names _RS_TRASH/{run_id} but execution does not use it. The manifest has this shape: { "run_id": "20260113-154200-a1b2", "fingerprint": "0123456789abcdef", "target_root": "C:\\Output", "utc": "2026-01-13T15:42:00Z", "summary": { "hosts": 1, "unique_links": 3, "copy_bytes": 1000000, "predicted_output_bytes": 1500000, "items": 8 }, "status": "ok" } SafeWriteManifestRequest carries only the five summary scalars and Status. Execution projects these from PlanSummary. Operations does not depend on the planning aggregate. The manifest records summary/status, not an item-by-item rollback journal. The lock prevents concurrent Record Set executions at one target. It does not roll back file mutations. A failed run can leave copied or rewritten files. Inspect its log and manifest before cleaning output or retrying. Remove a stale lock only after establishing that its execution is no longer active. Manage Items The Options menu opens discipline or building catalogs through ManageDisciplinesCommand and ManageBuildingsCommand. ManageItemsWindowViewModel exposes AddCommand, RenameCommand, and DeleteCommand. Add trims NewName and requires nonblank input. It ignores case-insensitive duplicates and clears NewName after adding. Rename requires a selected item and nonblank RenameTo, trims the replacement, and rejects case-insensitive duplicates. It replaces the item in place, invokes the rename callback, selects the replacement, and clears RenameTo. Delete requires a selection, removes the item, invokes the delete callback, and clears selection and RenameTo. MetadataCatalogWorkflow returns the ordered catalog edits for the App view model to apply to host/link metadata. The dialog's default Close button closes without accepting a separate result payload. UI and test contracts PreviewWorkflowState requires a current preview, allowed target, and no Block messages before Process can run. Async Add Hosts, Sync Preview, and Execute commands use nonthrowing safe execution and restore busy state. Debounced preview handles expected owner cancellation separately. For Ok and Cancelled results, the production overlay reports completion and an alert shows status and manifest path. Execution failures throw to the application error-banner boundary without showing that completion alert. There is no separate progress window with Copy Logs or Cancel controls. Pure fixtures exercise production planning, collision handling, policy admission, execution ordering, cancellation, process-stream handling, lock cleanup, manifest output, and filesystem redirects. Hosted fixtures exercise actual TransmissionData and application interaction. See Record Set tests for WPF fixture lifetime requirements.
