developer-guide/tools/common/recordset.h.summary: Record Set Record Set copies Revit host files and external references into a target directory and rewrites copied references. It previews an ordered plan before executing filesystem, CAD, and Revit TransmissionData operations. Execution can leave partial output on failure. The current UI has no cancel action. See the technical specification for formats, ordering, safety checks, and CAD limitations. Use Choose an allowed target folder. Add host RVT files. Assign discipline and building metadata in the Hosts grid. Review the destination tree and Info, Warning, or Block messages. Configure DWG actions through the selected DWG's context menu. Run Process when the preview is current and has no blocking messages. Duplicate host picks produce issues and are skipped. A host with a failed reference scan is rejected. It does not become an empty row. Canceling a file or folder picker preserves the current state. Target, host, metadata, and CAD changes invalidate the preview immediately. RecordSetPreviewSyncCoordinator debounces automatic refresh by 350 ms at DispatcherPriority.Normal. Preview planning runs through Task.Run and publishes on the UI context. Execution remains on its caller context and uses a non-cancelable progress overlay. Busy state disables editing, CAD actions, options, and ordinary window close. The footer reports Root, Free, ACAD, and Sentinel status. Root is Pending, Allowed, or Blocked; Sentinel is Pending, Present, or Missing. ACAD shows the Core Console path or Unavailable. Presentation and lifetime The main modal shell loads DBTools.ToolViews.RecordSet.RecordSetWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. It uses title Record Set, size 1240 × 780, minimum 980 × 640, CenterScreen placement, and a taskbar entry. Manage Items loads DBTools.ToolViews.RecordSet.ManageItemsWindow.xaml with a bound title, size 520 × 420, minimum 420 × 300, CenterOwner placement, and a taskbar entry. Its Close button is the default button, so Enter closes the dialog. Both Close buttons use ButtonCommandCloseBehavior.ExecuteAndClose and honor the session close gate. User close returns false. With Debug Mode on, the logger window opens after the main dialog closes. Tree containers bind IsSelected and IsExpanded two-way. The stable selected-item behavior reports view selection through a OneWayToSource binding to SelectedTreeNode. A rebuilt preview reselects the same SourceFile and expands only its ancestor chain. Explicit selection changes or a missing file cancel pending reselection. Right-click selects and focuses a row or tree item. Right-clicking a Hosts row other than the current item makes it the sole selection, including when it already belongs to a multi-selection. Rows allow logical focus but remain outside Tab navigation. Options opens below its button. CAD actions require a selected DWG leaf. Manage Disciplines, Manage Buildings, Auto-discover CAD Xrefs, and Allow CAD repath remain disabled until hosts exist. Metadata Add new choices defer the prompt, preserve the prior value on cancellation, and never store the sentinel as metadata. Plan-message bindings use OneTime. CAD bind commands accept the view's string values Bind and Insert. Retirement releases the preview timer and deferred prompts synchronously. Active preview or execution work produces a Dev Mode retirement failure. Idle retirement disposes the view model and services without a dispatcher frame. Source ownership Source and manifest: src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. The manifest places Record Set on the Testing panel with InlineUi, order 60, and icon key recordset. Command and availability use DBTools.RecordSet.App.Composition.RecordSetCommand. The module is DBTools.RecordSet.App.Composition.RecordSetToolModule. Owner Responsibility App/Composition Module, command, registration, AppLauncher, and AppLaunchDependencies App/Views Main raw view and RecordSetWindowSession App/ViewModels Binding state, RecordSetWindowServices, debounce, and interaction sequencing App/DesignTime Designer binding surface and DesignTimeSampleFactory Features/Domain Files, hosts, plan options, plan items, summaries, and messages Features/Planning Host import, plan context, destination rules, preview Features/Execution Progress workflow, preflight, item dispatch, outcome handling Features/Operations Filesystem, Windows paths, Revit and CAD ports/adapters, safe-operation requests Features/Policy Embedded policy loading and file filtering Features/Metadata Catalog editing and neutral CatalogEdit results Features/ManageItems Catalog editor view, view model, and modal session AppLauncher constructs RecordSetWindowServices beside its consumer, RecordSetWindowViewModel. MetadataCatalogWorkflow returns ordered edits. The App view model applies them to host rows and linked-file metadata. Feature workflows do not import App row types. Stable controls and the byte converter live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/RecordSet/. Raw views merge the versioned Presentation theme and contain stable WPF types. Designer sample construction reuses PreviewTreeBuilder and locates the selected DWG by file identity at any depth. Tests The Pure project references the normal desktop tool project, which owns its source and resource mapping. Pure fixtures cover domain, planning, preview, execution, filesystem policy, CAD process handling, view models, and catalog editing. Hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover TransmissionData and WPF application behavior. WPF fixtures share WindowRuntimeScope, which releases only runtime state it installs. The hosted bootstrap supplies the Revit owner. Modal tests use ToolWindowDialog.Show with synchronous callbacks and a ten-second watchdog. The watchdog cannot interrupt native code or callbacks that do not pump the dispatcher. The CAD selection test uses a modeless test session to await preview/edit cycles outside a modal callback. It checks the selected node, ancestor expansion, CAD state, and manual Xrefs after rebuilds. Production remains modal. The execution fixture checks real copied bytes, the manifest, and lock release. Filesystem tests cover destination junctions and redirected manifest paths.

developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.title: TDV - Transfer Drafting Views | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.summary: TDV - Transfer Drafting Views TDV (Transfer Drafting Views) is a tool for importing and exporting drafting views between Revit documents and a central library. It enables teams to maintain a shared collection of standard drafting views that can be distributed across projects. Overview TDV provides two primary operations: Export to Library - Copy drafting views from the active document to a central library file Import from Library - Copy drafting views from a library file to the active document The tool handles worksharing, creates local copies for edits, and synchronizes changes back to the central library file after export operations. Features Core Capabilities Bi-directional transfer - Import and export drafting views between documents View type mapping - Map source view types to destination view types, or retain original type Conflict detection - Real-time detection of naming conflicts with existing views and duplicate destination names inside the current selection Replace mode - Option to replace existing views with the same name Preview panel - Live preview of selected drafting views with pan/zoom support Batch transfer - Transfer multiple views in a single operation Destination transaction grouping - Every batch group and item transaction is bound to the same explicit destination document for atomicity, including non-active library destinations Progress tracking - Per-view progress feedback during transfer operations Crash Hardening (2026-02-07) The TDV import/export apply path was hardened after a Revit 2026 hard-crash investigation: Destination-bound transactions - The transfer group and per-view transactions are now started against the explicit destination Document, not implicitly against ActiveUIDocument. Cross-document safety checks - TDV now validates that source/destination contexts are valid live documents and not the same document. Transfer run diagnostics - Transfer start logs include run id plus source/destination title and path to improve post-crash forensics. Non-activating library open - TDV now opens library files with Application.OpenDocumentFile(...) (no activate) so the host model stays active during transfer and cleanup. Close-failure truth - Required save/sync close treats a Document.Close(...) == false result as an operational failure. Best-effort cleanup (TryCloseAsync) returns false only when Revit refuses to close the active document; unexpected cleanup failures propagate instead of being converted into a warning-only result. Library Management Multiple library files - Configure multiple library files with fallback paths Path validation - Automatic validation of library file accessibility Local copy workflow - Creates local copies from central files for worksharing Automatic sync - Syncs changes back to central after export with detailed comments View Transfer Details When transferring views, TDV: Validates destination names before entering the transfer transaction Creates or prepares the destination view with the selected view type Copies the view scale and description parameters Copies all elements from the source view (excluding viewports, title blocks, schedules, etc.) Copies element graphic overrides from source to destination If any of those steps fail, the per-view transaction rolls back and TDV records the row as failed instead of reporting partial success. DestinationTransactionGroup receives the destination Document at begin, rejects item or finalization calls for any other document, and runs each item transaction against that owned destination. This keeps import (library -> host) and export (host -> non-active library) under the same real Revit group rather than resolving the group from ActiveUIDocument. Successful row state and add/replace counts are queued until the group returns an observed Committed outcome. An observed RolledBack outcome marks attempted rows discarded; an unknown or failed finalization withholds success without claiming either commit or rollback. Operation, finalization, and disposal failures remain ordered in the logged exception chain while the row result keeps the stable per-view error code and message shape. Sources: src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Execution/DestinationTransactionGroup.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Execution/Transfer.ApplySelection.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Execution/Transfer.RunState.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Domain/TransferResult.cs View Type Resolution Rules The row View Type combobox is destination-scoped for the active transfer direction: Import (library -> host): combobox options are drafting view types from the host document. Export (host -> library): combobox options are drafting view types from the library document. Retain Original always resolves to the source view's drafting type name for that row. If that type name is missing in the destination document, TDV creates it by duplicating an existing destination drafting ViewFamilyType and renaming the duplicate. If source type name resolution fails, TDV records a per-view SourceTypeNameUnavailable error and does not silently fall back. Architecture TDV's manifest entrypoints and DI live in App/Composition. App/Sessions/WindowSession creates a registered stable modal shell through Core's ToolWindowFactory, owns the owner provider, logger display, alerts, banners, initial load, normal-close cleanup, and result projection. App/Views/TdvWindow.xaml is embedded raw XAML with the named header, grid, preview, and actions sections inlined. The separate library settings view is also raw XAML, loaded with ToolWindowXaml.LoadElement. Both resources have explicit logical names and contain only stable/framework WPF types. TdvWindowViewModel remains the App orchestration edge. App/Persistence/CachePaths supplies cache roots to the Library and Preview capabilities. Preview image caching and its session temp-directory lifecycle remain in Features/Preview/State. Transfer is a single Revit-facing transfer service split across focused partial files: constructor/shared guards, catalog operations, apply-selection orchestration, and per-row transfer steps. The split is organizational only; it does not introduce an additional service boundary around Revit transaction state. DraftingViewAdapter.cs owns drafting-view enumeration/name lookup, DraftingViewTypeAdapter.cs owns drafting-view type lookup and missing destination type creation, DraftingViewAdapter.Transfer.cs owns drafting-view create/copy/clear/override transfer operations, and PreviewExporter.cs owns preview export behavior. Transfer.RunState.cs keeps the private per-run selection accounting beside, but out of, the apply-selection orchestration file. It holds duplicate destination names, deferred committed-row successes, cancellation, rollback/unknown-finalization row reporting, and the final TransferResult; it is compiled into the same Transfer partial class, not a second service or transaction boundary. Transfer command orchestration is split by operation direction. ExportTransferWorkflow and ImportTransferWorkflow own their feature-specific document and outcome decisions, while LibraryTransferWorkflow owns shared catalog selection, library-open coordination, close warnings, and host reactivation requests. The Library workflow consumes its Library-owned ILibrarySelectionDialog port; the two Transfer workflows consume the Transfer-owned ITransferDialog port. App/Sessions/WindowSession implements both inward ports: it owns library-selection presentation, loads the embedded TDV view and shows its stable shell modally with the application-provided IWindowOwnerHandleProvider, and projects the window counts/errors into TransferDialogResult. The App type deliberately uses window/session language; no feature-named presentation adapter is exiled under App. LibraryDocumentService stays focused on Revit document open/save/sync/close calls, while LibraryCatalog owns library path validation from the current TDV settings snapshot. Sources: src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Library/Workflow/ILibrarySelectionDialog.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Operations/ITransferDialog.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/App/Sessions/WindowSession.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs Project Structure src/Tools/Common/TDV/ ├── App/ │ ├── Behaviors/ │ ├── Composition/ │ ├── DesignTime/ │ ├── Persistence/ │ ├── Sessions/ │ ├── ViewModels/ │ └── Views/ ├── Assets/ ├── Features/ │ ├── Library/ │ ├── Preview/ │ │ ├── Revit/ │ │ └── State/ │ └── Transfer/ ├── Settings/ ├── Tests/ ├── DBTools.TDV.csproj └── manifest.yml Service Registration TDV registers its tool services from App/Composition/TdvToolModule through App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddTdv(). Registrations stay scoped because TDV consumes Revit run-scope dependencies. The composition root supplies the current Revit year and library-file metadata probe, keeps concrete Revit adapters in their feature Revit wings, and wires the import/export workflows at the tool edge. services.AddScoped<Transfer>(sp => new Transfer(gate, tx, groups, logger)); services.AddScoped<Func<LibraryCatalog>>(sp => () => new LibraryCatalog( settings.Get<LibraryOptions>().Files.ToList(), RevitInstanceIdentity.RevitYear, RevitYearProbe.Probe)); services.AddScoped<LibraryDocumentService>(sp => new LibraryDocumentService( gate, logger, CachePaths.LibraryLocalsRoot, RevitInstanceIdentity.RevitYear, RevitYearProbe.Probe)); services.AddScoped<WindowSession>(sp => new WindowSession( transferService, alerts, loggerFactory, loggerWindowHost, ownerHandleProvider, windowFactory)); services.AddScoped<ILibrarySelectionDialog>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<WindowSession>()); services.AddScoped<ITransferDialog>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<WindowSession>()); Key Services Service Purpose Transfer Core Revit transfer operations LibraryCatalog Library path catalog projection from a supplied library-entry snapshot LibraryDocumentService Revit document open/close/save/sync operations using an App-supplied cache root ILibrarySelectionDialog Library-owned inward port for library selection presentation ITransferDialog Transfer-owned inward port for the modal transfer window and result WindowSession App/Sessions implementation of both ports; owns WPF owner reuse, modal window lifetime, and result projection LibraryTransferWorkflow Shared catalog selection, document cleanup, and host reactivation workflow Transfer Service Operations The concrete Transfer defines: Method Description BuildViewItemsAsync Collects drafting views from source document ApplySelectionAsync Executes transfer work in one continuous Revit API callback WouldConflictAsync Checks for naming conflicts ExportPreviewAsync Generates preview image for a view ApplySelectionAsync must start inside an active Revit API callback. The supplied gate and transaction runner must keep transfer execution in that initiating callback. The three query methods can queue each complete operation independently. UI Components Main Window (TdvWindow) The registered modal shell retains the title "Transfer Drafting Views", initial size 1400 × 700, minimum size 1200 × 600, centered placement, taskbar entry, and resizable layout. The named sections in the raw view retain their controls and commands: TransferHeaderView: conflict warning, type filter, search, and separator. TransferGridView: drafting-view transfer grid and row visuals. TransferActionsView: status, selection/transfer actions, and errors. TransferPreviewView: preview panel, cursor-relative wheel zoom, mouse panning, zoom button, and image-update zoom. The Sandbox manifest also declares these shell dimensions, taskbar visibility, and centered placement. The authenticated discovery bridge carries them into the same stable options used by the raw Sandbox host. The main raw view merges Presentation's theme once at its root; the standalone library settings view merges its own theme. String item lists and tooltips use explicit text templates. Row-state triggers use enum names as strings. The existing stable PreviewZoomBehavior owns zoom-on-image-update and defers its zoom operation until layout. DBTools.Presentation.Tools.TDV.TdvPanZoomBehavior owns mouse pan/zoom and releases capture, cursor state, and subscriptions during retirement. ProgressOverlay.For(session.Window) attaches after the view is loaded and before showing the dialog. A normal Closed notification clears UI actions, cancels obsolete preview/conflict requests, disposes the view model, and removes its cache files. The host retires the session and releases owned subscriptions, behavior state, the initializer, overlay registration, and owner. TDV's cleanup and result contract uses the normal Closed notification, including a window closed before ShowDialog; a normal early close still permits library-document cleanup. Late callbacks and catalog results leave a disposed view model alone. A load failure after close does not show an alert or log a load error, and failure to present a load-error alert still requests close. Dev Mode retirement diagnoses a pending load, preview, conflict refresh, or transfer instead of cancelling tasks during retirement. Idle retirement is synchronous and does not pump the dispatcher. The library settings page uses stable tree selection and a focus-request counter. Selecting a main library entry with an empty or whitespace alias focuses and selects the alias text at Background priority. Entries with an existing alias and fallback entries do not take focus. ViewModel (TdvWindowViewModel) Key properties and commands: Property Type Description Items ObservableCollection<ViewItem> Filtered list of views Search string Search filter text SelectedViewTypeFilter string View type filter SelectedItem ViewItem Currently selected view PreviewSource ImageSource Preview image HasAnyConflict bool Indicates naming conflicts Status string Status bar text Command Description ApplySelectionCommand Executes the transfer ClearSelectedCommand Clears all selections ClearSearchCommand Clears search filter View Item (ViewItem) Represents a single drafting view in the UI: Property Type Description SourceViewId int Revit element ID ViewName string Editable view name ViewType string Selected destination type ViewTypeName string Original source type name Checked bool Selected for transfer Replace bool Replace if exists HasConflict bool Has naming conflict HasTypeWarning bool Source type unavailable RowState RowState Typed transfer status (Pending, Success, Failure, Conflict) ViewItem keeps row state and selection data native so its behavior can be tested in DBTools.TDV.Pure.Tests without Revit, WPF visibility types, or the local Revit host. Duplicate destination-name checks, blank-name validation, and transfer result row-state presentation live in TransferStateService, which keeps those presentation-state transitions pure while TdvWindowViewModel remains the Revit/WPF orchestration edge. The XAML designer uses a shell-design-time data model with the same binding shape as transfer rows, but it does not instantiate or import runtime ViewItem or TDV domain-state types. That keeps design-time sample data from coupling the designer package back into the production transfer view-model workflow. Preview Features The preview panel supports: Debounced loading - 200ms debounce prevents excessive exports Bounded cache - Keeps up to 32 preview images; the oldest inserted view is evicted first (first-in-first-out) Pan and zoom - Interactive image manipulation via PanZoomBehavior Zoom Extents - Fits + centers the preview image in the viewport Best-effort cropping - Preview exports are cropped to content bounds (non-background pixels) so extents-based zoom targets the real view content Honest placeholder states - The empty-state text now distinguishes no row selected from preview export failed Latest-request ownership - Each debounced request captures and owns one local cancellation source/token. Selection, image, unavailable, and exception terminal publications all re-check both that token and the captured sequence; a superseded request can log its fault but cannot overwrite the latest preview. Expected cancellation emits no exception stacktrace. Dark theme background - Consistent preview appearance (RGB: 43, 44, 61) Source: src/Tools/Common/TDV/App/ViewModels/TdvWindowViewModel.Preview.cs:30-114 Cache Locations TDV stores transient files under %APPDATA%\\DBTools\\Cache\\TDV\\: LibraryLocals\\ - Per-operation workshared locals (deleted after the operation closes the library document) Preview\\ - Per-window preview export images Settings Configuration Library Settings TDV uses the LibrarySettings class to store library file configurations: public sealed class LibrarySettings { public IList<LibraryFileEntry> Files { get; set; } public bool HasWarnings { get; set; } } public sealed class LibraryFileEntry { public string? MainPath { get; set; } public string? FallbackPath { get; set; } public string? Alias { get; set; } } Each library entry supports: Main path - Primary path to the library RVT file Fallback path - Alternative path (e.g., for different network locations) Alias - Optional friendly name used in the Import/Export library picker Settings Pack The SettingsPackContext provides the settings UI with: Tree-based library file management Add/remove library files Add/remove fallback paths Real-time path validation Pending changes tracking The settings-pack factory supplies the current Revit year and metadata probe from the TDV composition root, so library validation stays consistent with runtime import/export checks without making settings UI code depend on Revit/Services. Runtime library validation follows the same boundary: LibraryTransferWorkflow receives a Func<LibraryCatalog> from the composition root, so transfer workflows do not import the mutable TDV settings type directly. Settings Path Presentation Library paths in settings are rendered with: Validation icon at the left of each tree row (green check / red error) Tooltip showing the full absolute path Compact display text that keeps root + filename + the final 3 folder levels This avoids horizontal scrolling while preserving useful location context. Path Validation Library paths are validated for: File existence .rvt extension Revit version compatibility (file's saved version must match the current Revit session) Revit metadata readability (BasicFileInfo probe failures now mark the path invalid instead of allowing access) Accessibility Invalid paths trigger a settings warning that disables the import/export commands. Library warnings are evaluated on startup, so the Import/Export ribbon tools may be disabled immediately if configured library paths are invalid. Revit Version Validation Library files are checked at two points to prevent version mismatches or unreadable-version access: Validation time (LibraryCatalog.ValidatePath): Uses the injected Revit metadata probe to read the file's saved Revit version and compare it against the current session. Mismatched files are marked invalid with a descriptive failure reason. If the metadata probe throws or returns no saved year, the path is also marked invalid and TDV logs the probe failure with the full exception instead of allowing access. Open time (LibraryDocumentService.OpenLibraryAsync): A belt-and-suspenders check before opening. Throws InvalidOperationException if the file version doesn't match, which is caught by the command's try/catch and displayed as a banner. This prevents two dangerous scenarios: Workshared files: WorksharingUtils.CreateNewLocal() would throw a version mismatch error at open time Non-workshared files: Revit would silently upgrade the file, which is destructive Library Open Error Presentation When opening a library document, TDV routes import and export through LibraryTransferWorkflow.OpenLibraryAsync(...). Revit document open work still happens in LibraryDocumentService.OpenLibraryAsync(...); open failures propagate through the direction-specific workflow to the command ISafeExecutor boundary instead of being flattened into the same null path used for cancelled library selection. Fix the paths and save the settings to re-enable import/export." disableTools: - DBTools.ExportToLibrary - DBTools.ImportFromLibrary ribbonTools: - internalName: DBTools.ExportToLibrary commandType: drafting views to the library" controlKind: StackedButtonItem splitGroup: library_transfer order: 0 - internalName: DBTools.ImportFromLibrary commandType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvImportCommand Per-View Error Codes Transfer failures are categorized by error code: Code Description Unknown Unspecified error DestinationTypeMissing Target view type not found SourceTypeNameUnavailable Cannot read source view type CreateViewFailed Failed to create or prepare destination view CopyElementsFailed Failed to copy view elements OverridesFailed Failed to copy graphic overrides DestinationNameRequired Destination view name was blank DuplicateTargetName Another selected row used the same destination view name DestinationNameConflict Destination view already existed and Replace was not enabled ClearDestinationViewFailed Existing destination contents could not be cleared MetadataCopyFailed View scale/description copy failed TransactionRolledBack Revit discarded attempted changes for the run Error Reporting After each transfer attempt, TDV now always surfaces result UX: Top banner on the TDV window (success/warning) with selected/processed/result counts Summary alert with: Selected, processed, added, replaced, failed, and not-attempted counts Optional per-view issue table when failures exist Action buttons: Accept and Transfer More and Close Tool Copy-to-clipboard for per-view issue rows TDV also records and surfaces selection accountability: Transfer logs now include selected view identifiers/names (bounded preview) Result payload includes SelectedCount, ProcessedCount, FailedCount, UnprocessedCount, Cancelled, and the observed FinalizationOutcome; AllChangesDiscarded is derived only from RolledBack TDV now carries per-row transfer state through the shared RowState enum from Transfer into the row view models and XAML triggers instead of routing string status literals through presentation code TDV logs per-view operation failures with the preserved exception object while recording only the stable row-facing code/message in TdvApplySelectionResult Success row callbacks and committed add/replace counts publish only after an observed Committed transaction-group outcome An observed rollback marks attempted rows discarded. Unknown finalization zeroes projected success, marks attempted rows failed with Unknown, and reports that the destination edit state is unverified without claiming rollback. Save/sync paths always attempt library-document close. A Document.Close(...) == false result is a required-close failure, not success. A sole save, sync, or close failure preserves its original exception; when both the primary operation and close fail, TDV throws one ordered AggregateException with the primary failure first. Best-effort cleanup returns false only for Revit's active-document refusal. Other cleanup failures propagate; when an export has already failed, TDV reports one ordered AggregateException with the transfer failure first and the cleanup failure second. Revit API Operations Getting Drafting Views new FilteredElementCollector(doc) .OfClass(typeof(View)) .WhereElementIsNotElementType() .Cast<View>() .Where(v => v.ViewType == ViewType.DraftingView && !v.IsTemplate) Copying View Contents Elements are copied using ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements with a custom IDuplicateTypeNamesHandler that uses destination types when duplicates are found. Destination Name Validation TDV no longer auto-suffixes destination drafting view names during apply. If a selected row targets a blank name, collides with an existing destination view while Replace is off, or duplicates another selected row's destination name, the row is blocked/fails explicitly. Skipped Categories The following categories are excluded from copy operations: Title Blocks Viewports Views Schedules Guide Grids Command Reference Library Selection Dialog Sizing TDV export/import library selection dialogs override default alert dimensions to a compact tool-specific size: Width: 640 Height: 420 MinWidth: 520 MinHeight: 340 Library Picker Display The library picker list uses: Alias (when configured) for a short readable name A compact tail-of-path suffix when no alias is present (keeps the dialog narrow without losing location context) Export Command Flow Validate library paths are configured Prompt user to select a library file If workshared, create a per-operation local copy under the TDV cache folder Open library document Show the registered TDV modal session for view selection Execute transfer to library Sync changes to central with comment Close library and reactivate original document Surface a warning only when cleanup is refused because the library is active; otherwise propagate a close failure so a successful export is never reported after a required close failure Import Command Flow Validate library paths are configured Prompt user to select a library file If workshared, create a per-operation local copy under the TDV cache folder Open library document Show the registered TDV modal session for view selection Execute transfer to active document Close library (no sync needed) Surface a cleanup warning if the library document could not be closed automatically Cross-References Architecture Overview - Application architecture patterns App Project - Main application and tool hosting Testing TDV includes pure and local tests for: ViewItem - pure row-state/view item behavior TransferStateService - pure duplicate-name, blank-name, and transfer result presentation behavior LibraryCatalog - Path validation and library catalog projection TdvAdapterTests - local Revit source/destination document transfer tests LibraryDocumentServiceTests - local Revit document-lifecycle tests: non-workshared library open, Revit-year mismatch rejection (via the injected file-year probe), save-and-close primary/close aggregation, the documented active-library cleanup refusal, and host reactivation. Fixtures reuse the existing non-workshared test models via temp copies; the workshared SyncAndCloseAsync path is held out (no workshared central fixture in the corpus). Last updated: July 2026

developer-guide/tools/common/vtc-spec.ht.title: VTC As-Built Spec | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/vtc-spec.ht.summary: VTC As-Built Spec This file records the current VTC design after the March 6, 2026 native-only Revit Links rewrite. The current ownership boundary has one document façade: Revit/Template/TemplateRuntime. App composition supplies its concrete extractor, Revit-link adapter, difference evaluator, applier, and materializer. App batch-session orchestration consumes the focused App/Sessions/ITemplateSessionRuntime port implemented by that façade; tests replace the external port without redeclaring or shadowing the production runtime. Comparison owns SettingPreviewItem, window comparison state, the diff-tree filter contract, substantive Comparison views, and the UI-neutral RevitLinkActionSourceResolver; Library owns its concrete Library view; Template Apply owns pending overrides, apply outcomes, Revit-link batch execution, and expected conflict classification; App owns keyed outcome projection plus Revit-link prompting, modal hosting, refresh, result presentation, and cross-pane request handling. App composes outcome-only runtime templates into Comparison views; feature packages do not import App. AlertPresenter is the only App-facing alert boundary, so no workflow or view-model consumer receives IAlertService. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateRuntime.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/TemplateApply/Execution/TemplateApplier.Operations.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/Comparison/Window/VtcWindowComparisonCoordinator.cs Scope VTC compares two view templates from the current document. Category edits remain staged locally until Process. Import Categories are not a separate subsystem; they are ordinary category rows routed to the imported tab. Revit Links are limited to settings that the active public Revit API can both read and write. VG Tab Structure VTC still mirrors Revit VG organization at the tree level: ModelCategories AnnotationCategories AnalyticalModelCategories ImportedCategories Filters RevitLinks Worksets DesignOptions Imported categories are detected in VtcCategoryClassifier; Revit Links are a dedicated tab whose children are grouped link-setting rows. Import Categories Extraction and compare ExtractCategories(...) emits imported parents and imported layers/subcategories as VtcCategoryGraphicsData. AddCategoryChanges(...) keeps those rows in the same category compare pipeline as all other categories. Imported rows keep SettingType=CategoryOverride; there is no import-specific apply path. Edit/process behavior Inline edit buttons, Inspector-side edit actions, Preview, pending override retention, BatchApply, save-merged, and snapshot apply all reuse the standard category path. Missing-side imported selections reset visibility/graphics the same way as any other category row. Revit Links Contract The linked-file blob is deleted. The active contract is: VtcTemplateSettingsModel.RevitLinks VtcRevitLinkTargetInfo VtcRevitLinkSettingData VtcRevitLinkSettingValue VtcCopyRevitLinkSettingsOptions Each row is one target plus one native setting, not a mixed payload. Target kinds VTC extracts both: RevitLinkType RevitLinkInstance Targets are keyed separately, labeled separately, and copied separately. Supported setting matrix VTC derives support from runtime member availability on RevitLinkGraphicsSettings. Supported desktop Revit 2026.5+ and 2027 metadata: LinkVisibilityType LinkedViewId The current Revit 2026 metadata source is the pinned 2026.4.10 portable package used for cross-platform compilation, not proof of installed-Revit-2026.5 API parity. ViewFilterType NestedLinks ObjectStyles ColorFill ViewRange Phase PhaseFilter ViewDetailLevel Discipline The adapter binds directly to typed Revit API members; all 11 setting kinds are emitted and copied in every supported year. Extraction ExtractRevitLinks(...) enumerates link targets, reads View.GetLinkOverrides(...), and emits one VtcRevitLinkSettingData row for each of the 11 setting kinds. Simple settings use native LinkVisibility or ElementId values directly. Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level, and Discipline use their public getter/setter pairs and are stored as one explicit row each. VTC stores template display settings as typed VTC enums (DetailLevel, DisplayStyle, PartsVisibility, ViewDiscipline, VtcShowHiddenLinesMode) and only converts to Autodesk Revit enums at the Revit service boundary. Linked element names are resolved from the linked document only when available. Those names are the canonical cross-model identity for Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter. Compare and tree shape RevitLinkDiffEvaluator produces explicit diff rows keyed as link.{type|instance}.name.{link}.{setting}. TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares typed SettingValue cases instead of storing object payloads, so display/apply/App consumers pattern-match the concrete setting shape directly. LinkName is the canonical cross-model key. If it is ambiguous within a target kind, compare fails instead of guessing. DiffTreeBuilder groups those rows under Revit Links by LinkDisplayName, so the main tree shows link groups with native setting leaves. Apply and reset semantics ApplyRevitLinkSettingChange(...) reads current link overrides, mutates only the selected native setting, and writes the updated RevitLinkGraphicsSettings back through View.SetLinkOverrides(...). Apply resolves Revit-link targets by canonical LinkName only; there is no alternate id-path during snapshot/process apply. Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter are remapped by linked-element name during apply, and dependent rows prime the required top-level visibility mode before SetLinkOverrides(...) runs. Missing-side selections reset only the selected setting to host/default behavior; they do not use a compare-only fallback path. Copy Copy always handles all 11 Revit-link setting kinds from one link target to another, matching the complete set emitted during extraction. CopyRevitLinkSettings(...) reads and writes RevitLinkGraphicsSettings through typed API members. Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter copy by resolving the source linked-element name and finding the same name in the target linked RVT; raw linked-document ids are not reused. If the source linked document is unloaded and that name cannot be resolved, copy reuses the raw linked-element id only when source and target reference the same linked model. Cross-link copy fails instead of reusing an unverifiable id. The focused Revit-link modal and copy command operate on one concrete template side at a time. When both sides contain the row and no side is already selected, VTC prompts for the target template instead of silently defaulting to Left. RevitLinkActionSourceResolver first selects the only available side or a viable selected side. It reports no Revit-link value or a genuinely ambiguous two-sided input without presenting UI; App owns the corresponding error or prompt. Opening the focused modal from a leaf row scopes back to the full link group, so the modal always shows all 11 setting kinds for one link target. Removed Design Deleted from the active design: VtcLinkedFileOverrideData linked CategoryOverrides host category override masquerading copy flags for unsupported linked-category payloads compare-only linked-category UI A former in-tree VTC_Enhanced_Design.md design document was superseded by this rewrite and has since been removed; this spec is the live source of truth. Verification State Library JSON is admitted as one current snapshot shape. Required top-level members and collections must be present, explicit nulls and invalid required nested elements are rejected, and the same validation runs before saving an in-memory snapshot. Saved Revit-link rows require visibility modes from 0 through 2, no mode for linked-view ids, detail levels from 0 through 3, defined discipline values, and no enum payload on other setting kinds. GetSavedTemplates returns an empty list for DirectoryNotFoundException without creating the cache directory. Other enumeration failures raise TemplateStorageException with operation enumerate. TemplateExists returns false for a missing file or cache directory; any other probe failure raises TemplateStorageException (operation probe), so a save is refused instead of overwriting. An existing name is replaced only after the user answers Replace. Without that answer SaveTemplate publishes with overwrite disabled, so a template another process saves under the name after the probe is kept and the save fails with TemplateStorageException. TemplateStorage alone derives cache file paths from a logical template name. Its list metadata carries only name and modification time; load/delete/existence use the logical name, and rooted or separator-containing names are rejected before path derivation. DiffTreeBuilder is construction-only, while DiffTreeIndex retains the rebuilt roots and owns canonical key/path/selection and Revit-link subtree lookup for all live tree consumers. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Domain/Template/TemplateSnapshot.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/Library/Operations/TemplateStorage.cs VTC has dedicated [RevitLocal] fixtures for baseline Revit-link rows, extended Revit-link rows, transient imported-category coverage, and GM/SGT model audits. The Local harness opens promoted .rvt fixtures, creates temporary templates, imports a shared CAD asset only inside rollback scope, and leaves the seed models unchanged after the run. Current verification uses the repo wrappers for Revit 2026/2027 and the VTC test surface; Revit-hosted runs dispatch through the dbtools-daemon fleet.

developer-guide/tools/common/vtc.html.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) — Developer Guide | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/vtc.html.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) — Developer Guide VTC compares two Revit view templates, stages category edits locally, and applies selections plus eligible pending overrides through one ApplySelectedChangesCommand path (user-facing button label stays "Process"). Current Architecture Test ownership AlertBodyTemplateProviderTests belongs to VTC App composition. The VTC Pure project exercises the provider and its raw AlertBodyTemplates.xaml resource (DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml) through a plain reference to the normal desktop VTC owner; this is WPF-only and does not start a Revit host. Command + application shell VtcCommand remains the Revit entrypoint. VtcCommand validates the DBTools command context and delegates application assembly to App/Composition/VtcWindowLauncher. VtcWindowLauncher owns modal launch flow: it resolves document-scoped templates, handles the no-template alert, delegates collaborator construction to VtcWindowCompositionFactory, creates VtcWindowSession through Core ToolWindowFactory, and, after dialog close, ensures the logger window when Debug Mode is on. It always retires the comparer and linked-file windows; a dialog failure stays ahead of every retirement failure. VtcWindowCompositionFactory creates one document-scoped graph: TemplateExtractor, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, TemplateDifferenceEvaluator, TemplateApplier, TemplateMaterializer, and the single outward TemplateRuntime. TemplateRuntime is the only document façade. It owns template-ID resolution and exposes compare, extract, apply, materialize, Revit-link copy, and pattern queries without retaining a second pass-through comparison façade. App batch-session consumers depend on the focused ITemplateSessionRuntime port; the Revit façade implements it, and pure tests substitute only that external boundary rather than shadowing the production class. VtcWindowSession owns the modal tool-window session. Core ToolWindowFactory supplies the stable shell for the raw VTC view; Comparison owns the comparison workspace, Inspector, and Preview views; Library owns its concrete workspace view; the focused Revit-link modal reuses the Comparison-owned diff control. AlertPresenter is the one VTC presentation boundary. Composition supplies the raw alert service only to that presenter; App view-model and workflow consumers use the presenter for standard alerts plus bespoke requests and selections. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow owns only App session reactions for Process and Library work. The App view-model owns Revit-link prompts, modal hosting, refresh, and result presentation; TemplateRuntime delegates Revit-link batch apply/copy execution and expected-conflict classification to Template Apply. There is no App-facing feature workflow, callback inversion, or raw alert-service escape. Dev Mode view hosting VTC views are raw XAML EmbeddedResource items with explicit logical names. The main view uses DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.VtcWindow.xaml; the remaining resources are DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml, DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonWorkspaceView.xaml, DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonInspectorView.xaml, DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonPreviewView.xaml, DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.DiffViewControl.xaml, DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.LibraryView.xaml, and DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.RevitLinkSettingsWindow.xaml. VtcWindowSession reads the main resource through Core ToolWindowFactory and owns once-only owner attachment and cleanup. VTC has no custom close gate or native pick loop. Shared VTC resource dictionaries live in the stable DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC/ owner as VtcDiffViewStyles.xaml and VtcComparisonViewStyles.xaml. Stable converters in the flat DBTools.Presentation.Tools.VTC namespace are VtcConflictConverter and VtcRawViewConverter. VtcResourceTemplateSelector resolves App-owned outcome templates and always returns an empty template for standalone views. Alert bodies use full-name string keys with the stable TypeNameTemplateSelector; every content and item slot has an explicit template, immutable record values use OneTime bindings, and mutable view-model state uses INotifyPropertyChanged. The conversion preserves live comparison and Inspector bindings, preview navigation only for navigable setting keys, workspace path realization and selection, eligible left-button double-click override editing, Library split-button menu placement, and modal close behavior. Keyboard focus moves to the comparison row after the inspector tab loads. Pending navigation focus and close requests are aborted on retirement. Each raw view merges Theme once, before the VTC style dictionaries. The shared dictionaries do not merge Theme again. Vtc.TreeView keeps its original implicit TreeView base and VTC overrides; each tree retains its existing scrolling and virtualization settings. Named item selectors specify TextSearch.TextPath for prefix typing and automation names on their template text. SavedTemplateInfo, ViewFilterOption, LinePattern, FillPatternData, and TemplateOption return their display label from ToString() so item-container automation peers and text fallbacks also use the displayed label without changing the themed container styles. Two interaction changes are intentional: override editing responds only to the left mouse button, and the linked dialog’s context-menu selection commands now resolve through its own view model and work. The raw linked view itself carries the “Linked file override differences” automation name. The main window initializer retains the VtcWindow log prefix. Core services TemplateSnapshot stores explicit Revit-link setting rows in RevitLinks; the old linked-file blob payload is gone. Display settings now use typed VTC enums for detail level, display style, parts visibility, discipline, and show-hidden-lines, with explicit conversion only at the Revit API boundary. SettingDifference.LeftValue / RightValue store typed SettingValue cases instead of object, and compare/apply/App paths pattern-match those cases rather than recovering payload shape with runtime casts. TemplateDifferenceEvaluator is host-neutral under Features/Comparison; TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter own Revit mechanics behind TemplateRuntime. SettingPreviewItem and DiffTreeProjector.ViewFilter are Comparison-owned input/state contracts, so feature projections do not import App view models. DiffTreeNode contains comparison and local display state only. PendingOverrideState owns pending override DTOs without tree or UI dependencies, and TemplateApplyResult remains the sole apply-outcome authority. The App view-model projects that result onto current setting keys for row feedback and filtering without storing outcomes on comparison nodes. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow.SavedTemplates treats template extraction/merge and the cache save/delete as the mutation boundary. After a committed mutation, list refresh has its own error boundary: log the refresh failure with the template name and show one warning that the cache operation succeeded; show success only after the list refresh succeeds. Both save commands ask "Replace saved template 'X'?" through AlertPresenter before overwriting an existing name; Cancel writes nothing. DiffTreeBuilder only constructs a tree from differences. DiffTreeIndex retains the rebuilt roots and owns key lookup, canonical-node paths, tree-order selection collection, and Revit-link subtree queries for the coordinator, preview projection, and focused Revit-link modal. Owner layout VTC is multi-feature: Features/{Comparison,Library,RevitLinks,TemplateApply} own their domain/planning/state/Revit/UI layers. Tool-wide vocabulary remains under the small root Domain, including persisted RevitLinkSetting, RevitLinkSettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue, RevitLinkTarget, and RevitLinkTargetKind; application views, view models, resources, sessions, and composition live under App; shared Revit document adapters live under Revit/Template. The former Shell, Shared, and root UI organizers are dissolved. Extraction, diff computation, and native Revit-link loading/copy/apply logic live in focused owners rather than overlapping façades. Comparison owns window comparison state and UI-neutral source selection; Template Apply owns batch execution and expected conflict classification; RevitLinkSettingsAdapter owns extract/copy mechanics and reads and writes RevitLinkGraphicsSettings directly, while RevitLinkTargetResolver owns target lookup plus linked-document name/id remapping. Local Revit tests compose the same concrete runtime graph; no compatibility façade or forwarding alias remains. The App outcome projection remains App-owned. It is composed into Comparison views through runtime templates, while Comparison emits only selected-node, override-edit, and preview-setting requests for App cross-pane/modal coordination. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateRuntime.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/TemplateApply/Execution/TemplateApplier.Operations.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/App/Composition/VtcWindowCompositionFactory.cs Imported Categories Imported Categories stay inside the normal CategoryOverride pipeline. CategoryTabClassifier routes model categories with positive IDs to ImportedCategories. Other category types retain their native tab routing. Extraction, compare, inline edit, preview, Process, merged-save, and snapshot apply all reuse the same category contracts and VM state as any other category row. Tree rendering keeps imported categories under their own native-looking tab; imported layers/subcategories still inherit the imported parent tab. Revit Links Native-only contract Revit Links no longer use VtcLinkedFileOverrideData, CategoryOverrides, host-category masquerading, or compare-only linked-category blobs. VTC emits one explicit VtcRevitLinkSettingData row for each of the 11 Revit-link setting kinds. Revit-link rows now use one canonical key: target kind (type or instance), canonical LinkName, and setting kind. Cross-model compare/save/load/apply no longer switches between doc-local ids and alternate matching paths. If LinkName is ambiguous for a target kind, VTC now fails instead of guessing. The diff tree groups those rows under Revit Links by link display name, so the main tree shows all 11 leaf settings instead of one opaque link blob row. Supported API surface Supported desktop Revit 2026.5+ and 2027 public API metadata includes: ViewFilterType NestedLinks ObjectStyles Revit 2026 API/reference metadata currently derives from the pinned 2026.4.10 portable package for cross-platform compilation; it is not installed-Revit-2026.5 API-parity proof. ColorFill ViewRange Phase PhaseFilter ViewDetailLevel Discipline VTC always emits and copies all 11 Revit-link setting kinds through typed RevitLinkGraphicsSettings members. Type-level and instance-level link targets are both extracted through View.GetLinkOverrides(...) / View.SetLinkOverrides(...). UI and copy flow The context menu now exposes “Open Revit Link Settings...” and “Copy Revit Link Settings To...”. Those actions only appear on a concrete Revit-link group or leaf row, not on the Revit Links tab root. Opening the focused modal from any Revit-link leaf now scopes the modal back to that link target’s full setting group instead of showing a one-row subset. RevitLinkActionSourceResolver is the Comparison-owned, UI-neutral selection rule: it chooses the sole available side or a viable selected side, and reports ambiguity only when both sides remain viable. App owns the resulting prompt and all user-visible effects. If both Left and Right contain the same Revit-link row and no side is already selected, VTC prompts for which template the modal/copy action should operate on instead of silently defaulting to Left. The focused modal rehosts all 11 Revit-link rows present in the main tree, and a successful modal apply refreshes the main comparison so the tree is not left stale. Applying from the focused modal uses BatchApply in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one subtransaction per setting and one Undo entry. A missing comparison key is an ElementNotFound conflict; an unexpected fault rolls back the whole apply. Copy uses GetRevitLinkTargets() plus CopyRevitLinkSettings(...) and always handles all 11 Revit-link setting kinds, matching extraction. Copy runs each target in a Copy Revit Link Settings transaction, then assimilates those transactions into one Undo entry. An expected failure rolls back only that target; an unexpected fault rolls back every target. Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter are remapped by linked-element name when source and target point at different linked RVTs; raw linked-document ids are not copied across models. When the source linked document is unloaded and that remap name is unavailable, copy reuses the raw id only if source and target reference the same linked model. Cross-link copy fails instead of guessing. Removed behavior Deleted behavior: compare-only linked-category extraction CopyCategoryOverrides-style linked copy flags one-row linked-file blob compare/apply semantics linked-model Model/Annotation/Import Categories masquerading as host category rows VTC now either reads and writes a setting through public API or omits it entirely. Process + Serialization ApplySelectedChangesCommand still batches selections plus eligible pending category overrides, with per-setting SubTransaction isolation for expected conflicts. An apply failure becomes a per-setting conflict only after its subtransaction confirms RolledBack. A thrown rollback failure or another status aborts the batch with a BatchApplyException containing both causes, ordered apply failure then rollback failure. Unconfirmed rollback never publishes a pending-override conflict key. Create Merged runs template creation and the pending-override batch in one TransactionGroup (TemplateRuntime.CreateMergedTemplate), assimilated into one Undo entry named Create Merged View Template. Expected per-setting conflicts are reported and keep the new template; any other fault rolls the group back and leaves no template, so a retry with the same name succeeds. TemplateMaterializer copies the Left template with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements, using a duplicate-type handler that keeps destination types so Revit opens no modal dialog. It catches no copy failures, so any fault rolls back the group and reaches RunOrReport as an Error alert. TemplateStorage admits one complete current TemplateSnapshot graph on both load and save, including required collections, nested elements, and enum values. Incompatible data uses the existing storage exception channel; no normalization or old-format recovery is performed. TemplateStorage is the sole cache-path owner. Callers use logical template names; SavedTemplateInfo exposes only the name and modification time, and rooted or separator-containing names are rejected rather than normalized. Library enumeration and existence checks are pure queries when the cache directory is absent. Enumeration returns an empty list for DirectoryNotFoundException; other enumeration failures raise TemplateStorageException with operation enumerate. TemplateExists returns false for a missing file or folder and raises TemplateStorageException for other probe failures. Only SaveTemplate creates the directory. TemplateExtractor has no duplicability probe or logger dependency; the unused CheckDuplicability surface was deleted with all constructor callsites updated. Revit-link rows participate in Preview, Process, create-merged, and save-merged as ordinary diff rows. BuildMergedModel(...) now persists explicit RevitLinks rows instead of the deleted linked-file blob contract. Merged-template construction is Application-owned: Features/Application/Planning/VtcMergedTemplateBuilder derives the merged VtcTemplateSettingsModel from comparison result, selections, base side, and name. Application view-model operations keep only effect orchestration and call the feature builder. Missing-side Revit-link selections now reset only the selected native setting row to its default/host state. Snapshot-style compare/save/load/apply reuses the same canonical LinkName keys as normal compare; it does not switch between id keys and alternate lookup routes. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Domain/Template/TemplateSnapshot.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/Library/Operations/TemplateStorage.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateExtractor.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateMaterializer.cs Tests VtcDiffTreeBuilderTests and VtcDiffTreeNodeTests run in DBTools.VTC.Pure.Tests because diff-tree grouping, selection state, and property-change behavior are native shell state, not Revit-hosted behavior.
