developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.summary: Analytical Snap To Level Analytical Snap To Level moves selected analytical members to a chosen level elevation. Beams move both endpoints. Columns move the endpoint nearest the target elevation and retain the other endpoint. X and Y coordinates remain unchanged. A column tie moves the start endpoint. Use Select analytical members. Run Analytical Snap To Level on the Structural panel. Choose a level from the elevation-sorted level picker. Read the processed and skipped counts in the completion alert. The ribbon accepts any nonempty selection through CommandAvailability.HasSelection. Processing requires OST_AnalyticalMember, an AnalyticalMember instance, and structural role Beam or Column. The curve must be a straight Line. Girder, Member, Unset, and other roles are skipped. The tool has no persistent settings. Execution Source: src/Tools/Structural/AnalyticalSnapToLevel/. App/Composition/AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand resolves Features/AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflow. The workflow uses IAlertService for the level picker and completion alert, ITransactionRunner for changes, a window-owner provider, and a typed logger. It ensures the logger window through ILoggerWindowHost after successful completion when Debug Mode is enabled. The public snapper boundary is: public AnalyticalSnapper(ITransactionRunner tx, Document doc, ILogger logger); public (int ProcessedCount, IReadOnlyList<(ElementId ElementId, string Reason)> Skipped) Run(ICollection<ElementId> selectedIds, Level targetLevel); AnalyticalSnapper.Run(ICollection<ElementId>, Level) returns ProcessedCount and an ordered list of (ElementId, Reason) skips. AnalyticalSegment.SnapTo owns the pure endpoint rule. AnalyticalSnapper resolves the typed Revit structural role, constructs the adjusted line, and calls SetCurve. A processed member counts even when its endpoint elevations already match the target. All members run in one DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level transaction. Unexpected failures, including a SetCurve refusal, propagate to safe execution and roll back the entire run. An empty selection or a missing level choice produces SafeExecutionRefusedException. The level picker returns no choice when the document contains no levels. Skips and diagnostics Reason Constant on AnalyticalSnapper Condition not an analytical member NotAnalyticalMember Missing element, wrong category, or wrong runtime type role not supported RoleNotSupported Structural role is neither Beam nor Column not straight NotStraight Curve is not a Line would collapse WouldCollapse Adjusted length is less than Application.ShortCurveTolerance The completion alert groups skips in first-seen reason order. Each group shows its count and at most ten element IDs, followed by and N more when needed. The non-analytical group shows only its count. Debug logs include the target level, per-element skip or success, and final totals. Registration and tests manifest.yml registers DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel with the command and availability type DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.App.Composition.AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand. The button uses InlineUi, icon key analytical_snap, and order 20 on the Structural panel. The assembly is DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel. Pure tests cover endpoint geometry through AnalyticalSegmentTests and AnalyticalSegmentEdgeCaseTests. Hosted workflow tests cover skip-summary behavior. Revit integration tests live under Tests/Integration/Revit/ and exercise the command, workflow, and analytical curve changes. Related tool: Framing Joins.

developer-guide/tools/structural/erft-sp.title: ERFT technical specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/erft-sp.summary: ERFT technical specification ERFT calculates vertical offset changes for structural columns and beams against a triangulated floor or roof bottom surface. It modifies offset parameters, not level parameters. All lengths and coordinates in domain calculations use feet. Source: src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. See ERFT for composition, presentation ownership, and use. Selection and preparation Features/Selection/Revit/TargetSelectionPicker first picks a linked Floor or RoofBase. Esc switches to host selection through Selection/HostTarget/Revit/HostTargetSelectionFilter. Esc during host selection cancels launch. Each picker owns a yellow guidance banner and disposes its handle in finally. SourceSelectionFilter admits host FamilyInstance elements with: Category Requirement Structural Columns LocationPoint Structural Framing LocationCurve containing a Line, and StructuralType other than Brace SourceSelectionPicker excludes structural materials matching \bconcrete\b, case-insensitively, and reports the filtered count. It reads the instance material, then the type material when absent. Missing or blank material names do not match. Unexpected inspection failures retain element context and propagate. SourceSelectionCollector compares selected and extracted counts. Any extraction mismatch fails with Selection/SourceExtractionFailed. SourceSelectionValidator requires a selected column or a selected beam connected to a column. Beam-only validation extracts model columns and evaluates cloned beam values, so validation does not alter the live plan's connections. No connection produces Selection/NoColumnConnection. Features/Planning/PlanPreparation/Revit/PlanPreparationBuilder prepares the target, source values, framing graph, profiles, and initial adjustments before opening the window. Plan and identity Features/Domain/Adjustment/AdjustmentPlan contains: State Contents Target HostTargetId, LinkedTargetId, LinkInstanceId, TargetGeometry, TargetDisplayName Sources Lists of ColumnAdjustment and BeamAdjustment Hierarchy FramingGraph Rounding ToleranceFeet, default 1/48 ft. RoundingMode, default Nearest Profiles ProfilesByTypeId and ProfileExtractionFailuresByTypeId Storage SystemId, initialized from a GUID Revit element, type, level, link, and graph identities use long. Target IDs and connection IDs are nullable where absent. Mesh indices and counts use int. JSON numeric IDs within the older 32-bit range remain readable as long. ColumnAdjustment retains element/type identity, type name, base/top points, original top offset, and top-level identity/name. Calculation supplies target elevation, raw delta, rounded delta, new offset, status, and optional error text. BeamAdjustment retains element/type identity, type name, endpoints, original endpoint offsets, and reference-level identity/name. Each endpoint has a Free, ToColumn, or ToBeam connection and optional owner ID. Calculation supplies endpoint target elevations, deltas, rounded deltas, new offsets, status, and optional error text. Hybrid means one ToColumn end and one ToBeam end. Statuses are Pending, NoChangeNeeded, and Error. RequiresModification requires Pending and a rounded delta magnitude greater than 1e-9 at an affected end. Plan pending counts include only rows requiring modification. A Pending row without a required write contributes to no-change counts. Target geometry Features/Operations/TargetGeometry/Revit/TargetGeometryReader resolves host or linked targets. A linked target uses RevitLinkInstance.GetTotalTransform and requires a loaded link document. Geometry extraction uses Medium detail and ComputeReferences = false. It traverses solids, triangulates faces, and retains separate bottom-surface and full-element meshes. A bottom face has host-transformed normal Z at most -0.1, sampled at the midpoint of its UV bounds. No usable bottom surface returns no target geometry. Unexpected geometry faults log context and propagate. TargetSurface contains Vertices, TriangleIndices, Bounds, display/category names, ElementVertices, ElementTriangleIndices, and optional LinkTransformMatrix. Coordinates used by calculation are in the host frame. The link matrix contains 16 doubles in column-major order: [basisX.X, basisX.Y, basisX.Z, 0, basisY.X, basisY.Y, basisY.Z, 0, basisZ.X, basisZ.Y, basisZ.Z, 0, origin.X, origin.Y, origin.Z, 1] TransformLinkPointToHost requires exactly 16 values and applies the upper 3×3 basis plus translation. Features/Domain/TargetSurfaceProjector.ProjectToSurface visits every triangle, finds its nearest vertex, edge, or interior point, and retains the nearest point by squared 3D distance. GetTargetElevation returns that point's Z. It does not perform a vertical ray intersection. A query outside a triangle can resolve to an edge or vertex. An empty mesh returns no projection. There is no spatial acceleration structure. Framing graph FramingGraphBuilder.ResolveConnectionsAndBuildGraph resolves connections and emits ColumnToBeams, BeamToBeams, and ProcessingOrder. Connection tolerance is 0.5/12 feet (half an inch). Connect free beam ends to column top points within the tolerance, inclusive. For remaining free ends, find the closest other beam segment at a strictly smaller distance than the tolerance. Reject an edge that would form a dependency cycle, log a warning, and leave that end Free. Emit columns first, then topologically sort beam dependencies. Column connections use the first qualifying column in input order. Beam candidates use 3D distance to a segment with the projection parameter clamped to [0,1]. A nearly degenerate segment uses its start point. Each endpoint is independent, so hybrid connections are supported. Ready beams that frame to columns precede other ready beams. Element ID breaks ties. If unresolved dependencies remain, the builder logs and appends remaining beam IDs in sorted order. It does not return a Hierarchy/CycleDetected failure. Adjustment and rounding Features/Planning/Adjustment/AdjustmentEvaluator.CalculateAdjustments follows ProcessingOrder. It keeps adjusted column-top and beam-end elevations in dictionaries without mutating Revit. For a column: targetZ = nearest surface point Z delta = targetZ - originalTopZ roundedDelta = round(delta, tolerance, mode) newTopOffset = originalTopOffset + roundedDelta adjustedTopZ = originalTopZ + roundedDelta For each beam end: Connection Target elevation ToColumn The connected column's adjusted top Z ToBeam Interpolated Z on the supporting beam's adjusted segment Free Nearest target-surface point Z Missing dependency elevations produce Error. For beam interpolation, only XY determines the segment parameter: dx = supportEnd.X - supportStart.X dy = supportEnd.Y - supportStart.Y t = clamp(((query.X - supportStart.X)*dx + (query.Y - supportStart.Y)*dy) / (dx*dx + dy*dy), 0, 1) Z = adjustedStartZ + (adjustedEndZ - adjustedStartZ)*t When XY length squared is less than 1e-10, use adjustedStartZ. The query's Z does not influence interpolation. Each new endpoint offset is its original offset plus rounded target-minus-original-Z delta. RoundingEvaluator.ApplyRounding uses: Mode Rounded delta Nearest Math.Round(delta / tolerance) * tolerance, including .NET's midpoint-to-even rule Up Math.Ceiling(delta / tolerance) * tolerance Down Math.Floor(delta / tolerance) * tolerance Up and Down refer to signed numeric direction, including negative deltas. At helper level, nonpositive tolerance or an undefined mode returns the raw delta. UI and stored-data admission reject invalid settings before normal use. IsWithinTolerance tests abs(delta) < tolerance/2. Columns with a rounded delta within that interval become NoChangeNeeded. Beams become NoChangeNeeded when both rounded deltas satisfy it. Missing target geometry marks every row Error. Tolerance and window behavior Presets are 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1 inch, plus Custom. The default is 1/4 inch. Custom text parses with invariant culture and must be finite and at least 0.01 inch. Invalid input appears inline and disables Apply. ErftWindowViewModel.CanApply also requires a positive pending count and zero errors. The modal window contains the target/re-pick control, rounding controls, 3D preview, column/beam comparison grids, summary, Cancel, and Apply. Both grids end with a stretch Status column and a minimum width. Re-pick calls HideForPick, performs selection, recomputes the plan, and shows the same shell and preview presenter. An expected apply failure leaves the dialog available with error feedback. Successful apply reports modified and unchanged element counts, then closes the window. WindowSession.Interaction ignores duplicate Apply and Re-pick requests while IsApplyInProgress is true. The view model's close gate blocks Cancel and ordinary close during that interval. An apply exception triggers a gated-close bypass and propagates when the interaction result is collected. A concurrent close failure is retained with the apply exception. Escape clears both grid selections and marks the key event handled, so it never closes the window. The Cancel button has no IsCancel route. A mouse-down outside a grid row clears both selections regardless of button. Alerts WindowSession uses the active ERFT window as the owner for apply alerts. If that session is absent or retired, it uses the injected owner-handle provider. Selection diagnostics always use the injected provider. Event Presentation No plan to apply Info alert Expected apply failure Error alert Apply success Success alert with modified column/beam and unchanged counts Selected or stored target geometry extraction failed Top Warning banner Source extraction failed or source selection invalid Warning alert All stored sources missing Error alert Some stored sources missing Warning alert with missing count Invalid stored tolerance or rounding mode Error alert Alerts use the tool name as title and window title, with a default OK button. Profiles and preview MemberProfileExtractor creates temporary placements for unique source types and extracts section loops. It owns each temporary instance immediately after creation, before commit and geometry bake. Creation, bake, and cleanup transaction starts/commits must return Started/Committed. Any subsequent creation, commit, disposal, bake, or extraction fault reaches cleanup. Concurrent extraction and cleanup failures preserve both causes. Expected ProfileLoops/* conditions return structured per-type failures. Unexpected faults and cancellation propagate. One Info summary reports total, extracted, and unsupported counts. Per-type progress uses Debug. PreviewSceneBuilder.Build renders adjusted endpoints using extracted profiles. Missing profiles omit affected members and log counts. No successful profile still permits target-only preview. Target selection prefers bottom-surface TargetSurface. Full TargetElement is a fallback only when that mesh is unavailable. No usable mesh throws Preview/TargetMeshMissing. Mesh Color Opacity Target #4080C0 0.12 Pending member #00CC00 1.0 No-change member #808080 0.7 Error member #CC0000 1.0 PreviewProjector maps meshes, colors, tooltips, IDs, and bounds into immutable StructuralScene3D snapshots. It clamps opacity to [0,1] and uses a fixed Vector3.UnitZ exterior normal. A null mesh, empty vertices, incomplete triangle indices, out-of-range indices, or non-finite vertices throws InvalidOperationException. Missing or invalid RGB/ARGB hexadecimal color text throws FormatException. RGB input receives an opaque FF alpha prefix. A leading # is optional. The projector does not replace invalid mesh or color input with default data. The Presentation presenter owns camera/navigation, device lifetime, hit testing, and cleanup. ERFT selects PreserveAngle and FitRedefinesHome. See preview interaction. Apply transaction AdjustmentPlanExecutor rejects row errors with Apply/PlanHasErrors. With no pending writes it returns all elements unchanged without invoking the writer. AdjustmentWriter selects RequiresModification rows, sorts columns by ID, and applies beams in graph order followed by any omitted beams in ID order. One ERFT Apply Adjustments transaction performs: Purge recognized legacy ERFT entities. Obtain and validate the element schema. Set column FAMILY_TOP_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM. Set beam STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END0_ELEVATION and STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END1_ELEVATION. Tag changed elements and save the system snapshot in DataStorage. Missing elements/parameters, read-only or wrong-storage parameters, and a false Set result fail apply. Offset, tag, and storage writes must all succeed or the transaction rolls back. After commit, changed rows become NoChangeNeeded. Cancellation propagates. Expected FramingAdjustmentFailureException becomes a structured result. Other exceptions retain their chain and reach the safe-execution boundary. Storage formats Features/Persistence/StorageSchema/Revit/StorageSchema defines public-read/public-write String fields: Schema GUID Fields DBTools_ERFT_V2 C736C6F5-34C8-4E50-A890-E5420C3E5391 Tag, SystemId, MemberRole, OriginalOffset, Timestamp DBTools_ERFT_System_V2 06C087B9-DA5B-4E3B-9496-13C7C8732B0E SystemIdString, DataJson Vendor is DBTools. Element Tag is ERFT, MemberRole is Column or Beam, and Timestamp is UTC round-trip text. OriginalOffset contains an invariant number for columns or start;end invariant numbers for beams. Lookup validates schema name and required simple String fields before use. Apply removes legacy element entities at B2C3D4E5-F6A7-4B8C-9D0E-1F2A3B4C5D6E and legacy system entities at C3D4E5F6-A7B8-4C9D-0E1F-2A3B4C5D6E7F only when vendor/name identify DBTools_ERFT or DBTools_ERFT_System respectively. It deletes an emptied DataStorage carrier and logs removals. Foreign registrations under those GUIDs remain untouched and log a warning. Legacy entities are removed rather than migrated. This cleanup shares the apply transaction. SystemPlanRepository.Save(Document, StoredPlan) and Load(Document, systemId) return structured failures for expected missing/duplicate/incompatible storage states. Duplicate records for a system fail explicitly. Unexpected Revit repository faults log the system ID and propagate. StoredPlan serializes target IDs/name, ToleranceFeet, RoundingMode, Columns, Beams, SystemId, and Timestamp. Stored columns retain ElementId, OriginalTopOffsetFeet, NewTopOffsetFeet, and AppliedDeltaFeet. Stored beams retain ElementId, original/new endpoint offsets, and applied endpoint deltas. CreateSnapshot includes rows with Pending status before the writer changes statuses after commit. It does not store geometry or profiles. StoredPlanMapper.Deserialize requires serialized tolerance, mode, both collections, and SystemId. Both collections and every member must be non-null. Element IDs must be positive. SystemId must be nonblank and match the DataStorage key ignoring case. A positive host target or a positive link-instance/linked-target pair is required. Tolerance must be positive and rounding mode defined. No schema-version migration participates in admission. Null display name or timestamp normalizes to empty text. Failure code Condition Storage/EmptyPayload Blank JSON Storage/InvalidJson Malformed JSON or missing required serialized members Storage/NullPayload JSON null Storage/IncompatiblePayload Invalid collection/member identity, tolerance, or enum Storage/SystemIdMissing Blank payload SystemId Storage/SystemIdMismatch Record key and payload disagree Storage/TargetMissing No positive target identity Contextual edit App/Composition/ErftContextualRibbonInjector adapts Core's contextual ribbon runtime. It targets Modify tabs for Structural Columns, Structural Framing, Multi-Select, Multi, or Multi-Category. Eligible selected elements have a supported category, compatible V2 entity, Tag ERFT, and a SystemId. Selection evaluation logs only when (hasErftElements, systemCount, buttonCount) changes. Missing-schema logging occurs once until a schema becomes available again. Selection-hook safe execution suppresses start/completion noise and banners. Edit clicks require a system ID, an initialized ExternalEvent, and an Accepted raise result. The event executes through ISafeExecutor with ErrorOnly notification and an owned InlineUi App run scope. Multiple systems use the system selector. The repository loads the chosen system. A failed repository load logs its code/context and shows this banner before returning: Cannot edit the selected ERFT system because stored plan data is missing or invalid. {Error.Tag} The banner retains the repository failure tag. Edit does not enter new-flow selection. The scope resolves FramingAdjustmentWorkflow and clears its current RevitRunScope before disposal. EditReconstructionBuilder resolves stored source IDs and reads current geometry/offsets. Partially missing sources produce diagnostics and permit remaining sources. No resolvable sources prevents reconstruction. EditReconstructionValidator rejects nonpositive tolerance and undefined modes with Edit/InvalidStoredTolerance or Edit/InvalidStoredRoundingMode. Reconstruction retains SystemId and stored rounding settings, then recomputes adjustments against the target. Re-apply uses current offsets, rather than adding a stored applied delta again. Failure and test boundaries FramingAdjustmentFailure carries expected codes, messages, and context, formatted with [SpecFail/*] tags. These results represent expected contract failures, not every runtime exception. Unexpected selection, material inspection, extraction, cleanup, reconstruction, repository, and apply failures propagate with context. Cancellation is not converted to failed data. Pure tests exercise TargetSurfaceProjector, FramingGraphBuilder, AdjustmentEvaluator, RoundingEvaluator, storage mapper/field validation, preview building/projection, selection rules, and window behavior. The hosted FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests fixture exercises real beams and columns against transient host floors in gm_test_model.rvt. It checks calculation, offset writes, element tags, and DataStorage inside rolled-back groups. Its Revit 2027 regression case checks legacy-schema cleanup without saving 2027/Regression/realtest_model.rvt. Linked-target acceptance needs additional hosted coverage.

developer-guide/tools/structural/erft.ht.title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/erft.ht.summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) ERFT adjusts host structural column and beam offsets to follow a host or linked floor/roof bottom surface. It preserves level associations, previews calculated changes, and applies offsets and storage in one transaction. See the technical specification for geometry, rounding, storage, and failure contracts. Use Run Extreme Roof Framing on the Testing panel. Pick a linked floor or roof. Press Esc to switch to host target selection. Pick a host target if needed. Esc at this stage cancels launch. Select source columns and beams, then Finish. Review the target, comparison rows, tolerance, and preview. Apply when the tolerance is valid, at least one row requires modification, and no row has Error status. Sources must be point-based structural columns or straight non-brace framing in the host document. Material names matching \bconcrete\b case-insensitively exclude members. The source set needs a column or a beam that connects to a model column under ERFT's hierarchy rule. Unsupported extracted sources fail launch rather than disappearing from the plan. Edit ERFT on contextual Modify tabs restores a selected system's stored plan and settings. Missing or incompatible storage fails edit launch. Re-pick hides the window with HideForPick, selects another target, and reuses the same shell and preview presenter with the rebuilt plan. Re-applying calculates from current model geometry and offsets. During apply, a second Apply or Re-pick request is ignored. Cancel and window close are blocked. A successful apply reports its result and closes the window. An expected apply failure keeps the window open. A thrown apply exception closes the window and propagates to safe execution. Escape clears both comparison-grid selections and does not close the window. Cancel has no WPF IsCancel route. Clicking an empty area of either grid with any mouse button clears both selections. See the alert and preview contracts for event severity, ownership, and validation. Ownership Source: src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. The manifest registers DBTools.ERFT, module DBTools.ERFT.App.Composition.ErftToolModule, and command/availability DBTools.ERFT.App.Composition.ErftNewCommand. The command uses InlineUi, icon key erft, and order 60 on the Testing panel. Owner Responsibility App/Composition Command, module, registration, contextual ribbon adapter App/Sessions/WindowSession Modal shell, alerts, banners, and lifetime App/ViewModels Tolerance, row selection, commands, and binding state App/Views/ErftWindow.xaml Raw embedded view Features/Domain Plan values, target projection, and framing graph Features/Selection Source rules, diagnostics, and Revit pickers Features/Operations Revit column, beam, target-geometry, and member-profile readers Features/Planning Preparation, edit reconstruction, target re-pick, adjustment, and rounding Features/Execution Apply orchestration and Revit writer Features/Persistence JSON, schemas, and system DataStorage repository Features/Preview Domain meshes and stable scene projection Features/State/AdjustmentPlanStore Current plan state Features/Workflow/FramingAdjustmentWorkflow New/edit/re-pick/apply interaction through feature-owned IWindowSession Feature decisions remain behind IWindowSession and WindowSessionAction. App implements their typed presentation methods. ERFT production has no dependency on another tool. A missing active document returns Failed before opening the window. The per-run DI scope owns and disposes WindowSession on every exit path. The workflow does not dispose it. Normal-close cleanup diagnostics belong to the shared window host. ERFT logs failures from its own close-and-retire release path without replacing the caller's primary failure. The shell explicitly sets the title Extreme Roof Framing Tool and loads the raw EmbeddedResource DBTools.ToolViews.ERFT.ErftWindow.xaml. The view merges its theme directly and uses the stable string-based EnumMatchConverter for rounding radio buttons. Preview PreviewSceneBuilder creates target and member meshes. PreviewProjector maps them into StructuralScene3D snapshots. DBTools.Presentation.StructuralPreview owns device lifetime, camera state, navigation, hit testing, hover tooltips, emphasis, outlines, target crease edges, and cleanup. DBTools.Presentation.Tools.ERFT.ErftPreviewOptions chooses the preserve-angle camera and fit-as-Home policy. The initial look direction is parallel to (0, 20, -10), with Z up. The camera home angle does not derive from the target mesh. Scene bounds include every rendered mesh vertex. Geometry updates within unchanged bounds preserve Home. Changed bounds fit the scene at the current angle and capture a new Home. Zoom to Fit also replaces Home and the viewport's default camera. Re-pick retains the current angle rather than constructing a new camera. Hover text uses the themed WPF ToolTip with a 16-pixel cursor offset. Member identities use element:<ElementId> and connect preview clicks to comparison rows. Targets are non-pickable context. Empty-space clicks clear row selection. Target hover does not replace member tooltips. Selected members use cyan emphasis and a 1.6-pixel all-edge outline. Target fill opacity is 0.12. Target and member edges use the palette’s cyan-gray color. The stable presenter owns lighting and camera bounds constraints. Status remains visible while the scene prepares or degrades. Navigation buttons disable when no scene exists. Both grids use a final stretch Status column with a minimum width. Thrown zoom/reset exceptions log a warning and appear in the preview status line. Fit failures log a diagnostic; reset without a Home attempts Zoom to Fit. A projection failure clears the rendered scene and shows its cause until the scene changes or the presenter becomes unavailable. Without a specific reason, the placeholder reads 3D Preview is unavailable: the presenter is unavailable. A graphics-device or WPF D3DImage failure permanently disables the presenter for that window. StructuralPreviewDevice releases resources once and does not forward Reinitialize to the native effects manager. It does not substitute WARP for the D3DImage bridge. The placeholder asks the user to update the graphics driver or enable GPU acceleration and reopen the tool. Preview navigation disables, but adjustment, Apply, Cancel, and target re-pick remain available outside an active apply. Re-pick retains the unavailable presenter and does not retry graphics initialization. Profile extraction reports expected unsupported geometry per type. The preview can show only the target when no profiles succeed. Unexpected geometry, transaction, cleanup, or cancellation faults propagate. One Info summary records total/extracted/unsupported counts. Per-type progress is Debug. Selection-hook logs suppress per-event start/completion banners and report evaluation changes only when state changes. Tests Pure tests cover graph construction, target projection, adjustment/rounding, storage admission, scene projection, window selection, close gating, modal lifetime, and injected device creation failure during re-pick and Apply. Core tests exercise presenter recovery and resource release without a GPU. Presentation's hosted StructuralPreview3DTests covers fit-as-Home through the renderer. Hosted FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests uses gm_test_model.rvt and transient host floors with real beam and column instances. It covers seed viability, target extraction, calculation, offset writes, tags, and DataStorage inside rolled-back transaction groups. A Revit 2027 regression case checks legacy-schema cleanup on 2027/Regression/realtest_model.rvt without saving the model. These cases do not establish linked-target coverage. ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects DBTools.ERFT.Local.Tests -y 2026 ./test.sh test --tool ERFT --scope local -y 2026 --fixture FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests

developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.title: Foundation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.summary: Foundation Tags Foundation Tags updates pier/footing association parameters and moves combined tags to footing corners. Source: src/Tools/Structural/FoundationTags/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.FoundationTags. Commands Ribbon command Identity Split-button order Update Combined Foundation Tags DBTools.UpdateCombinedFoundationTags 0 Move Combined Tags DBTools.MoveCombinedFoundationTags 1 Both use InlineUi on the Structural panel in split group foundation_tags. Their command and availability classes are UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsCommand and MoveCombinedFoundationTagsCommand under App/Composition. Icon keys are update_combined and move_combined. Organize Foundation Types occupies order 2 in the same group. Update Features/CombinedFoundationTagsUpdater collects visible FamilyInstance elements from the active view. Configured family patterns classify piers and footings. Updates affect host-document instances. Compute each pier's top as Top Level elevation plus Top Offset. Write Foundation Pier Top by GUID. Find the nearest pier to each footing using XY location points, within two feet inclusive. Write that pier's type mark to Associated Pier and its top to Associated Pier Elevation. Publish current-run result IDs and timestamped selection sets. A missing or invalid Top Level records a pier failure. Missing Top Offset uses zero. Piers without LocationPoint cannot participate in nearest-point matching. Equal-distance ties retain the first candidate. Without a pier, the updater clears the association text to an empty string. It keeps a stored elevation and reports failure because these length parameters cannot be cleared. Parameter.ClearValue requires HideWhenNoValue, which the shipped definitions do not set. An elevation without a stored value needs no clearing. Double writes compare values rounded to two decimal places in internal feet. String comparison is ordinal. UpdateParameterWriter returns failures for missing, read-only, wrong-storage, or rejected parameter writes. The updater records these failures and continues. A footing can appear in both Modified and Failed sets when one parameter changes and another fails. Unexpected exceptions escape the parameter transaction and roll back the run. Parameter writes and selection-set publication use separate transactions inside one transaction group. The group assimilates to one Undo entry. A selection-set failure preserves committed parameter writes, then propagates after assimilation. Other failures attempt group rollback and preserve concurrent cleanup faults. UpdateRunResult contains UpdatedCount, FailedCount, and read-only snapshots of Modified and Failed IDs. The manual workflow offers Select Modified and Select Skipped when updates exist. Those banner actions check that the source document is still active before selecting IDs. With no updates, it shows an Info or Warning toast without selection actions. Selection sets use DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (...) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (...) names with Eastern-time timestamps. Repeated names receive suffixes starting at (2). Pruning retains five sets across both kinds, ordered by descending element ID. Move Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsRunner collects visible IndependentTag instances, resolves a tagged host or linked structural foundation, and filters tag family/type names by the configured patterns. Only the host tag moves. Linked footing geometry transforms into host coordinates. The desired name is the trimmed tag name, or its type name when the tag name is blank. Supported values are case-insensitive Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right, and Bottom Left. The runner tessellates fine-detail footing geometry, including nonvisible objects, in the instance's local frame. Local XY extents define four rectangular corners. FoundationTagsGeometry.SelectCornerByViewOrientation labels them against the view's RightDirection and UpDirection. The edge most aligned with view-right becomes horizontal. A tie uses the second declared edge. The tag retains its current Z. Unsupported names, missing point locations, and geometry without usable corners are skips. All candidate moves share DB Tools - Move Combined Foundation Tags. Unexpected transform, geometry, tessellation, or tag-write errors log the tag ID and propagate, rolling back every move. MoveRunResult separates moved, skipped, candidate, total-view-tag, structural-foundation, and pattern-rejection counts, with rejected-name samples for diagnostics. Prerequisites and repair Manual commands and automatic updates validate shared parameters without modifying them. The required definitions are owned by Features/Prerequisite/PrerequisiteRequiredParameters: Parameter GUID Type Instance category Initial group Associated Pier 7f6c2c2a-46ab-4e78-9bf6-9b9c2ef8f7d1 Text Structural Foundation Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation 6d9b0f7f-4f7a-44a4-9c5c-0c0f4bf0da21 Length Structural Foundation Identity Data Foundation Pier Top 93de44b8-bb7c-4e58-a7e0-9a3a1c8e4d70 Length Structural Columns Constraints Invalid prerequisites activate core.structural.combined_tags and refuse manual commands with SafeExecutionRefusedException. Safe execution shows a Warning banner and logs a Warning without a stack. Unexpected validation faults remain errors and do not assert invalid prerequisites. Use Settings → Combined Foundation Tags → Refresh to inspect the active document. Use Fix (Install/Repair) or Install/Repair Required Parameters to repair it. Construction of the settings context is passive and shows a Refresh prompt. SettingsRuntime receives the settings host's UIApplication explicitly. It creates a temporary shared-parameter file, restores Revit's original shared-parameter path, and attempts temporary-file deletion. No startup deployment is required. Repair deletes conflicting definitions with the same required name and a different GUID, including duplicate-name collisions. It preserves other categories and the existing group when extending a binding. An instance binding already containing the required category remains unchanged. A type binding becomes an instance binding with its existing categories plus the required category. Revit drops the type values and the installer logs a Warning naming the parameter. The updater accesses these parameters by GUID. The warning disables Update, Move, and Organize Foundation Types. Its title is Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. Clear it after resolving the prerequisite issue. PrerequisiteRetryCoordinator retains each original event source and detach callback. Evaluation faults log and can be checked again on the next view activation. The monitor disposes its own retry coordinator at synchronous App shutdown. An injected coordinator remains caller-owned. Disposed lifetimes reject scheduling. Failed-detach entries retain cleanup state without retry work. A late Idling event can retry detachment. Settings Configuration section: Tools.FoundationTags. developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.title: Framing Joins | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.summary: Framing Joins Framing Joins allows or disallows joins at both ends of selected structural framing instances. The tool has no persistent settings. Commands Command Manifest identity Operation Allow Join DBTools.AllowJoinSelected Calls StructuralFramingUtils.AllowJoinAtEnd for ends 0 and 1 Disallow Join DBTools.DisallowJoinSelected Calls StructuralFramingUtils.DisallowJoinAtEnd for ends 0 and 1 Both commands use InlineUi and the Structural panel's framing_joins split button. Their manifest order is 0 and 1, respectively. The icon keys are allow_join and disallow_join. Availability uses CommandAvailability.HasStructuralFramingSelection. Select structural framing elements. Run Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the completion banner for the processed instance count. Execution App/Composition/AllowJoinSelectedCommand and DisallowJoinSelectedCommand resolve Features/FramingJoinsWorkflow through their CommandService registration. The workflow receives ITransactionRunner, ILoggerWindowHost, a window-owner provider, and a typed logger through dependency injection. The workflow reads the current selection, filters by OST_StructuralFraming, removes duplicate IDs, and retains only elements that resolve to FamilyInstance. An empty selection or a selection without usable framing instances produces SafeExecutionRefusedException. FramingJoinTargetBuilder owns the category filter. FramingJoinsWorkflow.ExecuteCore owns the endpoint loop. All targets run in one transaction named DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. The count increases after both endpoint calls succeed. It counts processed instances, including instances whose join state already matches the request. An endpoint failure logs the exception and element ID, then throws InvalidOperationException with the original cause. The transaction rolls back the complete batch. A successful batch shows a six-second completion toast and ensures the logger window when Debug Mode is enabled. Source and tests The implementation and manifest are under src/Tools/Structural/FramingJoins/. The project references Core and the Revit API. Pure fixtures FramingJoinTargetBuilderTests and FramingJoinsWorkflowTests cover filtering and endpoint execution. Hosted fixtures FramingJoinsCommandTests and FramingJoinsWorkflowRevitTests cover command and Revit integration.

developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.title: Joist Girder Weight | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.summary: Joist Girder Weight Joist Girder Weight estimates pounds per linear foot and writes the result to a writable Double parameter named Wt. It scans structural framing in the active document. The ribbon command runs manually. A view-activation task runs automatically when enabled. Inputs The configured regex tests the family name. It tests the type name only when the family name is blank. The default family pattern is: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ It matches G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder, and Vulcraft Joist Girder. Input Resolution Constraint Number of joists Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Greater than 1 Span Cut Length, Length Positive internal feet Depth Depth Positive internal feet Load Total/point load, or dead plus live load Nonnegative kips Output Wt Writable Double on the instance or type Numeric aliases are checked in the listed order, with instance then type lookup for each name. Load resolution prefers instance parameters over same-named type parameters. It rejects multiple populated matches in any Total, Dead, or Live group, even when a Total value exists. One Total value takes precedence over Dead plus Live. Without Total, exactly one Dead and one Live are required. Force-typed Double values convert from Revit internal units to kips. Unitless numeric values are kips. Text uses invariant numeric parsing and accepts these units: Units Conversion to kips Omitted, k, kip, kips Unchanged lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds Divide by 1000 kN, case-insensitive Multiply by 0.2248089431 Examples are 10, 10 kips, 10000 lb, and 45 kN. Blank, negative, malformed, or unsupported-unit text produces an input issue. Formula Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightEvaluator.EstimateWeight(n, load, lengthFeet, depthFeet) returns lb/ft. The calculation converts length and depth to inches. panelSpacing = lengthInches / n numberOfPanels = n - 1 totalReaction = loadKips * numberOfPanels / 2 maxMoment = totalReaction * lengthInches / 2 For even n, subtract loadKips * panelSpacing * i for integer steps starting at 1 while i < numberOfPanels / 2. For odd n, subtract loadKips * (panelSpacing / 2 + panelSpacing * j) starting at 0 while j < numberOfPanels / 2. effectiveDepth = depthInches * 0.95 chordForce = maxMoment / effectiveDepth requiredArea = chordForce / (50.0 * 0.6) topChordWeight = requiredArea * lengthInches * 0.28356 * 1.06 bottomChordWeight = topChordWeight * 1.13 webWeight = topChordWeight * 0.7 weightPoundsPerFoot = (topChordWeight + bottomChordWeight + webWeight) / lengthFeet 50.0 is the stress constant in ksi. 0.28356 is steel density in lb/in³. The remaining constants are depth, connection, and member multipliers. This is one estimation formula. It does not select manufacturer sections or validate SJI load tables. Update and failure behavior JoistGirderWeightUpdater validates candidates and computes weights before opening a transaction. Invalid candidates become skipped items. Valid candidates share Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. An unexpected transaction or setter exception propagates and rolls back that transaction. The updater calls Parameter.Set without checking its Boolean result. The returned summary contains Candidates, Updated, Skipped, and up to five sample issues. Zero candidates returns an empty summary. All-invalid candidates return skipped counts. The manual workflow displays an Info toast when nothing updates, Warning for mixed updated/skipped results, and Success when all candidates update. Configuration exceptions produce a ten-second Warning toast. Automatic execution catches configuration exceptions, sets the configured warning, and shows a banner. Other runtime faults propagate to Core's view-activation handling. Warning core.structural.joist_girder disables DBTools.UpdateJoistGirderWeights and automatic updates. Settings Configuration section: Tools.JoistGirderWeight. Pack key: structural.joist_girder_weight, titled Joist Girder Weights. Property Persisted default Effective default AutoUpdateEnabled true true FamilyNamePattern Empty string Family pattern above DeadLoadPattern Empty string (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) LiveLoadPattern Empty string (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) TotalLoadPattern Empty string (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) For example, the Total pattern matches Point Load, Panel Point Load, Total Load, and Total Load - User Defined. Features/DefaultPatterns owns defaults. Settings/SettingsPackContext derives from SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<JoistGirderWeightSettings> and owns pattern editing, empty-value defaulting, regex validation, snapshots, and baseline comparison. The Core base owns the toggle, warning, pending-change, and notification state. Ownership and registration Source: src/Tools/Structural/JoistGirderWeight/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/JoistGirderWeightToolModule Module, settings pack, hooks, and warning registration App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions Dependency registration App/Composition/UpdateJoistGirderWeightsCommand Manual command Features/Workflow/WeightUpdateWorkflow Settings retrieval, update, completion/configuration banners Features/AutoUpdate/AutoUpdateTask View-activation execution Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderClassifier Family and load-name classification Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightUpdater Revit collection, validation, and writes Features/Load/Operations/ElementLoadReader Parameter and unit resolution Features/Load/LoadParser Text parsing Features/Load/LoadResolutionEvaluator Load group ambiguity and precedence Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightEvaluator Pure formula Features/JoistGirder/Settings/Views/JoistGirderWeightSettingsView.xaml Settings view manifest.yml registers assembly DBTools.JoistGirderWeight and module DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.App.Composition.JoistGirderWeightToolModule. The command uses InlineUi, icon key joist_girder, and ribbon order 30. The asset is Assets/joist_girder_icon.png. developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.summary: Organize Foundation Types Organize Foundation Types renames foundation family types, assigns type marks, and merges types with equal dimensions. It processes all matching types in the active document. It does not use the current selection or persistent settings. Families and parameters Family names match exactly with ordinal comparison. Family Category Dimensions Prefix Sort order Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P b * h Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Diameter Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Width, length, thickness Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Width, length, thickness All sorts are ascending. Dimensions use Double parameters. Type marks use the String parameter Type Mark. Production dimension text comes from Revit's feet-and-fractional-inches formatter. Missing dimension parameters display ?. Duplicate keys use the nullable raw dimension values, so types with the same missing dimensions can also compare equal. Marks and names Family group Mark format Name format Example Rectangular pier P-{n}, starting at 1 {b}x{h} ({mark}) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Round pier RP-{n}, starting at 1 {d} DIA. ({mark}) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing or pile cap {prefix}-{widthFeet}.{n}, starting at 0 {width}x{length}x{thickness} ({mark}) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) widthFeet is the floor of the width in internal feet. Each family group maintains its own ordinal set of marks encountered during processing. Generation searches from the starting counter for an unused mark in that set. It does not reserve marks on types that have not yet been processed. The confirmation asks whether to overwrite existing marks. Yes selects TypeMarkPolicy.OverwriteExistingTypeMarks. No selects PreserveExistingTypeMarks. Preserve mode generates marks only for blank values, but still renames types and merges duplicates. SetParam leaves a missing, non-String, or read-only Type Mark unchanged, so a generated name does not guarantee a mark write. Processing and transactions Collect and sort the four family groups. Compare each type's dimension tuple with retained types in its group. For a duplicate, reassign its instances to the retained type. For a retained type, assign its mark when permitted and rename it. Delete successfully merged source types after processing the group. The first successfully retained type for a dimension tuple becomes the merge target. Dimension comparison is exact. Each rename/mark operation and duplicate reassignment runs through a nested transaction-runner call. A failed reassignment rolls back that type's changes and records a skip. The organizer deletes a duplicate only after all its instances change type. All groups share the outer DB Tools - Organize Foundation Types transaction. A deletion error logs at Error and propagates, rolling back the complete operation. Per-type failures log at Debug and increment the skip count. The final warning and completion alert include skipped totals and up to five type id: reason samples. The alert also reports renamed and merged counts. Registration and ownership Source: src/Tools/Structural/OrganizeFoundationTypes/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/OrganizeFoundationTypesCommand Manifest command, active-document availability Features/FoundationType/OrganizeFoundationTypesWorkflow Confirmation, organizer invocation, completion alert, Debug logger window Features/FoundationType/FoundationTypeOrganizer Collection, dimension comparison, rename, merge, deletion Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkGenerator Mark generation and pure formatting helper Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkPolicy Preserve or overwrite mode manifest.yml registers DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes as an InlineUi split-button item in foundation_tags, order 2, icon key organize_types. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags occupy orders 0 and 1. The structural.foundation_tags pack's core.structural.combined_tags warning disables all three commands. A typical documentation workflow runs this organizer, then Update Combined Foundation Tags, then Move Combined Tags. Tests Pure TypeMarkGeneratorTests covers sequential numbering, gaps, width groups, prefixes, and invalid arguments. Hosted OrganizeFoundationTypesTests covers confirmation, completion reporting, duplicate merges, and document changes inside a rolled-back fixture transaction group.

Revit-free session construction remains under App/Sessions; live-plan synchronization is App state under App/State/PlanSynchronization, not session infrastructure. Feature Contracts Change Review session contract Features/ChangeReview is a raw-XAML child hosted by the existing ToolWindowFactory/ToolWindowHost path. Its view-model and workflow are session-owned; no static stores candidate state or subscribes to a Revit event. The workflow compares one synchronized plan revision with one live snapshot, then analyzes a confirmed candidate before publishing the detached plan and ledger. Accept, Keep, and Ignore are the only decision vocabulary. ChangeReviewPlanBuilder is the one decision authority: it resolves each item's decision once and derives both the candidate plan and the ledger Confirm saves; rows display the resolved decision. Its AllowedDecisions is the allowed-decision matrix and ProposeDecision the one default rule: the dialog offers the matrix's decisions (SetInvalidated removes Ignore for a released user-created opening unless Ignore is already selected) and preselects an allowed proposal, and the builder applies a proposal to an undecided item that needs no attention only when the matrix allows it. An explicit Ignore returns a Placed opening to its Placed framing configuration, held, even when the draft carries a local edit; an opening that was never placed stays unframed, and a later Keep frames a never-placed manual opening again. Without a live observation a row offers only Keep and Ignore. The live snapshot carries the grid crossings along the Placed wall and the observed wall, and girt grid anchors resolve against the grids of the wall the review adopts. Review rows show the opening source name (or Manual opening for an unnamed detached manual row), source, status, and decision; effects appear in the selected row's details pane. Placement validation messages include the along-wall range when it is relevant. The canonical key is never user-facing. The parent session owns the one TransactionGroup named Super Girt Tool. Review Confirm saves the decision ledger inside that group without changing framing. Place, Update, Delete System, and Deconstruct run ordinary transactions inside that group. A successful window close assimilates once; Cancel, an error, native close failure, or forced retirement rolls back once. A relink child is retired in finally, and active review-to-pick re-entry remains in the same synchronous modal driver. Unsupported SGT storage is purged, including its owned element tags, inside that group so the same close decision governs the purge. The release acceptance uses real Revit commands, model elements, tags, and reloaded storage. Pure tests prove decision/evaluator transitions and relink pairing; RevitLocal tests prove physical placement/update/removal, target occupancy, unsupported-data purge, rollback after multiple inner writes, and the single Super Girt Tool Undo result. No test substitutes a fake transaction or Undo-history counter for the operator's Revit evidence. UI synchronization maps only those typed failures to banners and must leave plan-store and preview state unchanged. Argument errors, cancellation, and unexpected runtime faults propagate with their original identity. Transactional Revit storage/model-write boundaries retain exception unwinding where rollback requires it. TemporaryTransactionRunner records operation, accessor, and rollback failures before diagnostics. Snapshot and rollback logging failures join that list in attempt order, so logging cannot replace the probe or rollback cause. A lone operation failure keeps its original exception identity. Placement command execution preserves the safe-execution status as one explicit result. Update success/cancellation closes the window, and update failure requests a rollback close; removal success clears the system and closes, while rejection/failure/cancellation retains it. Every removal result requests exactly one reactive preview refresh. Features/Orientation/Revit/Analysis owns orientation analysis against Revit families and its solver inputs; portable math/results remain in Features/Orientation/Analysis; WallAnalysis consumes the named FramingTypeOrientationAnalysisResult data result while progress remains status-only. Features/WallAnalysis/Domain owns the plan-builder port and Features/WallAnalysis/Revit/Planning owns wall analysis, calibration, target-geometry resolution, profile warming, seeding, and plan construction against the selected Revit wall. Calibration checks cancellation before validation and cache access, treats argument defects as argument exceptions, converts typed SpecFailureException failures to results, and caches only successes. Family calibration is a per-family preflight that logs a failed family and continues; each type of that family carries the typed failure, with family and type names, as a per-role orientation failure. The orientation analyzer throws SpecFailureException for expected family incompatibilities, and WallAnalysisFramingTypeAnalyzer converts them per role. WallGeometryBuilder converts typed frame failures for host and linked frames at one boundary. Cancellation, rollback failures, and invariant defects propagate after contextual logging. App/session workflow owns command-level orchestration. New and edit plan builders apply the same admission rules before returning success. Admission rejects invalid configurations with PlanValidationFailed before plan-store publication. Edit analysis rehydrates stored values and analyzes current wall geometry. The session workflow owns UI reconciliation. Initial seeding belongs only to PlanSeedingStep. Post-analysis App feedback reads existing row counts and never seeds or republishes a plan. No-opening feedback is suppressed for foundation mode. The initial preview completion barrier remains required. Total profile-warming failure retains the first five type-specific causes, ordered by numeric type ID, and the omitted count. Its failure code remains ProfileLoopsAllFailed. Partial-success warnings and cancellation behavior are unchanged. Features/BulkEdit owns the bulk-edit flyout workflow, centered on BulkEditFlyoutViewModel and its partial family. Bulk apply mutates girt and opening rows under both reactive-sync suppressions. After a successful commit, the girt owner refreshes selected rows' Flip capability and option lists while still suppressed and clears a previous type-change preview blocker only if its own row now has valid orientation. Opening-only edits and failed applies do not dismiss that blocker. One UI-edit preview refresh then synchronizes the committed rows to the plan. A failed apply restores its row snapshots and reports one bulk error without projecting transient edits. Collapsed segment-group deletion and undo each publish one accepted plan revision: row mutation, saved group metadata restoration on undo, and renumbering execute inside the same PlanStore.Update. Undo refuses a group changed after deletion without overwriting its later edits; the window keeps the editing session open, warns the operator, and clears stale edit history. Tool-Wide Contracts Contract family Owner Revit-free entities, rules, geometry, wall/opening/orientation semantics Domain/; GirtPlanRow is the plan-member row under Domain/Girt, FamilyOrientation is under Domain/Orientation, and wall mode/face/execution context are under Domain/Wall Mutable live plan, baseline snapshot, clone/sandbox behavior, and store port Domain/Plans Generic plan editing and runtime/read projections Domain/PlanEditing, Domain/Plans/Projection; PlanProjectionMapper alone converts girt plan rows and runtime member configs Live plan store, hashes, and UI-to-plan synchronization Domain/PlanStore, App/State/PlanSynchronization Private storage transport, repository contract, schema, and serialization admission Persistence/ Revit Extensible Storage adapter Persistence/Revit/SystemRepository.cs Cross-feature Revit adapters Revit/ App-only UI settings persistence App/Persistence/ PlanStore.Initialize prepares and validates a candidate before replacing the live plan or advancing its revision. Rejected reinitialization preserves the accepted plan and sends no change event; a successful admission publishes one initialized event after the lock is released. Plan admission rejects duplicate member keys before a candidate becomes the live plan. Segment deletion undo relies on that identity invariant when matching surviving group rows against its applied snapshot. Key fidelity names are domain GirtPlanRow with MemberKey, feature GirtRowViewModel with UI-only MemberId, girt-grid GirtTypeItem, inward FramingTypeOption, RangeMath, and WallFramingMode. GirtTypeItem and FramingTypeOption expose matching TypeId values. The wall-layer contract is split one type per file: WallLayer.cs, WallLayerCollection.cs, and WallLayerFunction.cs. Dependency Facts The baseline projection direction is inward: Features and App may use Domain/Plans/Projection/PlanBaselineMapper, which captures a Plan as PlanBaselineSnapshot and restores the editable desired plan from that snapshot plus PlacedSystem. Girt rows come from the stored girt members through PlanProjectionMapper; opening rows and wall geometry come from Placed; the runtime collections are derived from those rows, and the stored snapshot is retained in Plan.BaselineSnapshot. Edit startup reads one live snapshot, lets Change Review apply remembered decisions, and then the registered edit builder analyzes that desired plan against the current target. Persistence separately owns PlanData transport/admission in SystemStorageMapper.Plan.cs, plus StoredSystem, ISystemRepository, and the Revit repository adapter. Features do not depend on Persistence for pure baseline projection, and Persistence does not import App. At the broader tool boundary, Domain has no dependency on App, Features, Persistence, CommunityToolkit, ObservableCollection, or WPF. Features have no App dependency. Feature-owned ports and behavior inputs are implemented or composed at the App/session boundary where needed. EndpointAssociationOpeningEdgeSide is the sole semantic opening-edge representation in Domain, Features, App state, and the persistence transport. Stable text conversion occurs only at actual serialization, UI-label, or cache-key boundaries. WallAnalysis may invoke Placement planning/model-write contracts while building an executable plan, but Placement has no WallAnalysis dependency. App/session composition depends on both and owns the analysis lifecycle; there is no Placement-to-WallAnalysis backedge. Project Surfaces DBTools.SGT.csproj owns both desktop and portable targets. Shared portable rules select inward code by layer, disable content identity and merging, and exclude desktop resources. SGT has no sandbox profile or production-source links. portable Pure: Tests/DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests.csproj references SGT directly for domain/features, plan-store, persistence, review-workflow, and preview-status behavior. desktop Pure: Tests/DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests.csproj references normal desktop SGT for WPF and session behavior. local/Revit: Tests/DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests.csproj references the owning projects and stages the desktop product. Review cancellation/relink stays in IChangeReviewOperation; desktop lifecycle composition binds App/Views/IChangeReviewDialogHost to the dialog constructor for child ownership. The presenter maps Presentation status to portable readiness/reason values. Raw XAML and the Windows test lane remain because these views need WPF. Test-only behavior and helpers remain under Tests/Support; they are not represented as production-owner mirrors. Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/Tests/DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests.csproj Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/DBTools.SGT.csproj Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/MAP.md Any future move must update source namespaces, XAML, manifest FQNs, project links/removes, test namespaces, Loader bridge output, App suppression targets, and the generated MAP in the same change. Persistence Shape Persistence/Revit/SystemRepository.cs is the repository implementation and Persistence/ISystemRepository.cs is its current contract. StoredSystem.cs, the private records in SystemStorageMapper.Data.cs, SystemStorageMapper*, and schema builders are co-owned there. Domain/Plans/Projection/PlanBaselineMapper.cs owns pure baseline capture and rehydration; SystemStorageMapper.Plan.cs owns only transport mapping and admission into the complete current PlanBaselineSnapshot contract. Runtime plan JSON is the private SystemData graph: OpeningDefinitionData, OpeningFrameData, OpeningFrameSpanData, MemberConfigData, MemberSpanData, and MemberSpanEndpointData carry the persisted opening/frame/member fields, then map into fresh Domain instances during admission. Nullable transport collections and entries are kept nullable so malformed storage is rejected by the mapper, not normalized by Domain constructors or clones. Current-shape validation is allowed; schema-version dispatch, legacy readers, compatibility forwarding, or Persistence-to-App imports are not. Persisted system-id schema and Revit tag values remain text; their single edit-launch conversion is fail-closed in App/Composition/ContextualEdit/ContextualEditHook.cs. Every SGT DataStorage must have a valid entity whose SystemIdString parses as a nonempty SystemId. Its name must exactly match GetDataStorageName(parsedSystemId) using ordinal comparison. A lookup also requires the parsed ID to equal the requested ID. Invalid entities, invalid IDs, and mismatched identities return typed failures. Each canonical storage name must identify exactly one row. Lookups reject duplicate names before reading or mutating either row. Save and Delete reject corrupt or ambiguous matching rows without changing them. GetAllSystemIds rejects invalid SGT-prefixed rows and duplicate system IDs instead of returning a partial or ambiguous list. ISystemRepository.Exists returns Result<bool, SpecFailure> to distinguish absence from corrupt storage. A missing schema or system remains a typed Load failure. Exists returns false when no matching row exists. Deleting a missing row succeeds. Enumeration is empty when the schema or rows are absent. Cancellation and unexpected Revit faults continue to propagate. Revit family/type/instance identities remain long from API conversion through plan state, caches, projections, selection, and storage. FamilyTypeId.Value, framing option IDs, selected plan IDs, member type IDs, and placement update IDs follow this contract. Existing JSON field names and ordinary positive integer tokens remain valid. Counts, indexes, rotations, category enums, manual-opening surrogates, and geometry face indexes remain 32-bit. Geometry face indexes must not be treated as document element identities. Verification Anchors The structural acceptance gates are: generated MAP consistency (.agents/work/canon_source_maps.py --check); manifest-type validation (ValidateManifestTypes); CANON source fidelity, including the sibling-family and parent-cadence checks (.agents/work/canon_source_fidelity.py --gate). The pre-push hook runs all three; ValidatePrePush owns the manifest-type gate. The Loader bridge and MAP generators must be rerun after owner or front-door changes.
