developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.summary: SGT (Super Girt Tool) SGT is the structural wall-framing tool registered as DBTools.SGT. Its source is organized by runtime owner, not by the former Shell/ and Shared/ convenience buckets. Test lanes StartupTargetResolverTests is Revit-local. The host-free OpeningSynchronizationControllerTests, PreviewRefreshCoordinatorTests, and BulkEditFlyoutViewModelTests suites run in the Pure lane beside OpeningMemberExtentSnapTargetResolverTests; none occupies an Integration/Revit path or depends on a hosted-runner category merely for routing. Owner Layout src/Tools/Structural/SGT/ +-- App/ | +-- Composition/ | +-- Converters/ | +-- DesignTime/ | +-- Persistence/ | +-- Resources/ | +-- Sessions/ | | +-- TransactionGroup/ | | +-- ViewModels/ | | +-- WindowSession/Revit/ | | +-- Workflow/ | +-- Startup/ | +-- State/ | | +-- PlanSynchronization/ | +-- ViewModels/ | +-- Views/ +-- Domain/ | +-- Defaults/ | +-- FamilyResolution/ | +-- Geometry/ | +-- Identity/ | +-- MemberResolution/ | +-- Openings/ | | +-- Roles/ | +-- Orientation/ | +-- PlanEditing/ | +-- PlanStore/ | +-- Plans/ | | +-- Projection/ | +-- Wall/ | +-- WallTarget/ +-- Features/ | +-- BulkEdit/ | +-- Openings/ | +-- Orientation/ | +-- Placement/ | | +-- Domain/ | | +-- Execution/ | | +-- Girt/ | | +-- Orientation/ | | +-- Planning/ | | +-- Operations/ModelWrite/ | | +-- Revit/ | | | +-- ModelWrite/ | | +-- Workflow/ | +-- Preview/ | | +-- DesignTime/ | | +-- Domain/ | | +-- Editing/MemberResolution/Segmentation/ | | +-- Geometry/ | | +-- Handle/ | | +-- HitTesting/OpeningMember/ | | +-- Planning/ | | +-- Refresh/ | | +-- Rendering/ | | | +-- Scene3D/ | | +-- Selection/ | | +-- Snap/ | | +-- ViewModels/ | | +-- Views/{Geometry,Handle,HitTesting,Rendering,Selection,Snap,View2D,Viewport}/ | +-- WallAnalysis/ | +-- Domain/ | +-- Revit/ | +-- Geometry/ | +-- Planning/ +-- Persistence/ | +-- Revit/ +-- Revit/ +-- Tests/ +-- DBTools.SGT.csproj +-- manifest.yml The feature owners are Openings, Orientation, Placement, Preview, WallAnalysis, and BulkEdit. Preview-owned editing lives under Features/Preview/Editing. The remaining top-level owners have distinct responsibilities: App/ owns command/window composition, modal sessions, startup, the live plan-store implementation and UI refresh coordinator, UI-only persistence, whole-window XAML hosting, view models, converters, and design-time binding shapes. AddAppStateServices is the App-state registration entrypoint; WindowSessionBuilder directly composes the one window session, and its runtime state remains private to the window view model. Domain/ owns the required-target Plan aggregate, its IPlanStore port, PlanBaselineSnapshot, plan editing/projection, pure default/family resolution, and Revit-free wall/opening/orientation semantics. It has no dependency on App/, Features/, Persistence/, CommunityToolkit, or ObservableCollection. Persistence/ owns ISystemRepository, the private storage transport, current-contract admission and serialization mapping, and the Revit-backed SystemRepository under Persistence/Revit. It has no dependency on App/. Revit/ owns cross-feature Revit adapters that are not naturally owned by one feature. Features/ owns feature-specific contracts, workflows, row mutation, observable UI items/collections, and Revit adapters. Features do not reference App/. The generated SGT MAP is the current tracked folder and manifest-type index. Application Boundary manifest.yml binds the runtime front door in lockstep: module: DBTools.SGT.App.Composition.SgtToolModule command: DBTools.SGT.App.Composition.SgtCommand window: DBTools.SGT.App.Views.SgtWindow design-time view model: DBTools.SGT.App.DesignTime.SgtWindowDesignTimeViewModel (live Sandbox window consumer) App/Views/SgtWindow.xaml, PreviewView.xaml, OpeningView.xaml, and GirtView.xaml are raw EmbeddedResource views. The stable ToolWindowFactory owns the modal shell; SgtWindow is a payload composition object that supplies the view model, composes the three child raw elements, attaches the preview presenter, and releases the view graph through the host session. The payload contains no XAML code-behind or WPF-derived view type. The compiled design-time resource page was retired, while SgtWindowDesignTimeViewModel and SgtWindowSamplePopulator remain as the live Sandbox window's manifest-selected design-time model. FeetInchesConverter was removed because no runtime consumer remains. There is no ShellWindow compatibility type or namespace forwarder. The Sandbox creates the raw SgtWindow shell through its manifest entry and then invokes the stable ISgtSandboxViewComposer callback implemented by SgtWindowDesignTimeViewModel. The tool's SgtWindowRawViewComposer is shared by that callback and the live window, so the sample receives the same Girt, Openings, and Preview fragments, stable preview input behavior, and session-owned cleanup. The callback is declared in Presentation rather than Core because Sandbox and the candidate tool may use distinct host contexts while Presentation remains the stable WPF owner. Revit-hosted window tests use modeless Window.Show() with a bounded DispatcherDrain. SgtWindowSessionTests drives the real run scope through RunWindowFlowAsync and keeps transaction rollback, plan-target, preview, DataContext, and overlay-cleanup assertions. Windows Pure WindowSessionLifecycleTests uses the real modal host and watchdog. It proves same-window re-entry after a pick without depending on another ContentRendered event. App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionLifecycle.cs owns the lifecycle states, close intent, startup outcome, and finalization result. Its synchronous modal driver always returns a completed task because both production Revit command callers block immediately. A relink hides the window, executes the synchronous picker, then re-enters ShowDialog in the same command frame. One owned ContextIdle callback resumes target analysis after the window is visible. The driver rejects a modal return before the pick or shown handshake completes. It never posts modal re-entry. WindowSessionStartupAnalysis observes the current initial-analysis or target-analysis producer. A completed producer delivers inline. A pending producer delivers through one owned dispatcher operation while the modal frame remains active. Closing during analysis cancels analysis and keeps the window and transaction group alive until its outcome arrives. Retirement revokes the producer callbacks and aborts the operation. No custom awaiter, scheduler, or nested task chain owns shutdown. Forced retirement clears commit intent, releases payload resources, and publishes cancellation. If the synchronous picker is still on the stack, cancellation publication and transaction rollback wait until it returns; no target analysis or banner runs afterward. Ordinary Closed cleanup remains a distinct state and preserves an accepted commit. Native window and dispatcher references are captured before registration retirement. Transaction operations must complete through the inline Revit call gate, before the command returns. App/Sessions/WindowSession/Revit/SgtWindowSession.cs supplies Revit picking and startup, window resource effects, and error-boundary integration to the lifecycle owner. Its RunModalFlowAsync is the production entry point. New/edit launch flows use a closed WindowSessionLaunchRequest: New requires a concrete WallTarget, and Edit requires a nondefault SystemId. The builder requires an inline Revit call gate and rolls back construction failures with ordered cleanup. The command consumes only completed lifecycle tasks. Cosmetic UI-state persistence has its own context-free observer and never delays transaction finalization. Native X/Alt+F4 close reuses the WPF close already in progress. An active analysis delays close until its outcome settles. An accepted Closed releases mandatory preview/window resources and then finalizes the single owned Super Girt Tool transaction group inline. Successful close intent plus a healthy, successful session assimilates the group; Cancel, errors and forced retirement roll it back. SGT refuses an already-modifiable document at launch. A programmatic close that throws or returns without Closed rolls back once and leaves a close-only retry available to X, Alt+F4 and Cancel. The retry never finalizes again. No transaction is committed outside the session group. The view model owns queued plan, preview, and render dispatcher operations. Disposal stops both refresh coordinators, drops the pending plan snapshot, and aborts queued callbacks before cancelling in-flight analysis. Late preview results cannot publish to a retired view. Girt/opening projection still publishes validation flags, but those derived notifications do not queue another UI edit; segment group display refresh uses the same suppression. This prevents invalid rows or refreshed group labels from feeding a perpetual preview queue. Each analysis run owns its cancellation source until its finally completes. A newer run or view-model disposal cancels active work without disposing that source early. An idle source is cancelled and disposed immediately when replaced. Cancelled or superseded results cannot publish a plan or resume preview-mode changes after an asynchronous wait. A disposed view model creates no replacement idle source. Model commit requires an explicit successful startup/model outcome and a healthy transaction group. UI-state persistence contains only cosmetic layout and bulk-edit preferences (expanded panels, column widths, and bulk defaults), so it is best-effort and does not gate model commit. Neither OK nor Cancel waits for cosmetic disk I/O. A successful model commit with a still-pending save logs that preferences are being saved in the background without showing a banner. An already-failed save reports a warning through the Revit/default-owner notifier after the accepted close. A finally block always attaches the context-free disk-task observer, including when transaction finalization throws. The deferred observer logs a later disk failure but does not touch the retired window. A Cancel path releases the transaction and window first, then observes the save task without changing its Cancelled outcome. Mandatory preview/window cleanup failures select rollback before assimilation. Synchronous transaction, cleanup, and finalization failures propagate; cosmetic save failures do not change a definite model commit. This cosmetic-save policy supersedes the pre-commit persistence gate introduced in 7e0c558faa. WindowInitializer attaches the exact per-window Core boundary, while WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry owns the dispatcher subscription and routes DBTools-owned failures (thrown from or passing through an assembly named exactly DBTools or starting with DBTools., which covers DBTools.HandyControl and the Helix merged into DBTools.Presentation; another add-in's raw HandyControl or Helix copy never qualifies) to the most recently attached active window, or the most recently attached window when none is active. The selected WindowErrorBoundary remains the sole classifier, presenter, and handled-state owner. SgtWindowSession subscribes to its exact boundary; a missing host fails session construction rather than entering a pending, global, or timing-dependent route. When Core routes and handles a failure on that SGT window, the session records the original exception and any presentation failure, requests rollback closure while preserving the modal frame, completes all owned cleanup, deterministically unsubscribes, and then propagates the original failure ahead of cleanup or modal-assertion failures through the command safe-execution boundary. Foreign dispatcher exceptions are neither handled nor signalled by Core, and SGT does not attach a competing dispatcher handler. A direct ShowDialog failure before ContentRendered cannot have started analysis, so rollback, preview/window release, and transaction finalization are attempted synchronously on the current Revit UI thread before only context-free persistence can remain. Broken modal-continuation invariants are collected as finalization failures without short-circuiting mandatory rollback or owned cleanup. When the modal frame is already absent, the session records that invariant and does not knowingly await incomplete dispatcher-affine startup work; transaction admission downgrades an invalid modal lifetime to rollback and continues every safe owned cleanup step. UI-state persistence observes late failures without retaining the retired session and logs them without posting UI work after retirement. Opening-member snap endpoints are explicit: header/sill use Start or End, while jambs use Top or Bottom; the resolver rejects any mismatched role/endpoint request before resolving a target or creating an edit. WallGeometry is a Revit-free Domain contract for validated construction, point/face/center projection, and inclusive physical bounds. The safe-execution boundary owns user-facing reporting. No forwarding StartSession entrypoint, competing SGT dispatcher exception subscription, or window-owned fallback lifecycle remains. Feature Boundaries Placement Features/Placement/Domain contains pure command-state values/evaluation, preflight/readiness rules, gaps, validation, and placement-only domain projections. Features/Placement/ViewModels/PlacementCommandStateProjector.cs adapts the live girt/opening view models into those pure inputs and applies their validation state. Features/Placement/Planning creates placement projections from the domain plan; Features/Placement/Operations/ModelWrite owns the inward writer port, write context, contract catalog, and opening target; Persistence/ElementTagSchema holds the element-tag schema constants; Features/Placement/Revit/ModelWrite implements model mutation. App/session workflow owns command-level analysis orchestration through App/Sessions/Workflow/AnalysisSessionWorkflow; Revit-backed wall analysis and plan construction live under Features/WallAnalysis/{Domain,Revit/Planning}. Placement has no dependency on WallAnalysis. The ModelWrite name identifies the external model-write boundary. Recoverable plan rejections use SpecFailure results at the opening-segment, preview girt-snap, member-segment hydration, and placement-projection boundaries. Their UI callers show the exact typed rejection and do not publish a plan or preview change. Argument defects, cancellation, and unexpected projection/runtime faults remain exceptions and propagate unchanged through the established safe-execution boundary. Revit transaction/model-write owners may still use SpecFailureException where exception unwinding is required to roll back; callers must not translate unrelated runtime faults into ordinary validation results. Plan admission rejects invalid updates with SpecFailureException carrying PlanValidationFailed and the validation details. Parent opening persistence and segment mutation translate only that code into their existing failure results. Rejection preserves the committed plan and version. Parent edits remain suppressed until a successful retry or cancellation. Rejected segment add, delete, and property changes show the typed failure in both the banner and preview status without requesting a refresh. Unrelated exceptions still propagate. UI-to-plan synchronization reads the committed layer directly when the UI selection is absent. It constructs the girt projection at its consumer and lets opening persistence own opening projection. Segment lookup and deletion use canonical opening rows through the existing row resolver; no synchronization or segment context wrapper duplicates those owners. PlacementElementTagStore owns element admission for contextual selection, update, removal, and deconstruction. An owned element must have the structural-framing category, a valid SGT schema entity, the exact SGT marker, and a nonblank system ID. Updates collect admitted instances once per transaction and decode each tag into a role-and-identity index. Each target consumes its matching entry. Unmatched admitted instances are retired only after all requested walls are processed. Wrong-marker elements remain outside SGT ownership even when their stored system ID matches. PlacementWorkflow retains the command's SafeExecutionResult and returns one placement/removal outcome. Successful commands request successful close. A failed or cancelled model write requests rollback close. Declining removal confirmation leaves the window open because no write began. Revit/CommittedWrite/CommittedWrite maps Revit refusals and non-committed transaction status to Transaction/NotCommitted while retaining the original cause. Each command uses ordinary transactions inside the existing session group. Placement-owned dialog ports are IDangerConfirmationDialog and IUpdateSummaryDialog under Features/Placement/Workflow. App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionDialogs.cs implements them. Placement does not depend on an App-owned dialog contract. Change Review and physical acceptance Features/ChangeReview owns the detached review candidate, row decisions, target precedence, decision ledger, relink pairing, and the raw dialog. The dialog is loaded as an embedded raw XAML view by the tool-window host; it has no payload x:Class or code-behind. Accept, Keep, and Ignore are the only decision terms exposed to users and code. Opening labels use source name and along-wall range; the canonical opening key remains an internal identity only. ChangeReviewWorkflow synchronizes the accepted plan before capturing its revision, reads one live snapshot, and analyzes a confirmed candidate before publishing it. A review Confirm writes only the detached plan/ledger state. The later Place or Update command owns model writes and updates Placed from the actual write result. A successful review can therefore be followed by several ordinary model commands while the same session TransactionGroup remains open. The session lifecycle owns the review child and any relink picker. It retires a child in finally, closes the child before hiding the parent for a pick, and resumes the same synchronous modal driver after the picker returns. Normal window Cancel, native close, command failure, and forced retirement roll back the one session group. Only a successful window close assimilates it, producing one Revit Undo entry named Super Girt Tool. No review or placement command starts an outside transaction group. The current RevitLocal acceptance map is deliberately explicit: Contract Kept real fixture Place creates physical members, tags, and storage WallSystemWriterTests.PlaceAsync_RealProjection_PersistsTagsCountsAndProgressInOneTransaction Delete System removes owned members/storage and keeps a copied foreign tag PreviewPlacementParityTests.DeleteSystem_DeletesStorageAndPlacedElements Deconstruct removes SGT associations while retaining native framing PreviewPlacementParityTests.DeconstructSystem_DeletesStorageAndTags_PreservesPlacedElements Update keeps held opening members and does not adopt a copied identity WallSystemWriter.Updates_HeldOpeningLeavesFramingUntouchedAndNeverAdoptsCopiedIdentity Update preserves matches and retires unmatched tagged instances WallSystemWriter.Updates_UpdateAsync_PreservesMatchesAndDeletesUnmatchedTaggedInstance Persisted configuration is reloaded while current wall geometry is reanalyzed PreviewPlacementParityTests.Persisted_system_edit_plan_preserves_configuration_and_reanalyzes_desired_geometry Unsupported owned storage is purged and restored by group rollback WallSystemWriterTests.PurgeUnsupportedAsync_removes_only_owned_opaque_entities_inside_the_session_group Accepted opening removal re-anchors physical placement consistently with preview PreviewPlacementParityTests.Removing_an_opening_reanchors_girt_ends_and_placement_matches_preview Review ledger and inner physical Update commit or roll back with session OK/Cancel SgtWindowSessionTests.Real_change_review_confirm_and_inner_update_follow_session_close The Confirm proof injects only the child-dialog boundary: the production workflow, repository, analysis, placement executor, elements, tags, and session transaction group remain real. It performs the ledger write from Confirm and a physical Update before requesting either Cancel or OK. Revit does not expose an Undo-stack enumeration API, so the exact Super Girt Tool dropdown label and single-entry check remain operator evidence. The relink pairing and occupied-target case is released only when the B17 active-review picker is present. Missing linked/central-model inputs remain unexecuted release inputs; they are never replaced with fake transaction or Undo-history counters. Preview Features/Preview/Domain owns preview scene, palette, wall, girt, opening, grid, and computed segment-assignment state. Features/Preview/Rendering/Scene3D builds plain SGT mesh values; Features/Preview/Views/Rendering/Scene3D/StructuralPreviewSceneAdapter maps them to stable IStructuralPreview3D snapshot DTOs. WPF renderers and canvas layout live under Features/Preview/Views. The stable Presentation viewport owns Helix, camera navigation, fit/reset, hit testing, hover, and selection materials; SGT payload code has no Helix reference. PreviewPresenterBehavior retains 2D elevation/section drawing, handles, snapping, context menus, and row selection, while forwarding 3D scene and emphasis updates through the stable API. SgtWindow composes PreviewView.xaml into the stable host and retires the presenter before transaction finalization. Placement view models do not store Preview domain objects. Preview edits mutate the Domain plan and request FromPlan projection instead of mirroring state into Placement rows. PreviewServiceCollectionExtensions.cs registers the feature, and the App window-session builder binds it into the modal runtime. Preview edit workflows live under Features/Preview/Editing/MemberResolution/Segmentation; reusable plan-edit calculations live under Domain/PlanEditing. StructuralPreviewSceneAdapter is the sole boundary from payload scene metadata to stable Presentation DTOs. Mesh IDs preserve source row, role, and segment identity so click selection, hover tooltips, sibling dimming, segment emphasis, and wall-context materials remain deterministic. SGT disables the stable viewport's own tooltip popup so the payload PreviewView overlay remains the sole user-visible tooltip surface; stable pointer events still feed payload formatting, including wall-only click tooltips and wall-hover clearing. Wall meshes remain pickable context hits but never select rows; member hits retain precedence when both are present. The adapter also emits the legacy transparent floor plane and clamps overlay thickness to the former minimum. Scene bounds and exterior normal preserve the previous home camera orientation; the stable presenter owns orbit/pan/zoom/fit and camera persistence for the lifetime of the hosted view. Features/Preview/Refresh/PreviewProjectionService projects an explicit Plan without changing that plan or its store. App owns segmentation reconciliation for UiEdit and PlanMutation. A changed plan refreshes the UI and queues RenderOnly before any preview publication. RenderOnly reads the committed plan without reconciliation. PreviewRenderingService owns scene construction and its cache, not plan state. PlanSynchronizationWallSetupProjection projects the Layer selector items from the accepted plan; the preview projection does not own them. PreviewRefreshCoordinator owns monotonic request, completion, and success sequences. Only Applied advances success. Blocked completes without success. Deferred completes without success and the coordinator queues one RenderOnly successor; readiness waits for it. Disabled previews, rejected UI synchronization, missing plans, canceled builds, and failed builds cannot satisfy publication readiness. A UI-dispatch rejection fails the attempted sequence and preserves any newer request for dispatch. The production presenter acknowledges a scene only after the available viewport applies the scene, emphasis or reset, and selection highlight. Missing subscribers, unavailable presenters, and contained rendering failures return Blocked; failures clear the scene cache so a later refresh can retry. When the runtime presenter attaches after the view enters 3D mode, it invalidates the prior publication key and requests one render-only refresh through the scene event. A reused view model therefore redelivers its cached scene to the new presenter instead of treating the old delivery as current. App records a scene cache key only after publication succeeds. DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests.csproj owns [RevitLocal] fixtures and modeless Revit integration coverage. Actual modal execution belongs to Windows Pure. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Views/SgtWindowHostedTests.cs constructs the raw SgtWindow through ToolWindowFactory and verifies the modal shell dimensions, root composition, and named Girt/Openings/Preview hosts before releasing the session. SgtWindowSessionTests retains failure-order and startup-task assertions without opening a modal dialog. Windows Pure WindowSessionLifecycleTests covers pending picks after HideForPick; the runner re-enters after each pick completes, before the continuing target analysis finishes. The SGT staged model, linked document and wall IDs, opening/geometry baselines, plan-build outcomes, and preview projections are required repository-controlled truth. Missing or unexpected state fails with the requested baseline, observed result, resolved model path, and Revit year. Per-case rollback and fixture document/UIDocument/logging cleanup are part of the assertion contract and cannot be reduced to log-only diagnostics. The launch-composition smoke likewise treats startup-analysis completion, UI-state save, preview/stable-viewport cleanup, transaction-group rollback, window close, handler/view-model release, and run-scope disposal as ordered failure-bearing cleanup rather than evidence inferred from a Close() call; the active Autodesk document remains daemon-owned. The separate WPF construction smoke explicitly releases the view model it directly attaches; production window/session disposal has one owner and no OnClosing/OnClosed fallback branch. PreviewPlacementParityTests.Persisted_system_edit_plan_preserves_configuration_and_reanalyzes_current_wall round-trips nested girt, left-jamb, opening-key, and offset selections through the registered repository, moves the linked wall after saving its baseline, then invokes the registered edit-plan builder. The test requires the live wall elevation to differ from storage and verifies the edit plan uses current geometry while preserving the stored configuration. The transaction group rolls back both the storage write and the link movement after the assertion. Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/Tests/DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests.csproj Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/DBTools.SGT.csproj Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Views/SgtWindowHostedTests.cs Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Sessions/WindowSession/Revit/SgtWindowSessionTests.cs Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/Tests/Integration/Revit/Features/Placement/PreviewPlacementParityTests.cs:581-714 Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/MAP.md Use ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope pure for the pure suite and ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope local -y <year> for daemon-backed Revit execution. Normal hosted submissions omit --machine; daemon AUTO selects eligible workers using holder affinity and pressure. An explicit --machine remains a diagnostic/operator override. See the test pipeline for execution metadata and host requirements. User Documentation The restructure changes internal ownership only. Product workflows and UI behavior remain documented in the SGT user guide and section preview guide.

developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | DB Tools
developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting This page lists common build, runtime and tool errors, and how to read the DBTools logs. For a reported failure, read the logs in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ first. Build Choosing a build command Build one project or test project with plain MSBuild: dotnet build path/to/project.csproj -c Release This computes content versions, restores only the selected year and stages the project's runtime inputs. It does not validate or publish a distribution. ./build.sh BuildAll builds, validates and publishes the complete distribution for every supported year, including the Dev Mode preflight and manifest checks. BuildAll compiles no tests; use ./build.sh BuildTests or a selected-test target. See Build Pipeline. Python 3.10 or later is required Python 3.10 or later is required. Install it with: sudo apt-get install python3 On Linux and WSL, build/DotNet/sdk.sh uses Python to verify and install the pinned SDK when the private SDK root is incomplete; test.sh also uses it for test discovery. Install Python and rerun the command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3 bash build/DotNet/sdk.sh On Windows, build.ps1 installs and verifies the SDK without Python. DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package missing or mismatched BuildAll requires the DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package version pinned in build/Distribution/protocol-package-lock.json, with the SHA-256 recorded there. The Validation Runner loads the package after the build tasks verify it. If the package is missing or its bytes differ from the lock, obtain the pinned package and update the lock. sourceKind is github-release for a published release, or local-candidate for an approved local candidate with its candidate-<version> tag, daemon commit, and copies of the bundle README and SHA256SUMS. Do not point the build at a daemon checkout or bypass the check. BuildAll does not need the daemon CLI or an installed Revit. The DIST suite and hosted Revit tests use the daemon CLI. Dev Mode preflight fails ValidateDistributionCandidate runs the Dev Mode policy on each year and prints: Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<x> Both years must pass. A CollectibleThreadStatic warning counts as a failure. A failed policy, boundary, graph, identity or candidate-byte check needs a source fix and a new build. HandyControl output missing A missing vendor import, resource or DBTools.HandyControl output means the vendor/HandyControl submodule is not initialized. build.sh and build.ps1 initialize it automatically, which requires a Git checkout and network access: git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/HandyControl ./build.sh BuildAll The output is .artifacts/vendor/<Configuration>/handycontrol/net10.0-windows/DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Revit backup files in test models Revit writes backup copies (*.0001.rvt, *.00001.rvt) when it saves a model. Under testing/RevitTestModels/ these files are ignored by Git. The build does not delete them; remove them by hand when you no longer need them. Runtime Tool assembly fails to load InvalidOperationException: Failed to load tool assembly 'DBTools.GM' from the declared Tools path '<path>' in ALC rooted at 'DBTools'. Related errors from ToolAssemblyResolver: Tool assembly '<name>' was not found at the declared Tools path '<path>'. Tool assembly path '<path>' declares simple name '<x>', expected '<name>'. Tool assembly '<name>' is already loaded from '<path>', but the declared Tools path is '<path>'. App loads each tool from Tools/<name>.dll beside DBTools.dll. Check that the year directory has the complete product tree (see Assembly Loading Contract) and that the manifest's assembly name matches the file. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll. "Assembly already loaded" during Dev Mode reload Revit shows a popup about an assembly that is already loaded during or after BuildAll, while the dbtools-daemon Dev Mode driver watches the distribution. Causes: The driver watches the multi-year root .artifacts/dist/Release instead of one year directory. A reload starts while promotion replaces the files. DBTools code loaded or resolved a DBTools.* assembly or type outside the driver's collectible AssemblyLoadContext (for example through an AppDomain-wide scan or Assembly.Load), so the context cannot unload. Point the driver directly at one year directory, .artifacts/dist/Release/2026 or .artifacts/dist/Release/2027, never at a copy, and publish with ./build.sh BuildAll. Promotion keeps each unchanged file as the same file (a hard link), so Windows Defender does not scan it again. A copied directory is a set of new files that Defender scans again, which can add tens of seconds to each Dev Mode inspection. The supported desktop years are Revit 2026.5 and later, and Revit 2027; the distribution and reference metadata use the year keys 2026 and 2027. A candidate for any other year is rejected; there is no fallback framework. Theme validation Startup validates the theme with ThemeValidator.ValidateOrThrow; a failure stops startup. In a Revit-hosted test run, read the daemon job's startup failure output instead of waiting for a dialog. Theme dictionary merge failed InvalidOperationException: Theme dictionary merge failed at '/DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Brushes.xaml'. A resource dictionary did not load: a missing assembly reference, a broken StaticResource chain or invalid XAML. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll and check that the year directory contains DBTools.Presentation.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll from the same build. Theme resource freeze failed InvalidOperationException: Theme resource freeze failed for key '<key>' in '<source>'. A Freezable resource (brush, geometry) cannot be frozen, usually because it has a binding or a dynamic reference. Make its values static. Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch: expected 9 dictionaries but found 8 in '<root>'. InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch at index <i>: expected '<uri>' but found '<uri>'. Resources/Theme.xaml must merge these dictionaries in this order: HandyControl Themes/SkinDark.xaml, HandyControl Themes/Theme.xaml, then Tokens.xaml, Brushes.xaml, Converters.xaml, Controls.xaml, DataGrid.xaml, Menus.xaml and Components.xaml. See Theme System. Revit API context errors ContextUnavailableException: No UIApplication in current gate scope. InvalidOperationException: ActiveUIDocument is null. Code used the Revit API outside a valid API context, for example from a modeless window without the call gate, after the document closed, or during shutdown. Run Revit API work through IRevitCallGate.RunAsync, check that a document is open, and handle cancellation when a document closes. WPF Dispatcher errors InvalidOperationException: No WPF Dispatcher is available (Application.Current is null and no Revit window dispatcher could be resolved). InvalidOperationException: WPF Dispatcher is shutting down. UI work ran during early startup or late shutdown, when no dispatcher is available. Check for a dispatcher and for Dispatcher.HasShutdownStarted before UI work, and use BeginInvoke where the caller need not wait. Unhandled UI exception from a window command A WPF command that calls ISafeExecutor.RunAsync and lets the exception propagate into an AsyncRelayCommand raises a Dispatcher unhandled exception, which the Dev Mode driver host can also show. In window commands, use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync: it logs and notifies but does not rethrow. Use RunAsync where the caller must receive the exception. XamlParseException on a read-only binding System.Windows.Markup.XamlParseException: A TwoWay or OneWayToSource binding cannot work on the read-only property '<name>' ... Run.Text binds TwoWay by default. Binding it to a get-only property fails when the window loads. Set Mode=OneWay, or bind a TextBlock.Text instead. Raw VTC XAML uses OneTime bindings for immutable record values. Contextual ribbon layout changes A contextual ribbon injector that modifies Revit's contextual tabs eagerly (for example the Multi-Select tab) or inserts at index 0 shifts the native buttons. Inject only when the selection contains matching elements, append panels and buttons with Add, and remove them when the selection no longer matches. Core's ContextualRibbonInjector follows these rules. Other startup and manifest errors Message Cause AppRuntime not initialized. Code ran before App startup completed or after shutdown Manifest '<id>' is missing required 'panel' field. (and other missing required messages) Invalid manifest.yml Tool module type '<type>' not found in assembly '<assembly>'. The manifest module type or assembly name is wrong Tools Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) TransferException carries a TransferErrorCode: Code Meaning Action DestinationTypeMissing The destination has no matching drafting view type Create the view type in the destination SourceTypeNameUnavailable The source view type name cannot be read Check that the source is a valid drafting view CreateViewFailed The destination view could not be created Check write access and view limits CopyElementsFailed The view elements could not be copied Check the elements and the target view OverridesFailed The view overrides could not be copied Some overrides cannot be transferred View Template Comparer (VTC): raw XAML resource not found System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Embedded tool XAML resource 'DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml' was not found. The VTC alert body templates are an EmbeddedResource with the logical name DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml, read with ToolWindowXaml.ReadEmbeddedResource. Check the item and its LogicalName in DBTools.VTC.csproj. The shared VTC dictionaries are in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC. Logs Log files Logs are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. File names use Eastern time: dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>.log dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>-manual-<ManualTimestamp>.log The second form is written after Start New Log File in the logger window. Example: dbtools-2026-ABC123-20260124-143022345-a1b2c3d4.log. Startup cleans up old files: at most 50 files across all instances, at most 14 days old, and at most 100 MB in total while more than one file remains (the newest file is kept even if it alone is larger). Failures that occur before logging starts are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log. Debug mode Debug mode lowers the minimum log level from Information to Debug, shows the logger window and flushes the log buffer every 120 ms instead of 600 ms. It is off at every startup and is not saved. It turns on when: you enable it in the Settings window or open the logger window; an Error-level entry is logged and the logger window can be shown. An error logged before the Revit main window exists opens the window once deferred startup can show it. Closing the logger window turns debug mode off. Logger window The title is DB Tools Log - Revit <Year> [<InstanceId>]. The window is a modeless utility window. The logger host applies pin mode changes centrally: a change that keeps the owner mode only updates Topmost, and a change of owner mode closes and recreates the window. Code must not change the owner of the live window directly. The window provides: level filters for INFO, WARN, ERROR and DEBUG, and a text search; Copy All and Export, which save every retained entry in arrival order regardless of the filters. Export writes DBToolsLog_<yyyyMMdd_hhmmss><AM|PM>.txt; auto-scroll, which follows new entries. Scrolling up pauses it until you scroll back to the bottom or until a new entry arrives after 15 s idle; turning it off keeps it off; Start New Log File (in the danger menu), which starts a new file, clears the window and logs a confirmation with the same instance ID. If closing the previous file fails, the new file stays active and a warning is logged. Correlation IDs and execution phases ISafeExecutor gives every operation a GUID correlation ID and logs its phases: [Start] GM Apply starting (CorrelationId=...) [Complete] GM Apply completed in 1234ms (CorrelationId=...) Phase Level Meaning [Start] Information The operation started [Complete] Information The operation finished [Cancel] Warning The operation was cancelled [Error] Error The operation failed Search for the correlation ID to find every entry of one operation and its duration. Reporting a problem Include: the log file from %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, or a logger window export; the Revit version (year and build number); the DBTools version; the correlation ID of the failed operation; the steps to reproduce; a screenshot of any error dialog.

index.html.title: DB Tools documentation | DB Tools
index.html.summary: DB Tools documentation DB Tools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026.5 or later and Revit 2027, mainly for structural engineering workflows. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and installs for the current user. Sections Section Audience Contents User guide Revit users Installation, getting started and one page per tool. Developer guide Contributors Architecture, building a new tool and troubleshooting. API reference Contributors Reference generated from the XML documentation comments. Tools Tool Purpose Global Mapper Bulk replacement of families, types, styles and materials; duplicate detection; shared parameters. Super Girt Tool Girt, header, sill and jamb placement on walls. Foundation Tags Data and positions for combined pier and footing tags. Transfer Drafting Views Copy of drafting views between a project and a library. View Template Comparer Comparison and merge of view templates. The user guide lists all tools. Requirements Item Requirement Revit 2026.5 or later, or 2027 (desktop) Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user. The installer needs no administrator rights. Architecture DBTools.dll is the Revit entry point. It loads DBTools.Core (shared infrastructure and the tool registry), DBTools.Presentation (WPF resources and controls) and one assembly per tool from the Tools folder. The architecture overview describes the layers. Source: https://github.com/kirsch33/dbtools. Report problems on the issue tracker.

user-guide/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | DB Tools
user-guide/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started This page describes the DBTools ribbon, the settings window and the conventions shared by all tools. For installation, see Installation. The ribbon DBTools adds the DB Tools tab to the Revit ribbon. The tab has these panels: Panel Contents DB Tools Settings Settings DB Tools Common Global Mapper, Transfer Drafting Views (Export To Library and Import From Library), Align Elevation Tags DB Tools Structural Super Girt Tool, Foundation Tags and Organize Foundation Types (one split button), Analytical Snap To Level, Framing Joins, Update Joist Girder Weights DB Tools Testing View Template Comparer, Record Set, Extreme Roof Framing The pages of this guide refer to a panel by its last word, for example DB Tools > Common. The Testing panel holds tools that are still under development. A panel is hidden when its group is turned off in the settings. A tool whose prerequisites are not met is disabled, and a settings warning explains why (see Warnings). Settings Click Settings to open the settings window. It opens without a model. The General section has these options: Option Default Effect Enable Common Tools On Shows or hides the Common panel. Enable Structural Tools On Shows or hides the Structural panel. Enable Testing Tools On Shows or hides the Testing panel. Enable Services On Shows or hides background services in the ribbon. Enable Debug Mode Off Writes verbose logs and opens the logger window. Below General, each tool that has options contributes a settings pack: Elevation Tags, Combined Foundation Tags, Joist Girder Weights, Library Files (Transfer Drafting Views) and others. Each pack has a Reset button. Button Effect Validate Checks the settings and refreshes the warnings. Save Settings Saves all changes and closes the window. Reset All > Reset All Settings Resets every setting. Settings are stored per user and per Revit year in %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json. Several tools have an Auto-Update Enabled option. It makes the tool run when a view is activated. It does not update DBTools itself. Warnings A tool can raise a settings warning when a prerequisite is missing, for example Combined Foundation Tags Disabled or Library Paths Invalid. The warning disables the commands that depend on the prerequisite. The settings pack of the tool shows a card with a fix action, or states what to correct. Logs and debug mode DBTools writes a log file for each Revit session to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, named dbtools-<year>-...log. With Enable Debug Mode on, the logger window opens after a tool runs. The window can search and filter entries, copy them, and export them. Conventions Tools that change the model run in a Revit transaction. A failure inside the transaction rolls it back and leaves the model unchanged. Tools report their result in a banner at the screen corner or in a dialog. A banner closes by itself after a few seconds, except where a tool page says otherwise. A completed run is normally one undo entry. Press Ctrl+Z to undo it. Each tool page states exceptions. Tools that match elements by name take .NET regular expressions in their settings. Next Open the page of the tool you need. See the User guide for the list.

user-guide/index.html.title: User guide | DB Tools
user-guide/index.html.summary: User guide DBTools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026.5 or later and Revit 2027. This guide describes how to install the add-in and how to use each tool. Installation: requirements, installing, uninstalling, files and troubleshooting. Getting started: the ribbon, the settings window, logs and shared conventions. Tools Common Tool Purpose Global Mapper Replaces families, types, styles and materials in bulk, finds duplicates, and adds shared parameters. Transfer Drafting Views Copies drafting views between the open project and a library project. Elevation Tags Aligns the labels of spot elevation tags in plan views. Structural Tool Purpose Super Girt Tool Places and manages wall girts, headers, sills and jambs. See also the section preview. Foundation Tags Updates the data of combined pier and footing tags and moves the tags to footing corners. Organize Foundation Types Renames foundation types by their dimensions, assigns type marks and merges duplicates. Analytical Snap To Level Moves analytical beam and column end points to a level. Framing Joins Allows or disallows joins at the ends of structural framing. Joist Girder Weight Estimates joist girder weight and writes it to the Wt parameter. Testing Tool Purpose View Template Comparer Compares two view templates and merges selected settings. Record Set Packages Revit host models together with their linked files. Extreme Roof Framing Adjusts structural columns and beams to sloped roofs and floors. The Testing tools are under development. This guide has no page for Record Set and Extreme Roof Framing. Help Each tool page lists the tool's limitations and the messages it shows. For a failure, read the newest log in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. See Getting started. To build or extend DBTools, see the Developer guide.

user-guide/installation.html.title: Installation | DB Tools
user-guide/installation.html.summary: Installation DBTools is a Revit add-in for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027 on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. The installer runs under a standard user account and needs no administrator rights. Requirements Item Requirement Revit 2026.5 or later, or 2027 (desktop) Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user Installing Download DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe from the GitHub releases page, or from the location your administrator provides. Close all running Revit sessions. Run the installer. On the Revit page, select the Revit years to install for. The installer checks %ProgramW6432%\Autodesk\Revit <year>\RevitAPI.dll. It enables only the years it detects, and it selects them by default. At least one year has to be selected. If a DBTools bundle is already installed, the installer asks An existing DBTools.bundle was found. Overwrite?. Answer Yes to replace it. Answer No to cancel the installation. Wait for the installer to finish. The installation log is shown on the progress page and on the finish page. The button Open install folder opens %APPDATA%\DBTools. Start Revit. The DB Tools tab appears on the ribbon. What the installer does The installer copies the release into a staging folder next to the active bundle, checks that the required files exist for each selected year, and rewrites PackageContents.xml so that the bundle registers only the selected years. It then renames the current bundle to a backup, moves the staging folder into place, and deletes the backup. If any of these steps fails, the installer restores the previous bundle and reports the error. Installing replaces the entire bundle. A new install removes the previous version folder and any other file in the old bundle. There is no in-app updater. To update, run the installer of the new release. Files and folders Path Contents %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\ The add-in, loaded by Revit as an Autodesk application plugin bundle. Contents\DBTools\<version>\<year>\ holds DBTools.addin, DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll, DBTools.Presentation.dll, DBTools.HandyControl.dll and the Tools\ folder with one DBTools.<Tool>.dll per tool. %APPDATA%\DBTools\ The installer's data folder: the uninstaller, the icon and Families\ (Revit families that the tools use). %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json User settings, one file per Revit year. %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ Log files, named dbtools-<year>-...log. %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\ Tool caches, for example VTC\ (saved templates) and TDV\ (temporary library copies). Each tool stores its own data under %APPDATA%\DBTools\ as its page describes. Uninstalling Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, select DB Tools, and select Uninstall. The uninstaller deletes DBTools.bundle together with its .staging and .backup folders, and the Families folder. The uninstaller keeps your settings, logs and caches in %APPDATA%\DBTools\. To remove all DBTools data, delete that folder. Silent installation The installer is an Inno Setup program and accepts the standard Inno Setup switches, for example: DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART A silent installation installs for every detected Revit year. With /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES, the overwrite question takes its default answer, Yes. The installer has no switch for choosing Revit years or the install folder. Troubleshooting The DB Tools tab does not appear Close Revit and make sure %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\PackageContents.xml exists and lists your Revit year. Start Revit. Open the newest file in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ and search for ERROR or FATAL. If startup fails before logging starts, %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log holds the failure. Reinstall DBTools. DB Tools theme failed to load Revit shows this message when startup cannot load the DBTools theme. The message is followed by the failure details. Check that the year folder in the bundle holds DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll, DBTools.Presentation.dll, DBTools.HandyControl.dll and the Tools\ folder. If any file is missing, close Revit and reinstall DBTools. The installer reports an error The installer reports Could not activate the staged DBTools bundle or a similar message when it cannot rename the bundle folder. Close Revit, close any program that holds a file in the bundle folder, and run the installer again. Antivirus software that locks files in %APPDATA% can cause this error. Revit years A Revit year that is not installed cannot be selected. To add a year later, install Revit for that year and run the installer again.

user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.summary: Analytical Snap To Level Analytical Snap To Level moves the end points of the selected analytical beams and columns to the elevation of a level you choose. It edits the analytical model only. The physical elements do not change. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Analytical Snap To Level. The button is enabled when at least one element is selected. Elements that are not supported analytical members are skipped and reported (see Result). Usage Select analytical members. Select the analytical members themselves, not the physical elements they represent. Click Analytical Snap To Level. In the Select Target Level dialog, select one level and confirm. Closing the dialog without a selection cancels the command with the message No target level selected. Read the Snap to Level Complete dialog. The level list is sorted by elevation, lowest first. Each entry reads <name> (Elev: <value>), where the value is the level elevation in feet with two decimals. The project has to contain at least one level. Snapping rules A member is snapped only when all of these hold: it is an analytical member (the Analytical Member category); its structural role is Beam or Column; its curve is a straight line. Role Rule Beam Both end points move to the level elevation. The member becomes horizontal. Its plan position is unchanged. Column Only the end point closer to the level elevation moves to it. The start point moves when both ends are equally close. The other end stays fixed. X and Y coordinates of every end point are unchanged. Result The whole run is one Revit transaction named DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level. If an unexpected error occurs, the transaction is rolled back and no member changes. The completion dialog shows the number of elements processed and skipped. Below that, it lists one line per skip reason with the count. Skip reason Meaning not an analytical member The element is not an analytical member (a physical element, an analytical wall or floor). Only the count is shown. role not supported The structural role is not Beam or Column (for example girder or brace). not straight The curve is not a line. The member is not changed. would collapse The snap would make the member shorter than Revit's short-curve tolerance. For each reason other than not an analytical member, the dialog lists up to 10 element IDs and and N more for the rest. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a completed run in one step. Limitations The tool snaps to levels. It does not accept a reference plane or an arbitrary elevation. To use another elevation, create a level at it. All selected members snap to the one level you choose. To snap different floors to different levels, run the tool once per floor. Braces, walls, floors and curved members are not supported.

user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.summary: Elevation Tags Elevation Tags places the label of each matching spot elevation at a uniform position beside its leader end. The elevation text is re-measured and positioned from the tag type's font, text width and the view scale. The tool runs on demand from the ribbon and, optionally, each time you open a plan view. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Align Elevation Tags. The button is enabled when a view is active. It processes the active view only. Supported views: floor plans, structural plans (engineering plans) and ceiling plans. In any other view type the command shows the warning banner Elevation Tags supports Floor Plans, Structural Plans, and Ceiling Plans only. Active view type: <type>. and changes nothing. Usage Open a floor, structural or ceiling plan. Click Align Elevation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on, the same alignment runs each time a supported plan view becomes active. Automatic runs show no banner. Failures go to the log. What is aligned A spot elevation is processed when all of these hold: one of its names matches a tag name pattern (see Settings); it has a leader; the elevation base of its type is not Relative. For each processed spot the tool computes the label position from the leader end, then applies the per-type offsets. It moves the label only when the new X or Y position differs from the current one after rounding both to two decimals (feet). Spots that already sit at the target position are not counted as updated. For a type whose elevation base is Project Base Point, the displayed elevation is measured from the project base point when the project base point and survey point are at different positions. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Elevation Tags pack. Setting Default Description Auto-Update Enabled On Align tags when a supported plan view is activated. Tag Name Patterns (Regex) ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete\|Steel\|Wall) Label$ Up to 3 regular expressions. A spot is processed when any pattern matches any of its names. Matching is case-insensitive. Along Leader 0 Moves the label away from the leader end (positive) or toward it (negative), along the horizontal direction of the label. Perpendicular 0 Moves the label away from the leader line (positive) or toward it (negative), vertically. A spot is tested against these names: the spot name, the spot dimension type name and its family name, and the name and family name of the type's marker symbol. Because spot elevations are a system family, the patterns match the type and marker symbol names, not only loaded family names. When the pattern list is empty, the default pattern is used. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is skipped and logged. The two offsets are stored per spot elevation type. The settings pack has a type selector (previous and next buttons) and a live preview that shows the label, the tag origin and the leader end for the selected type with the current offsets. The offsets are in paper inches. The tool multiplies them by the view scale divided by 12 to get model units. Settings are stored per user and Revit year in %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json. They apply to every project. Result The command runs one Revit transaction on the active view. The banner shows one of these messages: Message Kind Aligned N elevation tag(s). Success Aligned N elevation tag(s); M could not be updated. See the DB Tools log. Warning M elevation tag(s) could not be updated. See the DB Tools log. Warning No spot elevation tags were found in the active view. Info No spot elevation tags matched Tag Name Patterns. Check Elevation Tags settings. Info No matching elevation tags needed changes. Spot elevations without a leader are skipped. Info A failure on one tag does not stop the others. A spot whose names cannot be read counts as failed. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a manual run. Limitations Only the active view is processed. There is no multi-view command; auto-update covers each view as you open it. Linked models are not processed. Spots without a leader and spots on a Relative elevation base are skipped. The last info message does not say which of the two causes applies. The text width is measured with the Windows font engine and the tag type's font. Arial is used when the type defines no font.

user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.title: Foundation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.summary: Foundation Tags Foundation Tags prepares and positions the combined pier and footing tags (family DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag). It has two commands: Update Combined Foundation Tags computes the data that the combined tag displays and writes it to shared parameters on piers and footings. Move Combined Tags moves combined tags to a corner of the footing they tag. The tool does not place tags. Place the tags with Revit's tag commands. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button. The split button also contains Organize Foundation Types. Command Effect Update Combined Foundation Tags Writes Foundation Pier Top on piers, and Associated Pier and Associated Pier Elevation on footings, in the active view. Move Combined Tags Moves each matching tag in the active view to the corner of its footing that the tag's name specifies. Both commands are enabled when a view is active and process the active view only. Both are disabled while the shared-parameter prerequisites are not met (see Prerequisites). Prerequisites The update command needs three project parameters, bound as instance parameters and identified by GUID: Parameter Type Category Group Associated Pier Text Structural Foundations Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation Length Structural Foundations Identity Data Foundation Pier Top Length Structural Columns Constraints DB Tools checks the parameters when the active model changes and before each command. If a parameter is missing, has another GUID, has the wrong data type, is bound as a type parameter, or is bound to the wrong category, DB Tools raises the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. The warning disables Update Combined Foundation Tags, Move Combined Tags and Organize Foundation Types. To repair the parameters: Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Click Refresh to list the status of each required parameter. Click Install/Repair (or Fix on the warning card). Install/Repair needs an active Revit document. It loads the definitions from the embedded shared parameter file, binds them to the required categories as instance parameters, and clears the warning. It also resolves conflicts: it deletes parameters that have the same name with another GUID, or duplicate definitions with the same name, and reinstalls the DB Tools definitions. It keeps any other categories bound to these parameters and their values. If one of those bindings is a type parameter, Install/Repair changes it to an instance parameter and Revit drops its type values. Status values include MISSING, GUID_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_NAME, WRONG_DATA_TYPE, UNBOUND, WRONG_BINDING_TYPE and WRONG_CATEGORY. Update Combined Foundation Tags Usage Open a plan view that shows the piers and footings. Run Update Combined Foundation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the update also runs each time you activate a floor plan or ceiling plan. Automatic runs show no result banner. What it does The command considers the family instances visible in the active view. A family instance is a pier when its family name matches a pier pattern. It is a footing when its family name matches a footing pattern (see Settings). For each pier, it computes Foundation Pier Top = the Top Offset parameter (0 if absent) plus the elevation of the level in the Top Level parameter, and writes it to the pier. For each footing, it finds the pier nearest in plan (X and Y of the location points) and within 2 ft. It writes the pier's Type Mark to Associated Pier and the pier's Foundation Pier Top to Associated Pier Elevation. A footing with no pier within 2 ft gets an empty Associated Pier. A value is written only when it differs. Lengths are compared after rounding to two decimals. Revit cannot clear a length value. A footing with no pier in range keeps its previous Associated Pier Elevation and counts as skipped on every run until a pier is within 2 ft. Result The update is one undo entry. A transaction group wraps the parameter writes and the selection sets. If a Revit write fails unexpectedly, the whole update is rolled back and the error is shown. A failure while creating the selection sets keeps the parameter writes and is reported. The banner reads Updated N element(s); M failed/skipped. or No elements modified. An element is counted as skipped when a pier lacks a valid Top Level, a footing or pier has no location point, a parameter is missing or read-only, or a length cannot be cleared. Outcome Banner At least one element modified Stays open. Has Select Modified, and Select Skipped when some elements were skipped. Nothing modified, some skipped Warning that closes after 10 seconds. No buttons. Nothing modified or skipped Info that closes after 6 seconds. The buttons select the elements of the run that just finished. They work only while the model that ran the update is active. Each run also creates selection sets named DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (<timestamp>) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (<timestamp>) when the respective list is not empty. The timestamp is in Eastern time. A second run in the same second adds a suffix such as (2). The model keeps the 5 most recently created sets with the prefix DB Tools - FoundationTags - . If an automatic update fails, DB Tools shows the error and stops automatic updates for that model until you close and reopen it. After Save As, or the first save of a new model, it tries once more. The commands remain available. Move Combined Tags Usage Open a plan view with combined tags. Run Move Combined Tags. What it does The command examines the independent tags in the active view. It moves a tag when: the tag tags a Structural Foundations element (in the model or in a linked model); the tag's family or type name matches a tag family pattern; and the tag's name is a corner name. The corner name is the name of the tag, or the name of its type when the tag has no name: Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right or Bottom Left (case-insensitive). The command computes the footing's bounding rectangle from its geometry in the footing's own X and Y axes. It selects the corner by the view's orientation, so Top Right is the corner at the top right of the view even in a rotated view. It sets the tag head position to that corner. The Z value of the tag head is unchanged. Linked footings are transformed into the host model's coordinates. The tag's leader is not changed. Result The banner reads Moved N; skipped M of K candidate tags. A candidate is skipped when the corner name is not valid, the tagged element is not a family instance with a location point, or it has no geometry. When no candidate exists, the banner says why: Message Cause No tags were found in the active view. No independent tags in the view. No tags in the active view are currently tagging structural foundation elements. The view's tags tag other categories. No tags matched the configured Tag Family Patterns. Check Combined Foundation Tags settings. Sample rejected tag families/types: <list> Tags tag foundations, but no tag family pattern matches. The move is one transaction. If an unexpected Revit geometry or write error occurs, the whole move is cancelled and no tag stays moved. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Setting Default Used by Auto-Update Enabled On Update (runs on floor plan and ceiling plan activation) Tag Family Patterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ Move Pier Family Patterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ Update Footing Family Patterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Update Each pattern list holds up to 3 regular expressions. Matching is case-insensitive. An empty list uses the default. An invalid expression is skipped and logged. When no valid pier or footing pattern exists, the update does nothing. When no valid tag pattern exists, the move does nothing. Limitations Both commands work on the active view only. Only family instances that are visible in the active view are updated. The nearest-pier search is 2D and has a fixed 2 ft radius. Piers and footings are recognized by family name only. Families with other names need a matching pattern. The corner a tag moves to is taken from its name. A tag with another name is skipped.

user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.title: Framing Joins | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.summary: Framing Joins Framing Joins allows or disallows joins at both ends of the selected structural framing elements. Revit joins a beam or brace to the column or framing it meets and cuts the geometry accordingly. Framing Joins sets that behavior for many members in one operation. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Framing Joins (split button). Command Effect Allow Join Allows joins at both ends of each selected framing member. Disallow Join Disallows joins at both ends of each selected framing member. The top part of the split button runs the current command. The arrow lists both commands. Availability Both commands are enabled when the selection contains at least one element of the Structural Framing category. The commands are disabled when nothing is selected or when no selected element is structural framing. Usage Select the framing members. Use a selection box, Ctrl+click, or a Revit selection filter. Run Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the confirmation banner. Selected elements that are not structural framing are ignored. Only family instances of the Structural Framing category (beams, braces and joists) are changed. Columns and other categories are not. Result The command runs in one Revit transaction named DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. It sets both ends (end 0 and end 1) of each member. A banner shows Allowed joins on N element(s). or Disallowed joins on N element(s). for 6 seconds. N counts the members processed, including members that already had the requested state. If Revit rejects the change on any member, the command stops, reports Failed to apply allow join operation for element <id>. (or disallow) and the transaction is not committed. No member keeps a partial change. The banner No elements were modified. appears when no member was processed. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a run in a single step. Limitations The command sets both ends together. To set the ends differently, use the end-join controls in Revit. Structural columns are a separate category and are not changed.

user-guide/tools/gm.html.title: Global Mapper | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper Global Mapper (GM) replaces project content in bulk. You map a source (a family, a type, a line style, an object style, a material or a parameter) to a target, review the plan, and apply every mapping in one operation. GM also finds likely duplicates, ranks replacement candidates by name and property similarity, and adds shared parameters to families and categories. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Global Mapper. GM opens as a modeless window and needs an open, active project. It works on the active document only. Linked files are not changed. Tab Purpose Duplicates Finds likely duplicate elements and lets you choose which one to keep. Families Maps families and their types, parameters, object styles and materials to other families. Line Styles Replaces line styles. Object Styles Replaces Detail Items object styles. Materials Replaces materials. Shared Parameters Adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to them. The Shared Parameters tab needs a Revit shared parameter file with at least one group. Without one, GM disables the tab and explains why. Workflow Open a tab. Choose the source rows to change and the target for each. A target can be chosen by hand or by the similarity ranking. Check Apply on each mapping to include in this run. Click Review Plan. GM opens Commit Review as a modal window and shows the plan. The model is not changed until you click Apply there. Click Apply. Then choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back (see Commit Review). Save the project before a bulk change. Window Header controls These controls apply to the current tab. Control Effect Search: Filters rows by name. Threshold: Slider from 0 to 100%. Sets the minimum similarity for automatic target selection. Sort mode (Similarity / A-Z) Orders target lists by similarity, with colored scores, or alphabetically with no scores. One setting covers the top-level and nested target lists. Hide Unused Hides elements with no instances in the project. Hide Unscanned Hides unscanned rows. Shown on the Families and Shared Parameters tabs only. Applied Only Shows rows with Apply on, including rows linked from other tabs. Not shown on Duplicates, which has its own status filter. Inspector Pane, Preview Panel, Views Panel, SP Authoring Pane Show or hide those panes. Clear... menu Clear Saved Mappings, Clear Saved UI State, Clear Deep Scan Cache (see Saved state). Mapping Conflicts Opens the conflict list. Shown when conflicts exist. Auto-Resolve All resolves them in the order: Duplicates, Tab Defaults, Family Overrides, Manual. The status line at the bottom left shows the loading state, the number of visible rows and the number of applied and conflicting rows of the current tab. A grid shows Loading... while data loads and a No ... message when a loaded result is empty. Similarity and threshold GM scores each target against its source. Scores are colored green (high), orange (medium) or red (low). At a threshold, an unchanged row selects the highest-scoring target at or above it. If no target qualifies, the row stays empty. A manual choice is never changed by the threshold. Opening a list and closing it without picking another entry is not a manual choice. <Do Not Map> is an explicit choice. On the Duplicates tab, the threshold controls which keep-target candidates appear for each source row. Duplicates The tab scans automatically when you open it. It groups elements that look like duplicates by name and property similarity. Styles and materials are matched on their previews. GM does not report two styles or materials as duplicates when it cannot read their previews. Line-style detection covers the whole line-style catalog, including styles with no family usage. Detect refreshes the catalog and the Usage rows and keeps your keep targets. Usage indexing decides which keep targets every restylable curve of a source can accept. While indexing runs, rows show line-style targets pending Usage indexing. A saved keep target stays visible, and Review Plan validates the targets after indexing. Steps Scope the rows. Category limits family rows and follows the category selected elsewhere in GM. Kind filters sources: All, Families, Materials, Line Styles, Object Styles or Shared Params. The status bar filters groups by All, Open, Resolved, Excluded or Conflicts. Group nodes show resolved counts, for example Families (133) · 45 resolved. For each source row, choose the Keep Target. A target must be in the same domain and category as the source. Check Apply for the rows that are ready to commit. Click Accept Applied to stage the rows that are ready. Click Review Plan. Columns Column Description Apply Commit flag for this session. It is off when the tab opens and is never restored from saved state. Source The element to replace, with its Kind, Suggestions and Highest Score. Keep Target The one element that remains. Save Off makes the choice apply to this run only. On saves the keep target for later sessions. Status Ready, Accepted, Mapped, or blank. A row is Ready when Apply is on, the keep target is not the source itself, the row is not excluded, and it has no validation or conflict flag. Choosing the source itself as the keep target marks the row as the keeper and turns Apply off. Accept Applied stages the rows that are Ready, not every row with Apply on. The inspector pane shows candidate details and a Metadata section with the Source ID and instance count. Its Accept split button saves the selection. The drop-down Accept Once keeps it for this session only. For a family row, Edit Type Mapping... in the context menu sets which source types map to which keep types. Shared-parameter duplicate rows can drive the selections on the Shared Parameters tab (Map From and Apply). Keep targets, the one-time-save choice, ignored candidates and exclusions are restored with the saved state. Exclusion badges (Saved, Session, Saved (Overridden)) show the exclusion time in a tooltip when it is known. Conflicts A blocking conflict prevents Review Plan. An advisory conflict (a restored saved choice that is not applied) shows in the conflict list only. The conflict button appears when any conflict exists. If one source is accepted to more than one target, GM raises a duplicate multi-target conflict and offers one-click cleanup. Choosing Keep Manual for a duplicate-versus-manual conflict clears the duplicate row's keep and apply state, so the same conflict does not return. Families The tab maps families in the selected category to replacement families. A family can be replaced only by a family of the same category. Columns Column Description Expand (+) Shows the row details. Quantity Instances of the family in the project. Apply Includes the mapping. Source The family. Target The replacement family. Choose the category first, then the target. Select the target with the dropdown; entries show their similarity score. Row details Expand a row to map its parts. The detail tabs are Types, Object Styles, Materials and Parameters. Object Styles and Materials are disabled when empty. The nested target lists use the same sort mode and threshold as the parent list. When you change the parent target, nested lists refill and keep the rows you changed by hand. Types: map each source type to a target type, or select <Do Not Map>. To create a type in the target family, check Create on the type row and enter New Type Name. Created types appear after the refresh that follows a commit. Parameters: map parameter names, with example values. Instance and type parameters are separate mappings, labeled (Instance) and (Type). A parameter maps only to a target of the same scope. GM copies parameter values only through these mappings, and they run with the type replacements. A red ! badge marks a conflict, such as a duplicate target parameter or a missing type-write policy. Resolve it before Review Plan. The Parameters tab shows Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. when scanning is unavailable, and No mappable parameters detected for this family. when it finds none. Expanded rows restored from saved state refresh their Object Styles and Materials usage automatically once usage data is loaded. While a target list is open, the mouse wheel scrolls that list, not the grid behind it. Type-scope writes: if a type-scope mapping writes into a target type that already has instances, GM blocks the commit until you choose Keep target type values (skip type-scope copies) or Overwrite target type values (copy them). GM takes the decision from the model state before the replacement batch starts. Moving the target's instances away earlier in the batch does not cancel Keep target type values. When overwriting is allowed, each mapping copies the original source values, even if an earlier mapping changed that source type. Object Styles and Materials: usage found by walking one placed instance. Rows from a deep scan carry a DS badge. An instance cycler, with previous and next buttons and a zoom button, moves to the sampled instance, even when it is in another view. Badges Badge Meaning OS, MAT, OS+MAT The family Apply state is linked from the Object Styles or Materials tab. LK (OS/MAT) Marks the nested rows that currently drive that link. DS Row data came from a deep scan. A tooltip shows partial-scan warnings. A linked Apply marks the family row, but family-owned operations (type swaps, parameter maps, type creation) run only when you checked that family row yourself. A saved target that is no longer among the options is flagged as incompatible. Create the mapping again; GM does not inject a hidden target. Line Styles The tab replaces one line style with another.
