Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The current line style. Target The replacement. Qty The curves in this document that a commit can restyle from this style. Preview A swatch of the style. GM captures each source's curves before it applies any line-style mapping, so a swap A to B and B to A exchanges the two populations, and a chain A to B to C leaves A's curves on B and B's curves on C. The mappings commit one after another inside the single undo step of the apply. A failed mapping rolls back the whole apply. GM restyles a grouped curve only when its group, and every enclosing group, has exactly one placed instance of its group type. Curves in groups with more than one instance are not counted and not replaced, because Revit requires Edit Group mode for them. GM does not enter that mode and does not ungroup elements. Ordinary curves with the same style are counted normally. A target has to be usable by every restylable curve of the source. A saved target that is not usable stays in the saved intent, shows a warning and is left out of the plan until you choose a valid target or Do Not Map. On the Line Styles, Object Styles and Materials tabs, an unavailable saved or chosen target stays visible as a disabled entry with a reason. A refresh keeps it; choose another target to replace it. Object Styles The tab replaces object styles of Detail Items subcategories (styles that are not line styles). Selecting a style lists the families that use it. A preview pane shows the style. Checking Apply links the affected families on the Families tab. Unchecking it removes the link. A family keeps its Apply if you checked it or another source links it. A lock badge only tells where a mapping came from. To override a mapping that a duplicate seeded, edit its target. At commit, GM opens each affected family document and ensures the target style exists in it, creating the style when it is missing. It copies the core style appearance from the project target, rewrites the references to the source style, and reloads the family into the project. GM omits a top-level mapping before commit when the source style has no family usage and no deep-scanned family reference. A mapping that exists only through a deep scan is kept and appears in Commit Review. GM omits, with a warning, a nested mapping whose owner family no longer exposes the source in the current usage or deep-scan data. GM does not scan the host document at apply time to rescue a stale mapping. Materials The tab replaces materials. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The material to replace. Target The replacement. Color Preview A swatch of the material color. Families Count Families that use the material. Families affected by a mapping are linked on the Families tab with the badge MAT or OS+MAT. In Families Using This Material, the Apply indicator shows the active link, so a linked family stays marked when a filter hides it from the Families list. At commit, GM updates material parameters in the project and in the affected family documents. When the target material is missing in a family document, GM creates it, copies its core properties and rewrites the references. It then reloads the family. A mapping whose source or target cannot be resolved in the project is ignored before commit and shown as a warning. Revit does not support formulas for parameters of the Material data type. GM migrates writable material defaults for each family type. It leaves formula-determined parameters outside the replacement. A replacement material takes over the appearance and the physical and thermal properties of the new material everywhere the old one was used. Shared Parameters The tab adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to shared parameters. The left panel shows a tree of curated categories (Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls, Windows), then families, then types. Category labels show counts such as Mechanical Equipment (12), and empty categories show (0) and are dimmed. The right panel shows an authoring card for each shared parameter of the selected type. Select a group in SP Group. Expand a category and a family, and select a type. The panel shows the existing parameters with sampled values, and the shared parameters of the group. For each parameter to add, check Apply and choose the binding mode. Optionally choose Map From (or enter a formula) to fill the new parameter from an existing one. Click Review Plan. Binding mode Effect Host-level Adds the parameter to the category as a project parameter. If the parameter already has a binding, GM adds the category to it, keeps its group and refuses a change between instance and type. Embed-in-family Adds the parameter inside the family document, so it travels with the family. Plan validation checks that each selected type still belongs to its family and category. It rejects a mismatched or stale selection with an error before apply. Map From writes the value that the Examples column shows: Between two parameters of the same type (Length to Length, Text to Text, Yes/No to Yes/No), the stored value is copied exactly. Into a Text parameter, GM writes the source as shown, with the document's units (300 mm, Yes, or the name of a phase or level). Into a Length, Area or other measured parameter, GM reads the source as Revit reads typed input, in the document's units. In a millimetre project, 12 is 12 mm. Text read into a Number or Integer parameter uses the decimal separator of your Windows number format and no thousands separators. With a decimal point, 1.5 is 1.5, and 1,5 or 1,500 is not written. With a decimal comma, 1,5 is 1.5, and 1.5 or 1.500 is not written. An Integer parameter takes only whole numbers, so 2.5 is not written. A value that cannot be read this way is not written. Examples are a Yes/No into a Number, 300 mm into an Integer, or a level or phase name into another element parameter. Commit Review lists the operation as Failed, with the value, the parameter and the reason, and writes none of its values. The Formula preview reads values by the same rules, including a measured value in the unit it shows. When a value cannot be read as a number, the preview shows that it is unavailable. The first visit to the tab loads the shared parameter groups and the curated categories, with a loading overlay once. Later expanding and collapsing, searching, and conflict updates do not show the overlay. The instance navigator, between SP Group and the authoring pane, steps through sampled instances. Zoom to Instance goes to an instance even when it is not in the active view. Commit Review Review Plan opens Commit Review. Revit is blocked while it is open. The window shows: the planned operations, by section (Plan Overview, Planned Operations, Host Replacements, Family Changes, Nested Families, Shared Parameters, Validation Issues); sections that do not apply are hidden; after apply, Commit Results, Domain Summary (succeeded, failed and skipped counts per stage, with affected references, family and timing context) and Family Breakdown; an Operation Results table with a status for each operation (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped), its operation id, stage and timing. Failed operations are summarized per mapping rule, with the source and target display names rather than element ids. The status bar shows the apply phase before the commit and the Applied, Skipped and Failed counts after it. Right-click a report table for Copy Selected or Copy All. Copy Report copies the whole report. Failed in the rules summary counts failed mapping rules. One rule can run across many families. Use the Families line (Planned / Attempted / Failed) and the Failed Operations row, which adds up the per-family failures. Apply Apply runs the plan inside one transaction group named Global Mapper: Apply. The group stays open while Commit Review shows the results. The commit continues after a failed operation: failures are recorded and the remaining operations run. The overlay Cancel button requests cancellation at once. After the run, GM verifies that no references to a source remain. Outcome What you can do Every operation succeeded and verification found no remaining source Choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back. An operation failed, verification found a remaining source, or the apply was canceled GM rolls the attempt back. Nothing is kept. Inspect the errors and choose Retry Apply to run the reviewed plan against the current model. Succeeded with nonfatal warnings Labeled Completed with Warnings. The Operation Warnings section lists each distinct instance, parameter and reason. Review it before you keep the changes. Keep remains available when verification succeeds. Keep + Continue records the mappings and returns to GM. GM refreshes the mapped data in place and restores the expanded row context. Types created with Create appear in the refreshed rows. Deep Scan results stay for families the commit did not change. Scan a changed family again to restore its details. Keep + Close GM records the mappings and closes GM. Roll back restores the model and creates no undo entry. A kept apply is one undo entry named Global Mapper: Apply. Press Ctrl+Z to revert it. Do not leave Commit Review open after Apply. Choose Keep or Roll back first. Closing the window with the X: during apply, requests cancellation and cleanup, then closes. If the cleanup fails, the window stays open and shows the error; after apply, asks whether to keep or roll back, with Roll back as the default. After any apply, GM re-reads the affected rows and counts from the model, whether the apply was kept or rolled back. A banner reports the outcome. A successful apply with operation warnings shows a warning banner that ends with Operation warnings: <n>. Otherwise a green banner with the Applied, Failed and Skipped counts; a red banner that starts with the reason, for example Apply was rolled back: 1 operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. or Apply failed; no changes were kept.; or Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. If the apply fails, Commit Review stays open. If an apply seems to stall near 90%, a Revit API call is still running. Click Cancel once and wait for the call to return. Cancellation is queued and cleanup runs when the active call ends. If it does not recover, report it with the latest DBTools log. How replacement batches behave Line styles, host materials, family materials, family object styles, types, host symbols and nested-family replacements use each mapping's original source population. A swap A to B and B to A exchanges the populations. A chain A to B and B to C leaves the original A population on B and the original B population on C. References moved by an earlier mapping do not become a later mapping's source. A shared nested family can appear under several selected roots. GM combines its applicable mappings and changes each original reference once. Later family reloads keep the result. Equivalent duplicate mappings get a merged notice. Conflicting targets for the same family source need your attention. A source that is absent from a traversed family is zero work, not a failed mapping. When a family reload cannot complete, every family operation that ran in that traversal is shown as failed, including equivalent shared-family aliases. The report keeps the affected count for writes completed before the failure and shows the reason. GM rolls the whole apply back, and you can choose Retry Apply. A failed operation can report writes that succeeded before it failed. Those counts are diagnostics, and the rollback discards the writes. If one half of a swap fails, the successful half could leave both populations on one target. For that reason GM rolls back the whole apply. Unchanged shared children stay on the project version during another family's reload. Shared children that the current traversal changed are reloaded from the edited family document. The family-document counts in Commit Review include the examined root and nested family documents, including documents where a source has no references. A parent-only material mapping leaves a shared child's material defaults unchanged. Map the child itself, or include it in the traversal, to change those defaults. Deep scan Some family details, such as embedded parameters and nested families, need a deep scan. A deep scan opens the family document. It is always started by you; GM does not scan when you expand a row. A deep scan is needed to: unlock the expanded details of a family with no instances (Scan required); read embedded definitions, such as nested family graphs, that a placed instance does not expose. For a family with instances, the Object Styles and Materials details come from walking one placed instance, so a deep scan is usually not needed. That walk records whether a source appears directly in the root family or only inside nested family content, and planning reuses that. Action Effect Scan Family (in the expanded details) Always runs a fresh deep scan. A complete result replaces the cache entry. An incomplete result removes the previous reusable entry. Deep Scan Unscanned (top-bar icon, Families tab) Scans all unscanned families with no instances in the current category, after a confirmation, with a progress overlay. Clear Deep Scan Cache Deletes the cached results and refreshes the display before it reports success. Results are cached across sessions. At startup GM restores cached results for eligible families with no instances. The restore is strict: if the cache entry does not resolve in the current document (for example a missing or ambiguous style or material), GM logs a warning and leaves the family unscanned. No banner appears. If you clear the cache while the restore runs, the cleared families stay unscanned until you scan them again. If Revit reports an error while GM reads a family parameter, GM keeps the names it read as diagnostics and marks parameter discovery incomplete. Those names are not offered as mapping choices and are not used for duplicate scoring. GM also removes the older reusable cache entry for that family. A separate successful read of the host can still fill the mapping choices. Otherwise, scan again after you fix the reported problem. If GM cannot fully resolve nested-family or material usage during a scan, it keeps the extracted details and warnings visible as a partial result, and does not cache or restore the family as complete. Scan again after you fix the reported references. A malformed or incomplete cache entry is deleted and needs a new scan. The cache is disposable and is not migrated between formats. Saved state GM saves your mapping intent and window state for each project. It uses the saved file path when the document has one. An unsaved document uses its session key, so unsaved documents with the same title do not share state. On reopen, saved targets are restored as suggestions. Apply is left off, so nothing is enabled for commit. Menu item (Clear...) Effect Clear Saved Mappings Removes the mapping and duplicate selections for this document. It writes an empty snapshot before it confirms, so the mappings do not return from an old file or from an open GM window. Clear Saved UI State Removes the tab, search, filter and scroll state. It waits for pending writes first. The next GM window for the document starts with default state. An open window cannot write older state back on close. Clear Deep Scan Cache Removes deep-scan data and the DS badges. If a deletion fails or is canceled, GM does not report success. If GM cannot write the saved mappings, it logs the failure and shows an error banner, and your mappings may not persist. If the saved-mappings file does not match the current GM schema, GM shows a banner and continues without restoring it. A saved target, or a saved Shared Parameters Map From source, that no longer exists is flagged as incompatible and must be created again. Style targets have to belong to the source's scope (Line Styles or Object Styles). Style usage rows use canonical style ids, so family-usage counts stay tied to the real style after reopen or refresh. Usage rows are limited to the universe of the active tab (Materials, Line Styles, Detail Items Object Styles). Errors Message Meaning Action Invalid mapping Source and target are the same. Select another target. Target not available The target family or type was deleted. Reload the family or choose another target. Deep scan failed The family document could not be opened. Check that the family file is accessible. Conflict detected Several sources map to the same target. Resolve it in the conflict list. GM Duplicate Type Mapping The Duplicate Type Mapping dialog, or loading its type names, failed. The mapping is unchanged. Retry Edit Type Mapping... and check the DBTools log. Locked by Families tab A nested mapping is set on the Families tab. Change it there. If Review Plan is disabled, no mapping is applied, or a blocking conflict exists. If the target list is empty, the category has no other family. If a family shows Scan required, run Scan Family. If some instances were not replaced, open the family and check that every type is mapped. Limitations GM changes the active document only. A family can only be replaced by a family of the same category. Line style and object style scopes are limited as described above: curves in multi-instance groups are not restyled, and the Object Styles tab covers Detail Items subcategories only. A commit time grows with the number of elements and families: a few dozen changes finish at once, and thousands can take minutes. The progress overlay shows the state. The Shared Parameters tab lists the curated categories only: Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls and Windows.

user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.title: Joist Girder Weight | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.summary: Joist Girder Weight Joist Girder Weight estimates the weight per foot of joist girders from their span, depth, panel count and panel point load, and writes the result to the Wt parameter of each girder. The estimate is for preliminary design and takeoffs. It does not replace the manufacturer's tables. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Update Joist Girder Weights. The command processes the whole model. It does not depend on the selection or the active view. Usage Make sure each girder family provides the inputs listed under Family requirements. Click Update Joist Girder Weights. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the same update runs each time you activate a view, with no banner. Disable it in the settings if view changes are slow in a large model. Which elements are processed The tool collects the elements of the Structural Framing category whose family name matches the Family/Type Name Pattern. It matches the type name only when the family name is unavailable. Default pattern: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$. It matches G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder and Vulcraft Joist Girder. Family requirements Each parameter is read from the instance first and then from the type. Names match case-insensitively where the parameter is looked up by alias. Input Parameter names Notes Number of joists (N) Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Must be greater than 1. Length Cut Length, then Length Must be greater than 0. Depth Depth Must be greater than 0. Panel point load Parameters matched by the load patterns See Load resolution. Output Wt A writable Double parameter, on the instance or the type. Numeric inputs may be Double, Integer or text. A text value has to parse as a number. Load resolution Load parameters are found by matching their names against the three load patterns. Matching parameters are collected from the instance and the type. Pattern Default Matches, for example Dead Load (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) Dead Load, DL Live Load (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) Live Load, LL Total Load (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) Point Load, Panel Point Load, Total Load The load is resolved as follows: A negative value in any load parameter skips the girder as invalid. More than one parameter with a value in any one group (Total, Dead or Live) skips the girder as ambiguous. This check comes first: one Total Load value plus two Dead Load values skips the girder. If exactly one Total Load parameter has a value, it is the panel point load. Otherwise, if exactly one Dead Load and exactly one Live Load parameter have values, their sum is the panel point load. Otherwise the girder is skipped. A single Total Load value takes precedence over single Dead and Live values. Load values are converted to kips. A Force parameter is converted from its stored unit. A number with no unit is taken as kips. Text values accept a number followed by an optional unit: kip, kips, k, lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds or kN (for example 10 kips, 10000 lb, 45 kN). To use other parameter names, such as localized names, change the patterns in the settings. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Joist Girder Weights pack. Setting Default Auto-Update Enabled On Family/Type Name Pattern ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)\|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ Dead Load Pattern (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) Live Load Pattern (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) Total Load Pattern (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) An empty pattern field uses the default. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is reported as a configuration error. In that case the manual command shows the error as a warning banner for 10 seconds and changes nothing. Auto-update shows the same banner and raises the tool warning Joist Girder Weights Disabled, which disables the command until you clear the warning in the settings. Calculation The estimate uses N joists (N - 1 panels), panel point load P (kips), length L and depth D, in inches: panel spacing = L / N; maximum moment from the end reaction P(N - 1)/2, less the moments of the panel loads between the support and midspan; chord force = moment / (0.95 D); required chord area = chord force / (50 ksi x 0.6); top chord weight = area x L x 0.28356 lb/in^3 x 1.06; bottom chord weight = 1.13 x top chord weight; web weight = 0.7 x top chord weight; Wt = (top + bottom + web) / (L in feet), in lb/ft. The value is written to Wt as a number, without a unit conversion. Result The manual command writes all valid girders in one transaction named Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. A girder that fails validation is skipped, and the rest are updated. The banner shows: Candidates: <n> Updated: <n> Skipped: <n> Sample skipped element(s): - Element <id>: <reason> The sample list holds up to 5 skipped girders. The banner is a success banner when nothing was skipped, a warning when some girders were skipped, and informational when none were updated. No joist girders were found. appears when no element matches the family pattern. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a manual run. Limitations The tool writes only Wt. It changes no other parameter. The calculation uses a fixed allowable stress and fixed efficiency factors. Check the results against manufacturer data for final design. Auto-update runs on every view activation and reads every matching girder. It adds delay in models with many girders.

user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.summary: Organize Foundation Types Organize Foundation Types renames pier, footing and pile cap types by their dimensions, assigns sequential type marks, and merges types that have identical dimensions. It changes types. It does not move placed instances. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button (with Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags). The command processes the whole model. It is disabled while the Combined Foundation Tags Disabled warning is active (see Foundation Tags). Usage Save the model. Run Organize Foundation Types. Answer Do you want to overwrite existing type marks? Read the Organize Foundation Types result dialog. Answer Effect Yes Regenerates the type mark of every processed type. No Keeps existing type marks. Types with an empty type mark receive a new one. Processed types The tool processes types of these families (exact names, case-sensitive): Family Category Dimension parameters Mark prefix Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Types of other families are not processed. Naming and marks Each type is renamed as <dimensions> (<mark>). Dimensions are formatted in feet and fractional inches. Family Name format Example Foundation Pier <b>x<h> (<mark>) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Foundation Pier - Round <d> DIA. (<mark>) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) Pile Cap-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 4'-0"x4'-0"x2'-0" (CAP-4.0) Types are processed in ascending order of size, and marks are assigned in that order: piers: section area b x h; round piers: diameter; footings and pile caps: width, then length, then thickness. Pier and round pier marks are P-1, P-2, ... and RP-1, RP-2, .... Footing and pile cap marks are <prefix>-<w>.<n>, where <w> is the width in whole feet (rounded down) and <n> counts from 0 within that width: F-3.0, F-3.1, CAP-4.0. Merging Types of one family with equal dimension values are duplicates. The tool keeps the first in the sort order, changes every instance of the other types to the kept type, and deletes the other types. Equality is exact on the stored values, so types that differ by a small amount are not merged. Instances stay where they are. Result The tool runs in one Revit transaction. The result dialog shows the number of types renamed, duplicates merged and types skipped: Successfully organized pier and footing types. - N types renamed - N duplicates merged - N types skipped When types are skipped, the first line reads Organized pier and footing types with skipped types. and the dialog adds up to 5 lines <type id>: <reason>. A type is skipped when Revit rejects its change, for example when the new name already exists. The remaining types are still processed. If a merged type cannot be deleted, the command fails and the transaction is cancelled. Press Ctrl+Z to undo the whole run. Limitations With No, the tool does not compare new marks with preserved marks that come later in the sort order, so two types can end with the same mark. Use Yes for a consistent set. The tool changes only the type name and the Type Mark parameter, and the type of merged instances. The type mark is written only when the Type Mark parameter is a writable text parameter. Linked models are not processed. Types that Revit rejects are skipped, not retried.

user-guide/tools/sgt.html.title: Super Girt Tool (SGT) | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/sgt.html.summary: Super Girt Tool (SGT) The Super Girt Tool automates the placement of horizontal girts and opening framing (headers, sills, and jambs) on foundation walls. Instead of manually placing each structural member one at a time, SGT lets you configure an entire wall's worth of girts in one operation. When to Use It Use the Super Girt Tool when you need to: Add horizontal girt members to a foundation wall at regular spacing Frame out openings (doors, windows, penetrations) with headers, sills, and jambs Place multiple girt rows at once instead of one-by-one Ensure consistent spacing and alignment across a wall Edit or update previously placed girt systems Common scenarios: Scenario SGT Helps By... New foundation wall with multiple window openings Auto-detecting openings and framing them Girts at 5'-0" vertical spacing Pre-seeding rows at correct intervals Mixed girt sizes at different elevations Configuring each row independently Updating girt types after initial placement Editing the existing system in place Quick Start Basic workflow in 4 steps: Launch - Click "Super Girt Tool" from the DB Tools ribbon tab Select Wall - Pick the foundation wall or linked wall you want to frame Configure - Adjust girt elevations, types, and opening framing as needed Place - Click "Place" to create all the structural members That's it for basic use. The tool handles the technical details of rotation, justification, and positioning automatically. The SGT Window When you launch SGT and select a wall, the main window appears with these sections: Top Bar Control Purpose Offset Distance from the wall face to place girts (0'-0" means directly on the target layer) Layer Which wall layer to align girts to (for compound walls with multiple layers). The list shows the analyzed wall's layers and follows the current plan, even when the preview cannot update. Girt Elevations Section This is where you configure your horizontal girts. Each row represents one girt at a specific elevation. Column What It Does Elevation Height above the base reference (editable) Girt Type Family and type to use (e.g., "C Shapes : C10X15.3") Rotation Cross-section rotation (0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees) Y-Just Lateral positioning (Left, Center, Right, Origin) Z-Just Vertical positioning (Top, Middle, Bottom, Origin) Flip Flip Facing (mirror the member orientation) if needed Left Extent Where the girt starts - Full Length or at a grid line Right Extent Where the girt ends - Full Length or at a grid line Add Row: Type an elevation in the "Add" field and click "Add" to create a new girt row. Segmented girts: Auto-segmented girts show a chevron in the first column. Click it to open the MemberSegment Flyout, where you can edit Type/Rotation/Y/Z/Flip (and delete) per segment. Selecting a segment in the flyout highlights it in the preview so it’s clear which segment you’re editing. The flyout opens to the right of the chevron and centers vertically in the window; resizing primarily expands the Type field. The background behind the flyout is lightly dimmed so the preview remains visible. The chevron now follows the materialized segmented plan state: if opening analysis or later opening edits split a girt into multiple segments, the chevron appears; if recomputation collapses that group back to one segment, the chevron is removed. While another field is invalid, flyout edits are refused and nothing is lost (see the rule under Openings Section). Openings Section This section shows detected openings in Linked mode and also lets you add manual openings. In host foundation mode, SGT ignores physical/Revit wall openings entirely, so the grid is manual-only. Column What It Does Opening Name/ID of the opening Center Along Horizontal position along the wall Bottom Elevation Vertical position of the opening bottom Width Opening width Height Opening height Left Jamb Enable/disable left vertical framing Right Jamb Enable/disable right vertical framing Header Enable/disable top horizontal framing Sill Enable/disable bottom horizontal framing Use the chevron on each opening row to open the MemberSegment Flyout for opening members. The flyout shows role-level fields (Type/Rotation/Y/Z/Flip) and (when segmented) per-segment child rows for that role. Selecting a segment highlights it in the preview. The flyout opens to the right of the chevron, centered vertically in the window, with the same resizing rules as the girt segment flyout. While another field is invalid, segment edits in this flyout are refused (see below). Parent-level opening edits are draft-scoped. While you are editing Center Along, Bottom Elevation, Width, Height, or the parent role checkboxes, SGT keeps the last committed plan/preview visible. Leaving the row or pressing Enter commits one sync/re-segmentation/preview refresh; Esc cancels the draft (see the exception below). If you enable an opening role and then change that role's Type/Rotation/Y/Z/Flip before leaving the row, SGT preserves those explicit settings on commit instead of snapping the role back to seed defaults. If the row is still invalid, SGT keeps that row in edit mode and leaves the last committed plan/preview intact until you fix the highlighted fields or cancel the edit. When linked-wall analysis finds no openings, SGT now shows a neutral info banner instead of an error banner. The opening commit, segment flyout edits and preview canvas edits (snap, gap, delete, merge) each save your other unsaved field edits with them, in one step: for example a wall offset you typed just before clicking another opening row, or a field you changed while the 3D preview was still building. While any wall setup, girt or opening field is invalid, SGT refuses such an edit and writes nothing: the opening row stays in edit with its values, the gap editor stays open with the typed gap, also when the preview redraws, until you press Enter again or Esc, a refused flyout choice shows the saved value again, your other unsaved field edits stay, and the preview status says why (Fix invalid fields, Fix invalid rows or Preview blocked). Undo reverts a canvas snap, typed gap change, delete or merge; typed gap undo restores its prior override, while saved field edits stay. An accepted typed gap clears any existing redo action. Deleting girt rows in the grid, the invalid row included, is never refused; the next sync renumbers the segment group the deleted row left, and a group left with one row becomes a plain girt. If SGT writes the window while the opening row is still in edit (you fix the other field, or make another edit), that row's draft is written too, so Esc can no longer fully cancel it: the row shows its old values again, but the plan keeps the draft and a later refresh can bring it back (known issue). A successful linked-wall detection with no openings clears stale detected rows and keeps manual openings. In Change Review, saved live openings missing from a successful observation require an Accept, Keep or Ignore decision; an incomplete observation remains Unreadable and cannot become a deletion. Bulk Edit Flyout Double-click a row in either grid to open the Bulk Edit flyout. The flyout is an in-window overlay (not a detached WPF Popup), so it stays bound to the SGT window during minimize/restore and does not float above other apps. Targets: Choose which member roles the bulk operation applies to (e.g. Girt, Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header, Sill). Flip Facing: Tri-state; indeterminate means “don’t apply Flip” for this bulk operation. Apply (N): N is the number of active fields that will be applied (Type/Rotation/Y/Z/Flip). Preview Panel (Right Side) Shows a live preview of what will be placed: Elevation - Front view showing girts and openings Section - Cross-section view showing horizontal member profiles and clipped jamb bands 3D - Interactive 3D view you can orbit and zoom The Role Palette shows what each color represents: Blue = Girts Green = Headers Orange = Sills Purple = Left Jambs Cyan = Right Jambs Preview controls (mode selector, zoom-to-fit, reset view) are overlaid in the top-right of the preview. In elevation/section mode, the legend shows segment types and role colors. Section preview now keeps jambs visible whenever the clip range crosses their opening edge, drawing them as vertical depth bands that match placed geometry while girts/headers/sills continue to use resolved section profiles. In 3D, switching into the preview automatically jumps to the stable exterior “home” camera, and Reset view returns to that same camera (3/4 view + slight downward pitch), including for mirrored/rotated links. Wheel zoom now uses a looser near/far clamp (close inspection without an abrupt hard wall), and camera constraints use a relaxed leash that settles after interaction. Pan/orbit always stop on mouse-up and also cancel if the window deactivates. 3D click-to-inspect: Click any element in the 3D preview to select it (highlights in gold) and display a tooltip showing the role and section name. Selection commits on mouse-up when the gesture was a click (not a drag-pan). Clicking a wall layer shows a tooltip with layer info without clearing the current selection. Clicking empty space clears the selection and hides the tooltip. When a specific segment is selected, sibling segments from the same member are shown with a mild dim while unrelated elements are fully dimmed. Preview editing notes: Drag/snap edits from elevation preview handles (girt extents/segments and jamb/header/sill extents) now participate in the SGT window's Undo/Redo buttons. Undo and Redo restore the plan, so they also replace unsaved field edits, an invalid field included. Typed gap edits in the 2D gap editor also participate in Undo/Redo. An accepted typed change clears any redo action from an earlier edit. Drag/snap edits are association-locked: handles snap only to valid associations (other elements, grids, or wall edges). They do not create arbitrary free-along points. A drag only commits when you are inside snap threshold on an accepted target; until then, preview border/guide feedback stays in the invalid state. Snap guides now render continuously while dragging: dim bands for available targets plus an active guide line (cyan when valid, red when invalid). Opening geometry is not draggable in preview: opening rectangles/edges do not expose drag/snap handles. For segmented opening members, jamb/header/sill endpoint handles are created per segment; dragging one endpoint updates that specific segment's extent association. For bisected girts, only the true outer endpoints move member extents (first-left/start and last-right/end). Other segment endpoints edit opening-edge gaps. Interior bisected endpoints commit by opening-edge identity (opening key + edge side), so mirrored/rotated links do not move the opposite endpoint. A girt's outer endpoints snap only to opening edges that can bound them. An opening's lower edge is the edge nearer the wall start; its higher edge is the edge nearer the wall end. The start snaps to the higher edge of an opening that crosses the girt, the end to the lower edge, or the start to the lower edge and the end to the higher edge of one opening for a girt inside that opening. An edge of an opening the girt bypasses is offered too: snapping to it clears that bypass. An edge that would leave the girt no span of 6" (0.5 ft) or longer is not offered. A snap to an edge that cannot bound that end is rejected with GirtSnap/BoundaryInvalid, and a snap that leaves no usable span with GirtSnap/NoUsableSpan. When a girt endpoint is snapped to a new association, any explicit gap override for the touched endpoint/edge is cleared so geometry-aware defaults apply for the new association. A girt end on a wall edge or grid that lies exactly on the edge of an opening the girt stops at gets that edge's jamb gap, in the preview and in the placed girt alike. A gap override you set for that end replaces it. When you merge adjacent girt segments, any opening-member extents that targeted either segment are automatically re-targeted to the merged segment key, so snap-to-girt semantics remain stable after merges. If re-segmentation recomputation yields fewer than 2 segments, SGT collapses the segment group back into a single standalone row and shows a banner summarizing how many groups were collapsed. If geometry-aware gap computation fails (missing profile or transform failure), SGT reports an error. Re-run Analyze to refresh warmup data. A gap handle on an opening you just deleted can stay on the canvas until the preview redraws; double-clicking it then shows a "Gap edit failed" banner instead of a gap editor (known issue). Gap override fields reject NaN / Infinity values (negative values are allowed); invalid overrides surface as plan validation failures before placement. Placement validation failures remain explicit before commit and are reported without being converted into generic placement exceptions; unexpected Revit placement faults surface through the tool error boundary with their original cause. A girt segment that cannot be placed reports its own failure, with the same text on Place and Update; for example, a girt family without Start/End Extension parameters reports Writer/ExtensionParamMissing when an end gap needs them. A missing opening framing type reports Plan/EligibleOpeningTypesMissing, not an orientation failure. A girt whose start is on an opening's lower edge and whose end is on the same opening's higher edge spans inside that opening; every other girt is split at each opening it crosses unless it bypasses that opening. Girt pieces shorter than 6" (0.5 ft), such as a narrow pier between two close openings, are left out. Jamb, header and sill handles, and girt segment handles other than the girt's own start and end, are offered all eligible opening edges in the active preview, not only the currently selected opening row. A girt's outer endpoints follow the boundary rule above. An opening splits every girt it crosses even when all of its framing roles are turned off. When the opening or grid a girt end was attached to is removed, or that opening no longer crosses the girt (for example after an opening edit or a shortened wall), SGT moves that end to the nearest opening edge that is at least 6" (0.5 ft) from the girt's other end, or to the wall edge when there is none, and clears that end's gap override. A gap override you set for the opening edge it moves to is kept. The banner states how many ends moved ("Re-anchored N girt end(s) to the nearest opening or wall edge."). When two segments of one girt then overlap, SGT merges them into the first segment and the banner also states "Merged N overlapping girt segment(s) into their neighbors." A header or sill split position beyond the wall fails Place/Update with a message that names the opening. Grid markers in elevation preview now use a white bubble (white fill, black outline) with centered black label text for dark-theme readability. When multiple handles overlap, press Tab to cycle candidates; Enter confirms the highlighted handle and Esc cancels. Right-click on a segmented opening member now opens a segment-specific context menu (delete that segment only). Row-level delete actions appear only when you open the row menu itself. Deleting the last segment of a single opening role removes that role; the opening row itself remains until all roles for that opening are removed. Debug Log Volume (2026-03-08) When Debug mode is enabled, SGT now favors condensed summaries instead of per-probe noise: Step 1/2/3 preflight summaries report total/success/failure counts. Step 2 opening detection/merge logs stay summarized, with small opening samples instead of one line per internal probe. Orientation logging keeps concise per-role Debug summaries; detailed probe attempts are folded into those summary diagnostics instead of being emitted separately. Temporary probe transactions log only when they captured diagnostics, and blocking probe failures still surface as warnings/errors. This keeps long manual sessions readable while preserving the main breadcrumbs needed for parity triage. Bottom Bar Button Action Cancel Close without placing anything Place Create all configured members in Revit Update (Edit mode) Update existing members Remove (Edit mode) Delete the entire girt system Step-by-Step Workflows Creating a New Girt Plan Launch the tool Go to the DB Tools ribbon tab Click "Super Girt Tool" Select your wall A prompt appears asking you to select a wall Click on a foundation wall or linked wall The tool analyzes the wall and populates the window Review auto-seeded girts SGT automatically creates girt rows at approximately 5'-0" spacing Review the elevations and adjust as needed Change girt types if you need different sizes at certain elevations Configure openings (if any) Linked walls: Openings are auto-detected Foundation walls: Click "Add Opening" to manually define openings; SGT ignores any physical/Revit wall openings on the host wall in this mode Check/uncheck the boxes for which framing members you want Preview your layout Switch between Elevation, Section, and 3D views Verify everything looks correct before placing Place the girts Click "Place" The tool creates all members in Revit Adjusting Girt Elevations To change an existing row's elevation: Click in the Elevation cell for that row Type the new elevation (e.g., "7'-6"") Press Enter - the preview updates automatically Elevation and offset fields accept invariant decimal feet (7.5), feet marked with an apostrophe (7'), feet plus quoted inches (7'-6" or 7'-6 1/2"), and quoted inches (18", 6.5", or 6 1/2"). Spaces may surround the marks, hyphen, and fraction slash. One leading + or - applies to the entire value. Named units (ft, in, metric units), localized commas, exponents, component signs, unquoted fractions, and trailing text are rejected. To add a new girt at a specific elevation: Find the "Add" field at the bottom of the Girt Elevations section Type your elevation (e.g., "12'-0"") Click "Add" A new row appears with default settings To remove a girt row: Select the row Press Delete (or right-click and choose Remove) Working with Grid Extents If your project has grids that intersect the wall, you can limit girts to specific grid-to-grid spans: Look at the "Left Extent" and "Right Extent" columns By default, both show "Full Length" (wall end to wall end) Click the dropdown to see available grid lines Select a grid to start or end the girt at that location Example: A wall runs from Grid A to Grid D, but you only want girts between Grid B and Grid C: Set Left Extent to "Grid B" Set Right Extent to "Grid C" Configuring Opening Framing For each opening, you control which framing members are created: Opening members (header, sill, and jambs) use Channel or HSS types only. Zee and L-Angle types are girt-only and are not offered for opening roles. Member When to Use Header Almost always - provides support above the opening Sill Usually for windows; often omitted for doors at grade Left/Right Jambs Usually both enabled; disable if opening is at wall end To customize an opening's framing: Find the opening in the Openings section Check/uncheck the boxes for Header, Sill, Left Jamb, Right Jamb The preview updates to show your changes Editing an Existing Girt System If you've already placed girts using SGT, you can edit them: Select any girt from the system in Revit The "Modify - Structural Framing" tab appears Click "Edit SGT Wall" (only visible when SGT members are selected) The SGT window opens with your existing configuration Make changes as needed Click "Update" to apply changes, or "Remove" to delete everything During edit/update: Opening rows show Live or Manual source. Editing a live opening's position or size makes it Manual. Its distance from the wall start stays fixed when the wall length changes. A completed session creates one Super Girt Tool Undo entry. Cancel, an error, or a Dev Mode reload rolls back the session's model edits. Update tries to move existing members in place first. If any required existing member cannot be matched or moved, Update stops with an error instead of retrying through delete/recreate. Place and Update set each girt's Start/End Extension from its end gaps (0 where the girt has no gap), so placed girts match the preview. A family default extension is replaced at the next Place or Update. An extension typed on a placed SGT girt is replaced at its next Update. If Update must change an extension whose parameter is missing or read-only, the Update fails and rolls back its model changes. Change Review When an edited wall or opening differs from the stored observation, SGT opens Change Review before it writes the proposed update. Each row shows its source opening name (or Manual opening when a detached manual row has no name), its source, status, and decision. Change effects appear in the details pane for the selected row. Along-wall ranges appear in placement validation messages when an opening is outside the effective wall bounds. Choose one of the decisions shown by the row: Accept adopts the current live observation and applies its framing on the next Update. Keep keeps the placed/manual geometry and framing configuration for this session. Ignore leaves the existing framing untouched and asks about the item again on a later review. An opening you edited in this session returns to its placed geometry and framing. A manual opening that was never placed stays unframed; choose Keep on a later review in the same session to frame it again. Update does not save an ignored manual opening that was never placed. The review also lists wall and layer changes, remembered decisions, accepted removals waiting for Update, and girt ends that will be re-anchored. A missing live opening can be paired with a current opening by choosing Same as and clicking Pair. Unpair restores the previous pairing and its draft row. Locate selects the source element when it is available. Relink starts a wall pick for a system whose wall reference has changed. The selected wall is analyzed and the review draft is rebuilt before any decision is saved. Delete System removes the stored system and its placed members. Deconstruct removes the stored system and SGT tags while keeping the placed members in the model. These operations run inside the same session transaction group, so Cancel, an error, or forced retirement rolls them back. Review Confirm saves the detached plan and decision ledger inside the current SGT session. It does not place or update Revit members by itself; use Update after confirming. Cancel closes the review without saving its decisions. The main window's Cancel — Close without placing anything rolls back all model and storage writes made during the window, including a review confirmation. A successful window close assimilates the session as one Super Girt Tool Undo entry. An unreadable current SGT payload fails with a typed storage error. If an owned storage entity or element tag uses an unsupported schema or format version, the session purges that entity and its SGT tags inside the same transaction group. It also purges current-schema tags that point to a system that no longer exists. A successful close keeps the purge; Cancel, an error, or forced retirement restores it. Native framing is not deleted. Re-place the system after an unsupported-data message. Preview/Placed Alignment Notes Recent parity fixes align preview and placement behavior for linked walls and opening framing: Preview visuals (text/lineweights/preview styling) are normalized to a fixed visual scale (matching the “good HiDPI” look). Interaction hit-testing (snap thresholds, hit radii) remains DPI-scaled. Section preview renders compound wall layers as labeled thickness bands, and strongly highlights the selected depth-plane layer. 3D preview renders compound wall layers as wireframe-like context geometry: very low wall fill opacity with selected-layer emphasis. 3D preview uses brighter crease outlines (cyan-gray wall edges, luminous steel edges) and a stronger 4-light rig so concavities stay readable in dark theme. 3D preview draws thin wireframe opening extents for all detected openings (subtle and non-distracting). The default 3D floor plane is more transparent and rendered as transparent geometry so members below/within it remain visible. 3D click-to-inspect now resolves on mouse-up (click-only, not pan-drags), and navigation cancels if capture is lost or the window deactivates. Opening extents in linked mode now map with frame-direction inversion detection so preview/placement use the same wall direction convention. 3D preview now uses the same depth-plane offset helper as placement. Opening-edge trimming now applies gap-only cutbacks in both preview segmentation and final placement, removing oversized girt-to-jamb gaps; geometry-aware bisection gaps use calibrated profile transforms so cutbacks align with placed output for nested families. Preview no longer reconstructs member transform/sign/depth semantics locally; Elevation, Section, and 3D all consume the same final resolved contract used by placement. Opening-member preview meshes now enumerate the same materialized segment-contract list used by placement, so segment order/index stay aligned across elevation, section, 3D, and placed components. Preview profile transforms now run with the same operation order as placement (rotation then Flip Facing then justification), improving jamb rotation/depth parity in linked-wall previews. Opening members now resolve orientation semantics in role-first order (role metadata first, then type fallback), improving left/right/head/sill consistency for shared types. 3D opening members now use the same final resolved contract path as 2D previews, so head/sill/jamb profile orientation stays consistent across preview modes. Elevation, Section, and 3D now all read the same final line, basis, and loop data, so preview modes stay synchronized without preview-only orientation helpers. 3D debug logging now includes projection mapping for left/right jamb, header, and sill previews to make WW/WS mismatch diagnosis faster. Horizontal members (girts/headers/sills) now keep their canonical warmup sign rules, while jamb preview and girt-to-jamb gap ordering use the selected per-rotation vertical calibration data for the current canonical rotation. Preview now corrects secondary-axis direction when transform and projection semantics differ, so WW/WS walls render girts/headers/sills with the same up/down facing as placed members. Opening-role elevation/3D preview now applies this semantics mapping deterministically (no centroid-based correction pass), so 0/180 or Flip changes update orientation without side-translation artifacts from heuristic post-correction. Dragging a bisected girt interior endpoint now keeps endpoint ownership on the dragged side (no opening-edge side remap), so opposite-end movement is avoided. Dragging a bisected girt interior endpoint to the opposite edge of the same opening now auto-joins into a single continuous girt by marking that opening as bypassed. Snapping a girt endpoint directly to an opening edge for that same opening clears the bypass marker so normal opening-edge segmentation behavior is restored. Analyze now supports rotated linked walls with role-aware probing: horizontal members stay on canonical quarter-turn probes, while jamb probing applies azimuth compensation internally; resulting row defaults remain canonical quarter-turn values. Linked opening T mapping now follows detected frame direction swap directly, without an extra mirrored-link parity branch, to prevent mirrored+rotated opening side inversion. Analyze now also handles mirrored-link orientation gating in Step 2 by applying reflection-aware flange seating side rules, preventing mirrored runs from failing all girt types during orientation detection. Square HSS families now run through symmetric orientation seating (all non-endcap section faces), preventing false orientation rejection during Analyze. Rectangular HSS role mapping is now explicit and calibration-backed: deep/shallow face sets are captured during calibration, then horizontal roles seat deep faces to the exterior plane while jamb roles seat deep faces to opening-edge planes. Step 2 now re-fetches square-HSS non-endcap faces inside each Y/Z probe pass (after justification regenerate), preventing stale-candidate reuse that can make all Y/Z pairs evaluate identically. Angle girts now use short-leg/long-leg semantics during orientation analysis (short leg seats assigned elevation, long leg seats exterior plane), and Z-girt validation enforces exterior flange down / interior flange up ordering. Analyze now uses explicit shape/role web seating mode resolution in Step 2: open-section horizontal members use edge-contact web seating, while HSS and jamb paths retain full face-coplanar seating. This restores girt orientation viability without loosening closed-section checks. Step 2 now logs per-pair [SGT.Orientation.YZ.PairProbe] diagnostics in Debug output, and face lookup deduplicates by face id before seating comparisons. Step 2 analyzer diagnostics now explicitly reject non-finite (NaN/Infinity) Y/Z candidates and report candidates, finiteCandidates, and rejectedNonFinite counts when no valid pair is found, improving fatal-step root-cause triage in logs. Opening-role Analyze gating now anchors Head/Sill/Jamb web seating planes to the same structural target origin as exterior seating, preventing layer-offset origin drift from causing false OpeningOrientationAllFailed fatals. Analyze temp probes now surface Revit blocking failures as explicit type warnings/failures (instead of silent probe success), so problematic families/types are clearly identified in preflight outcomes. Post-Analyze refresh now runs as a deterministic two-pass UI dispatch (Loaded then Background) only after successful Analyze hydration; failed/canceled runs skip that extra refresh burst. If preview still appears wrong after editing row settings, re-run Analyze to refresh wall/opening direction context before placing. Settings Explained Offset The offset controls how far from the wall's target layer the girts are placed: 0'-0" = Girt exterior flange is directly on the target layer face Positive values = Girts are offset outward from the wall Negative values = Girts are offset inward into the wall Use the same signed input grammar described under Adjusting Girt Elevations; the sign belongs at the start of the complete value (for example, -6 1/2"). Layer (Compound Walls) For walls with multiple layers (e.g., concrete + insulation + finish), the Layer dropdown lets you choose which layer surface the girts align to: The tool defaults to the most-exterior structural layer Change this if you need girts on a different layer face Rotation Rotation controls how the girt cross-section is oriented: 0 = Default orientation (web vertical, flanges horizontal) 90 = Rotated 90 degrees 180 = Flipped from default 270 = Rotated 270 degrees (same as -90) Most C-channels and I-beams use 0 or 180 rotation for horizontal girts. Y-Justification Controls lateral positioning of the member: Left = Member shifted toward wall start Center = Member centered on the placement line Right = Member shifted toward wall end Origin = Uses the family's origin point Z-Justification Controls vertical positioning of the member: Top = Top of member at the elevation Middle = Center of member at the elevation Bottom = Bottom of member at the elevation Origin = Uses the family's origin point Flip Facing Mirrors the member using Revit Facing flip semantics. Useful when the auto-detected orientation isn't what you need. Flip Facing is enabled only when the selected type supports Revit facing flips (detected during Analyze). Tips and Tricks Keyboard Shortcuts Tab - Grid: move to next cell. Preview: cycle overlapping handles near the cursor (Shift+Tab reverses); otherwise Tab behaves normally. Enter - Confirm an edit and move down Delete - Remove selected row Escape - Cancel current edit Efficient Workflows Start with defaults, then refine Let SGT auto-seed the girt rows first Then adjust individual rows as needed Use the preview constantly Switch to 3D view to check member orientations Elevation view shows the overall layout quickly Work from bottom to top Configure lower girts first They're less likely to change if you add/remove upper girts Batch similar changes If multiple rows need the same girt type, change them together Multi-select rows in the grid when possible Performance Tips For large walls with many openings, the analysis step may take a moment The progress overlay shows which step is running Don't close the window during analysis - let it complete Troubleshooting "No structural framing families found" Cause: Your project doesn't have any structural framing families loaded. Fix: Load at least one structural framing family (like C Shapes or W Shapes) before using SGT. Girts not appearing at expected location Possible causes: Wrong wall layer selected Offset value is pushing girts off the visible area Rotation/justification settings are incorrect Fix: Check the Layer dropdown - make sure you've selected the correct layer Verify the Offset is 0'-0" or a small value Try switching to 3D preview to see where members actually are Preview shows nothing Possible causes: No girt rows configured All opening checkboxes are unchecked Analysis failed Fix: Make sure at least one girt row exists with a valid type selected Check that at least one opening role (Header/Sill/Jamb) is enabled Close and reopen the tool to re-run analysis "Place" button is disabled Cause: There's nothing to place - either no girt rows or all rows have invalid settings. Fix: Add at least one girt row Make sure each row has a girt type selected Ensure elevations are valid numbers Girts placed but openings not framed Cause: Opening checkboxes were unchecked, or openings weren't detected. Fix: In Edit mode, check the Openings section Enable the checkboxes for Header, Sill, Left Jamb, Right Jamb as needed Click Update Members have wrong orientation Cause: Auto-detected rotation/justification doesn't match your intent. Fix: Try toggling the "Flip" checkbox for that row Change the Rotation value (try 0, 90, 180, 270) Adjust Y-Just and Z-Just if the member position is off Note (2026-03-06): Preview parity on WW/WS walls now comes from the same final resolved contract used by placement. If preview still looks wrong after editing row settings, rerun Analyze or reopen the tool so the current wall/opening runtime state is rebuilt before placing. Manual validation and the exhaustive Revit-hosted parity harness now agree again when Revit is loading the correct loader/dev-driver payload. Can't edit existing SGT system Cause: You may have selected non-SGT members, or members from a different system. Fix: Make sure you select a member that was placed by SGT If you have multiple SGT systems on different walls, select from the correct wall FAQ Q: Can I use SGT on any wall type? A: SGT works best on foundation walls and linked architectural walls. It's designed for walls where you need horizontal girts at regular intervals. Q: What structural framing families are supported? A: Any standard structural framing family should work, including: C Shapes (channels) MC Shapes (misc channels) HSS (hollow structural sections) Angles (girts only) Z-shapes and angles are supported for girts only (not for opening framing). Q: Can I have different girt types at different elevations? A: Yes! Each row is independent. You can use C10X15.3 at 0'-0", C8X11.5 at 5'-0", etc. Q: What happens if I change the wall after placing girts? A: The girts don't automatically update. You'll need to use Edit mode to adjust or remove and re-place. Q: Edit mode says the stored SGT data is incompatible. What do I do? A: The stored runtime payload no longer matches the current SGT data shape. Remove and re-place the SGT system so DB Tools can write a fresh compatible runtime payload. Q: Can I place girts on only part of a wall? A: Yes, use the Left Extent and Right Extent options to limit girts to a portion of the wall length. Q: Do girts automatically avoid openings? A: Yes. When you place girts, they automatically segment around openings with proper gaps. Q: What's the minimum girt length? A: Girt pieces must be at least 6" (0.5 ft) long. Shorter pieces (for example a narrow pier between two close openings) are left out of the preview and placement, and a girt with no piece of 6" or longer cannot be placed. Q: Can I use SGT on curved walls? A: SGT is designed for straight walls. Curved walls are not currently supported. Q: How do I delete all SGT members from a wall? A: Select any SGT member from that wall Click "Edit SGT Wall" Click "Remove" This deletes the entire girt system for that wall. Q: Why are some rotation/justification options grayed out? A: Some combinations don't produce valid placements (member would be off the wall or incorrectly oriented). SGT disables invalid options automatically.

user-guide/tools/sgt/section-preview.htm.title: SGT section preview | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/sgt/section-preview.htm.summary: SGT section preview The section preview in the Super Girt Tool shows a cross-section of the wall at the position of the section marker on the elevation preview. Section marker The section marker is the blue dashed vertical line on the elevation preview. Drag it to change the cut position. The marker snaps to 6-inch steps along the wall length. The filled triangles at its top and bottom point screen-left, the viewing direction. Dragging the marker changes the view only. Member end points keep snapping to valid targets: elements, grids and wall edges. Viewing direction The section looks from the exterior side of the wall toward the interior. Screen-left is the exterior face, and screen-right is the interior face. Horizontal members (girts, headers, sills) are drawn from their resolved section profiles. When the cut meets a jamb edge, the jamb is drawn as a vertical depth band over its placed height, which matches the Revit output. Compound wall layers For a compound wall, the section draws each layer as a band across the wall thickness. Each band is labeled Material - thickness. The layer selected as the depth plane is highlighted, so you can see which layer the placement targets. Far clip The section shows only elements whose extent along the wall meets the clip range at the cut. The range works like the far clip offset of a Revit section view. The range is 2'-0" long, from the section marker to 2'-0" on its screen-left side. The elevation preview shows the range as a translucent blue band, bounded on the left by a dashed line. No distance label is shown. Girts, headers, sills and jambs that lie fully outside the range are hidden in the section.

user-guide/tools/tdv.html.title: Transfer Drafting Views | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) copies drafting views between the open project and a library file. A library is a Revit project (.rvt) that holds standard drafting views. TDV imports views from a library into the open project and exports views from the open project into a library. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common. Command Effect Import From Library Copies drafting views from a library into the active project. Export To Library Copies drafting views from the active project into a library. Both commands are disabled while the Library Paths Invalid warning is active (see Library settings). Library settings TDV reads its libraries from DB Tools > Settings > Library Files. Control Effect Add Library File Adds a .rvt file as a library entry. Add Fallback Path Adds an alternate path to the selected entry. TDV uses the fallback only when the main path is not valid. Remove Selected Removes the selected entry or fallback path. Validate Libraries Checks every path. Alias Name shown in the library picker. When empty, the picker shows the file name up to the first _R. A path is valid when the file exists, has the .rvt extension, and was saved in the same Revit version as the running session. A file from another Revit version is rejected with Revit version mismatch (file: <year>, current: <year>). TDV refuses to open a library from another version, so it never upgrades a library file. A file whose saved Revit version cannot be read is invalid on its own: TDV reports Could not read the library file's Revit version metadata. Re-save the library in Revit to fix it. If a saved path is invalid, the warning Library Paths Invalid disables both commands. Correct the paths and save the settings to enable them again. Several libraries can be configured. When you run a command, you choose one library from the picker. The picker lists only valid paths. If some paths are invalid, TDV shows a banner with their number. If no library is configured, the command fails with No library files configured. Configure library paths in Settings. If every path is invalid, it fails with All configured library files are inaccessible (<n> path(s) failed validation). Check library paths in Settings. Usage Run Import From Library or Export To Library. Select a library in the picker. TDV opens it in the background; the project you started from stays active. In the Transfer Drafting Views window, check the views to transfer. Resolve name conflicts (see Conflicts). Click Transfer Selected. Read the result dialog. For an import, the source is the library and the destination is the project. For an export, the source is the project and the destination is the library. Window Control Effect View Type filter Shows only the source views of one drafting view type. All Views shows all. Search box Filters the list by view name. The x button clears it. Transfer checkbox Includes the row in the transfer. View Name Destination name. Click it to edit. The name is trimmed before use. Replace Replaces an existing destination view of the same name. View Type Destination drafting view type. The list holds the types of the destination document. The default, Retain Original, uses the source view's type. Clear Selection Unchecks all rows. Transfer Selected Starts the transfer. It is disabled when no row is checked or a checked row has a conflict. Preview Shows an image of the selected source view. Drag to pan, use the mouse wheel to zoom, and click Zoom Extents to fit it. The preview shows Preview unavailable for the selected view. when the view cannot be exported to an image. Preview updates When you change the selection quickly, TDV cancels the older preview request. A late result of an older request, success or failure, never replaces the preview of the current row. Errors An expander that lists errors. The status bar shows <views> | Selected: <n> | Replace: <n> | Adds: <n>, and during a transfer the count of finished views. A status icon in front of each name shows the row state: pending, success, failure, or conflict. Success icons appear only after Revit commits the whole transaction group, not when a single view finishes. Conflicts A checked row has a conflict, and a warning bar asks you to resolve it before continuing, when: the destination name is empty; the destination already has a drafting view with that name and Replace is off; or two checked rows have the same destination name. Rename the row, or turn on Replace, to resolve it. View types With Retain Original, TDV looks for a destination drafting view type with the source type's name. When it is missing, TDV creates it by duplicating an existing drafting view type of the destination. A row shows a warning mark when the source type name cannot be read; select a type explicitly in that case. With a named type, the type must exist in the destination. TDV does not create it. What is transferred For each checked view the transfer: finds or creates the destination view: a new drafting view, or, with Replace and an existing view of that name, the existing view with its type changed and its content deleted; copies the view scale and the View Description parameter; copies the view's elements with Revit's copy mechanism, one element at a time. Groups are copied as groups. Duplicate type names resolve to the types of the destination; copies the per-element graphic overrides. Not copied: viewports, title blocks, schedules, guide grids, other views, and view templates. The transfer copies the view's type but not a view template assignment. If a family used in the view is missing in the destination, Revit copies the family with the element. A detail array arrives as its groups, without the editable array association. The transfer is processed row by row inside one transaction group named Transfer Drafting Views, with one sub-transaction per view. A failed view is rolled back alone: nothing from that view is added, and a view you chose to replace keeps its old content. The other views still transfer. If Revit discards the whole group, TDV reports All attempted changes were rolled back, and no view is added. You can cancel a running transfer from the progress overlay. The views processed so far are rolled back with the group. Result The dialog title is Transfer Completed or, if any view failed, was not attempted or the run was cancelled or rolled back, Transfer Completed with Issues. Its text is: Selected <n>, Processed <n>, Added <n>, Replaced <n>, Failed <n>, Not Attempted <n> followed by (All attempted changes were rolled back) or (Cancelled by user) when that applies. A Per-View Issues table lists each failed view with the error code and reason. Copy Details copies the table to the clipboard. Error code Cause DestinationNameRequired The destination name is empty. DuplicateTargetName Two checked rows have the same destination name. DestinationNameConflict The destination view exists and Replace is off. SourceTypeNameUnavailable, DestinationTypeMissing The destination drafting view type cannot be found or created. CreateViewFailed, ClearDestinationViewFailed The destination view cannot be created, renamed or cleared. MetadataCopyFailed The scale or description cannot be set. CopyElementsFailed Revit cannot copy an element. OverridesFailed A graphic override cannot be copied. TransactionRolledBack Revit discarded the transaction group. Click Accept and Transfer More to keep the window open, or Close Tool to close it. Import TDV closes the library without saving after the dialog closes. If it cannot close the library, a banner asks you to close it manually. Press Ctrl+Z to undo an import; the transfer is one undo entry unless Revit discarded it. Export After the window closes with at least one view added or replaced: a workshared library is synchronized with central, relinquishing all borrowed elements, with the comment DB TOOLS - ADDED [<n>] DETAILS AND REPLACED [<n>] DETAILS.; a library that is not workshared is saved in place. If the library cannot be saved, synchronized or closed, the export fails and is not reported as successful. If the cleanup fails as well, the error report holds both failures. TDV then reactivates the project you started from. An export cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z once it is saved or synchronized. If nothing was added or replaced, the library is closed without saving. Library files and worksharing For a workshared library, TDV creates a temporary local copy named <library>_<user>.rvt under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\TDV\LibraryLocals\<id>\, opens it with all worksets, and deletes the copy after it closes. A library that is not workshared is opened directly. If two users export to the same library at the same time, one synchronization can fail. Coordinate export times. To create a library, create a Revit project in the same Revit version, add the drafting view types you need, save it where your team can reach it, and add it in the settings. Limitations The library has to be saved in the Revit version that is running. Only drafting views are listed. A view with an element that Revit cannot copy fails as a whole. The names of the views and types in the destination decide conflicts; there is no rename-on-conflict option. The project and the library must be different documents.

user-guide/tools/vtc.html.title: View Template Comparer | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/vtc.html.summary: View Template Comparer View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two view templates in the open project, side by side. For each differing setting you choose which template's value to keep. VTC then writes the result to one of the templates or to a new merged template. It can also save templates to a library and load them back. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > View Template Comparer. The Testing panel is shown when Enable Testing Tools is on in the settings (the default). If the project has no view templates, the command shows No view templates found in the document. Usage Select the Left and Right templates. The Swap button exchanges them. Click a value cell in the Settings Comparison tree to choose which side wins for that row. The Inspector has Use Left, Use Right and a clear button for the selected row. For a category row, use Edit Left or Edit Right (in the Inspector, from the row, or from the context menu Edit Override...) to stage a local graphic-override edit. A staged edit is marked Edited. Review the selected rows and eligible staged edits in the Preview tab. Click Process and choose the target. Comparison tree The tree has these top-level groups: Template Parameters, Model Categories, Annotation Categories, Analytical Model Categories, Imported Categories, Filters, Filter Overrides, Revit Links, Worksets and Design Options. Control Effect Search box Filters rows by name. Filter Limits the rows by configuration (see below). Select Left / Select Right Selects all differing rows shown by the current search and filter, taking the value from that side. Wipe Clears all selections and conflict state. Filters are kept. Reset Resets the search, the view filter and the conflict filter. Expand/collapse button Expands or collapses all groups. Show: All, Conflicts, Success After Process, shows all rows, only rows that failed to apply, or only rows that applied. Context menu Select from Left (with children), Select from Right (with children), Clear selection (with children), Edit Override..., and for Revit links Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... A category row or a Filter Overrides row is configured in a template when that template hides it or overrides any of its graphics. A Template Parameters row is configured when the template includes the parameter. The Filter modes are: Configured (default): rows configured in either template. Configured in Left and Configured in Right: rows configured in that template. Rows that are not category, filter-override or template-parameter rows are always shown. Select Left and Select Right select every differing row that the filter and search show. Under Configured in Left, Select Left can therefore select a row that both templates hide when only Right overrides its graphics. Processing that row to the right template keeps it hidden and clears those overrides. Process Process applies the selected rows and the eligible staged edits in one batch. A staged edit is eligible when its row has a selected side and that side is the edited side, or when its row is not in the current comparison. An edit on a visible row with no selected side, or with the other side selected, is not applied. The dialog asks Apply changes to: Option Effect Overwrite <Left name> Writes the selected values into the Left template. Overwrite <Right name> Writes the selected values into the Right template. Create Merged Template Creates a new template named in Template Name:. The name is required. A merged template starts as a copy of the Left template, so settings VTC does not compare, such as the view scale, keep the Left values. Use Swap to choose the other base. For a row that has a selected side, the target takes that side's value. When the selected side lacks the setting (it is absent there), the row in the target is reset to its default, instead of keeping the base value. This applies to categories, worksets and Revit link settings. Each setting is applied in its own sub-transaction. A setting that cannot be applied is reported as a conflict and the others are applied. Any other failure rolls back the whole batch. Overwriting a template is one undo entry. Create Merged Template is one undo entry named Create Merged View Template. If it fails, no template remains, so you can retry with the same name. Imported categories Imported categories (DWG, DXF and other imports) appear under their own Imported Categories group. They use the same compare, edit, preview and process flow as other categories. Revit links Revit link settings appear under Revit Links, grouped by link. Type-level and instance-level link targets are listed separately. VTC lists only the settings that the Revit API can both read and write in the running Revit version: Visibility Mode, Linked View, Filters, Nested Links, Object Styles, Color Fill, View Range, Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level, Discipline. Links are matched by the canonical link name, not by element id. If a name is ambiguous, VTC stops instead of guessing. Action Effect Open Revit Link Settings... Opens Native Revit Link Settings for one link target. The window always lists all supported settings of that target, even if you opened it from one row. Apply to Template writes the selected settings; it is one undo entry. Copy Revit Link Settings To... Copies the supported settings to other link targets. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are matched by name in the target linked model. If the name is unavailable because the linked document is unloaded, the raw id is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. The copy is one undo entry. A target that cannot accept the settings is reported and the others are copied. Any other failure leaves every target unchanged. Loading a saved template from the library also remaps Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter by name in the target linked model. If the saved name is not found there, the setting fails with a not-found error. If the snapshot holds no name (the linked document was unloaded), the stored id is reused. When only one template contains the link row, VTC uses that template. When both do and you have not selected a side, VTC asks which template to use. Library The Library tab saves template snapshots to disk and applies them back to a template. Save Template > Left Template, Right Template or Merged Template. An optional name field sets the saved name. When blank, the source template name is used. Load applies the selected saved template to the side chosen in Load to:. It first asks for confirmation, because it overwrites the template's settings in Revit. A delete button removes the selected saved template, and a refresh button reloads the list. Snapshots are stored under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\VTC\. VTC creates the folder on the first save. Saved names ignore case and surrounding spaces. Saving under an existing name asks Replace saved template 'X'?; Cancel saves nothing. If VTC cannot check the name, or another Revit session saves that name during your save, the save fails and nothing is overwritten. A snapshot that is incomplete or malformed fails to load with a storage error. VTC does not repair or migrate it. If a save or delete succeeds but the list cannot refresh, VTC shows a warning that names the template. A save or delete that fails shows an error. Limitations VTC compares templates in the open project. It does not compare templates across projects, except through the library. Link settings that the Revit API cannot read and write are not shown. Create Merged Template copies the Left template, so use Swap to base the merge on the other template.
